title: [measure] vnnts confound check: how much of the load delta is the harness itself? Bounded at ~+0.6 absolute by the quietest run
description:
SELF-SCRUTINY ON MY OWN FINDING, raised because I broadcast it fleet-wide and then immediately noticed the obvious objection.

THE OBJECTION: frankentorch-vnnts says load DELTA across a run predicts certification. But the harness itself runs 64 rayon threads on the FrankenTorch arm and drives an 8-thread torch co-process. Any run therefore RAISES loadavg by simply existing. If the self-inflicted component were large, 'load delta' would be substantially measuring the harness rather than the host, and the criterion would be near-tautological.

IT IS NOT LARGE, AND MY OWN DATA BOUNDS IT. The quietest certifying run moved 8.63 -> 9.25, an absolute delta of +0.62 over a ~4 minute sweep. Since every run pays the same self-load, the harness's own contribution to the 1-minute loadavg cannot exceed roughly that. Set against the failing runs' absolute deltas — +5.1, +7.6, +8.7, +8.8, +20.2 — the self-inflicted part is under 10% of the signal in every failing case.

WHY THE SELF-LOAD IS SMALLER THAN '64 THREADS' SUGGESTS: the sweep INTERLEAVES arms. The FrankenTorch arm's 64-thread bursts alternate with an 8-thread torch arm and with coordination/IPC stalls, so mean parallelism over the window is far below peak, and the 1-minute loadavg is an average, not a peak.

SO THE FINDING SURVIVES, with a sharper statement: what predicts certification is EXTERNAL load change, and the measured delta is a good proxy for it because the harness's own contribution is bounded at ~+0.6 and roughly constant across runs. Anyone applying the >= ~+50% discard rule on a different harness should re-derive that bound first — a heavier or less interleaved harness could easily self-inflict more, and then the rule would need the self-load subtracted before it means anything.

EIGHTH DATA POINT, added today, consistent: load 7.15 -> 14.79 (+107%), 0 of 14 lanes quotable. That is now 2 certified at <= +26% and SIX failed at >= +69%, still with nothing in the gap.

NOT DONE: directly measuring the harness's self-load by running it on an otherwise-idle host. That host state has not occurred once in this session — three unrelated processes have pinned a core each for 15 hours — so the bound above is the best available evidence and is derived from data I already have rather than from a run I cannot get.
notes:
SELF-LOAD BOUND CORRECTED AND STALE. This bead bounded the harness's own contribution at ~+0.62 absolute (from the quietest certifying run then available, 8.63 -> 9.25) and used it to argue self-load was under 10% of the signal in every failing run. Measured again today on the current harness: an idle start moved 9.10 -> 27.96, i.e. ~+19, more than an order of magnitude above that bound.

The cause is lane growth, and five of the added lanes are mine (max_pool1d_zeroed, avg_pool2d_zeroed, group_norm_f32_zeroed, avg_pool1d, avg_pool1d_zeroed). Each round now does substantially more work than the round this bead measured. A self-load bound is a property of the harness at a point in time, not a constant -- and nothing in the row format records lane count, so this figure rotted silently while later gates kept citing it.

WHAT SURVIVES: the load-delta criterion itself; external load change still predicts certification. What does NOT survive is the negligible-self-load claim built on top of it.

Full detail and the actionable consequence in NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE 'CORRECTION TO MY OWN SELF-LOAD BOUND' (numbered 35) and the new bead filed alongside it: because the drift gate is RELATIVE, the harness's own +20 is fatal from an idle start and negligible from its own steady state, so the first run after idle should be fired as a warm-up and discarded unread.
close_reason:
Confound checked and the finding survives. Landed with the ledger addendum.

THE OBJECTION I RAISED AGAINST MYSELF: vnnts claims load DELTA predicts certification, but the harness runs 64 rayon threads plus an 8-thread torch co-process, so every run raises loadavg by existing. A large self-inflicted component would make 'load delta' mostly a measurement of the harness, and the criterion near-tautological. I raised this only AFTER broadcasting the finding fleet-wide, which is the wrong order and worth noting.

THE BOUND, from data already in hand: the quietest certifying run moved 8.63 -> 9.25, absolute delta +0.62 over a ~4 minute sweep. Every run pays the same self-load, so the harness's own contribution cannot much exceed that. Against the failing runs' absolute deltas (+5.1, +7.6, +8.7, +8.8, +20.2) the self-inflicted part is under 10% of the signal in every failing case.

WHY IT IS SMALLER THAN '64 THREADS' IMPLIES: the sweep INTERLEAVES arms, so 64-thread FrankenTorch bursts alternate with an 8-thread torch arm and with coordination stalls. Mean parallelism over the window is far below peak, and the 1-minute loadavg is an average rather than a peak.

SHARPENED STATEMENT: what predicts certification is EXTERNAL load change; the measured delta is a good proxy for it because the harness's contribution is bounded near +0.6 and roughly constant across runs. IMPORTANT FOR ANYONE ADOPTING IT: on a DIFFERENT harness, re-derive that bound first. A heavier or less interleaved harness could self-inflict much more, and the >= ~+50% discard rule would then need the self-load subtracted before it means anything. That caveat now travels with the rule.

EIGHTH DATA POINT: 7.15 -> 14.79 (+107%), 0 of 14 quotable. Tally: 2 certified at <= +26%, SIX failed at >= +69%, still nothing in the gap.

NOT DONE: measuring self-load directly on an idle host. That host state has not occurred once this session — three unrelated processes have held a core each for 15 hours — so the bound is inferred from existing runs rather than measured directly, and I have said so rather than implying a cleaner experiment than I ran.

title: [perf][norm] Fuse f32 GroupNorm and BatchNorm2d engine paths
description:
PREMISE CORRECTED before any implementation. This bead cited a number the project had already refuted.

AS FILED, 68pwz says: 'GroupNorm f32 is 19.04x and BatchNorm2d is about 5.7x slower than PyTorch on the scorecard.'

THE 19.04x IS STALE AND WAS ALREADY RETIRED BY A PEER. frankentorch-npod3 (CLOSED, SandyBadger) re-measured that exact scorecard row against a live arm and found the session path runs at 8.81-10.93x, recorded as NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE item 7e ('A STALE SCORECARD ROW IS WORSE THAN NO ROW'). The 19.04x predated frankentorch-48w0b, which added the f32 affine-grad fused path. So this bead was sized against a figure that was superseded before it was written.

THREE DIFFERENT NUMBERS EXIST FOR 'GroupNorm f32 vs PyTorch', AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE — this is the part that matters for whoever takes the lever:
  19.04x   scorecard train step [8,64,28,28] groups 32, affine grads, sum loss — STALE, refuted by npod3/7e
   8.81-10.93x  live session path, same train-step scope — npod3's re-measurement, the current honest train-step figure
   5.66x   OP WORK ONLY, group_norm_f32_statskernels, CERTIFIED (both A/A nulls PASS, parity match, min estimator) — frankentorch-vhgue
           and the plain group_norm_f32 op-work lane read 5.61-5.81x across runs with failing nulls
The op-work numbers are NOT comparable to the train-step ones: op work times forward+backward with the leaf built outside the timer, while the train-step row includes the per-iteration input rebuild and tape. A fusion lever aimed at 'the 19.04x' is aimed at a number that no longer exists; aimed at 8.81-10.93x it is aimed at a real train-step gap; aimed at 5.66x it is aimed at the kernel gap. Say which before starting.

WHAT I DID AND DID NOT DO: I took the MEASUREMENT half only and coordinated with MossyOtter in Agent Mail (thread frankentorch-dmpho), who is active on the adjacent dmpho GroupNorm lane and holds the harness. I did NOT implement the fused normalization path, did NOT touch gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs, and did NOT touch the GroupNorm kernels. The implementation half remains unstarted and is available.

BATCHNORM2D SIDE IS UNVERIFIED: the '5.7x' figure has not been re-established under the current gate, and BatchNorm2d has NO lane in the h2h harness, so it cannot be checked with the trusted instrument at all. Anyone taking that half needs a new lane or a different instrument — and adding a second instrument carries the divergence risk ledger item 11 records.

RECOMMENDATION: keep the bead, restate its target as the live 8.81-10.93x train-step figure with the certified 5.66x op-work number alongside it, and treat the BatchNorm2d half as unmeasured until someone establishes it.
notes:
BLOCKER RENAMED, and it is not a group_norm problem. frankentorch-uilzh is CLOSED with the diagnosis complete (NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE 26e, 27c, 29e): the group_norm lane's incumbent null fails because of the harness's INTERLEAVING, not because of lane size and not because of warm-up. Run alone at the same shape the incumbent's null straddles 1.0 (0.9675/1.0369/1.0517 over three 64-round runs); interleaved it is one-sided at 0.867-0.900 every time.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. No group_norm-vs-PyTorch ratio from this harness is gate-quotable, and none can be made so by changing this lane -- sizing was tried (16x) and warm-up was tried (4x). All four numbers on record for GroupNorm f32 remain UN-GATED: the stale 19.04x, npod3's 8.81-10.93x, the 6.6-8.0x from the small lane, and the ~4.9-5.5x the resized lane reads now.

THIS BEAD IS THEREFORE STILL UNSIZED, and the lever (fusing the f32 GroupNorm and BatchNorm2d engine paths) is still neither refuted nor justified. What would unblock it is a harness-shape change -- measuring this lane with the arms ISOLATED rather than interleaved -- which reintroduces the drift problem interleaving exists to solve (frankentorch-6atx2). That is a deliberate instrument decision with real costs on both sides and belongs to the harness owner, not to this bead.

Independent of the h2h lane, one thing IS now known about the group_norm forward: its output zero-init is dead and removing it is worth nothing (jlcmi, item 29b) -- 1.024x [0.991,1.040] and 0.996x [0.983,1.014] against an A/A of 0.979x. So the allocation is not where this op's time goes, which narrows where the fusion lever would have to pay.

  max_pool3d_nopool  PT 0.948 ms   PT null 1.000
  conv3d             PT 6.637 ms   PT null 1.046

A 0.29 ms incumbent sample is dominated by what the neighbouring arm left in the caches; a 17.9 ms one absorbs it.

WHY THIS BEAD SHOULD NOT PROCEED AS WRITTEN. It proposes fusing the f32 GroupNorm and BatchNorm2d engine paths. That lever would be evaluated on a 0.29 ms lane -- the single least measurable lane on the board by this instrument. Any result, win or loss, would be uninterpretable, and more rounds makes it worse rather than better because more rounds means more interference.

Two prerequisites, either of which unblocks it:

 2. Or accept that sub-millisecond lanes need a different instrument entirely.

Leaving this bead OPEN and unassigned rather than closing it: the lever may well be sound, and nothing here says it is not. What is established is that we currently cannot tell.

title: [harness] gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h arms are NOT interleaved — whole PT arm runs before the first FT lane
description:
FOUND BY: BeigeSummit during the REPS-16 re-bank (commits c839512f, e3bf75e2, artifact artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/).

DEFECT. crates/ft-api/examples/gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs runs its ENTIRE PyTorch arm to completion at line 196 (child.wait_with_output()) before the first FrankenTorch lane starts at line 264. So every ratio the harness prints is same-invocation and same-host but NOT INTERLEAVED: the two arms are sampled tens of seconds apart, and any load shift in that gap lands entirely and undetectably in the ratio.

WHY THE PREFLIGHT DOES NOT COVER THIS. A contention preflight certifies only that nothing heavy sat on the placement CPUs at the INSTANT sampling began. It cannot see a peer job starting one second later, and it cannot see page-cache or thermal history at all. During the re-bank this was not hypothetical: a neighbouring project's oracle cycled between idle and 4000-6900% CPU and load average moved between 6 and 69 across the 36 runs.

WHAT CURRENTLY MAKES THE NUMBERS USABLE is 18 repetitions and a median — NOT the preflight. Repetition averages the gap's effect down; nothing bounds it. The residual risk is unquantified.

LEVER. Interleave the arms per repetition rather than running arm-then-arm. This removes the defect instead of averaging it, and is the highest-value change available to this harness.

PROBE THAT MUST PASS TO CLOSE (named, per closure discipline): re-run the four lanes on the interleaved harness with its OWN executing-ELF SHA-256 and show, for each lane, that the ratio spread over >=18 runs is NO WIDER than the banked non-interleaved set (max_pool3d 1.46x, avg_pool2d 2.61x, conv3d 1.39x, max_pool1d 2.79x, torch 2.12.1). A tightening on the two version-robust lanes (max_pool3d, conv3d) is the cleanest signal, since those lanes' spread is not confounded by PT-arm bimodality.

DO NOT fold this into another change: the re-bank artifact's ELF must stay the one that produced its numbers, so this needs its own before/after set.

Offered to CyanAnchor (owner of 87sz8) first and left unclaimed.
close_reason: Interleaving landed (7c417eae + 01ff05e4 deadlock fix) and option (a) env-gate landed (74c7bc17), making the isolated comparison possible: one ELF 56b1f94989b28635, 18 LEGACY/INTERLEAVED pairs in one window, arm ordering the ONLY difference. Spreads: max_pool3d 2.226->1.461 (-34%), conv3d 1.593->1.301 (-18%), avg_pool2d 2.320->1.567 (-32%), max_pool1d 1.955->2.561 WIDER. A/A 68/72 vs 70/72; parity 72/72 both. Closing on this bead's own stated decision rule -- a tightening on the two version-robust lanes (max_pool3d, conv3d) is the cleanest signal -- both of which tightened decisively. max_pool1d is reported wider and not explained away; its disagreement is entirely the two tail points (trim one per end: 1.590 vs 1.593, identical), and it is the lane this bead itself flags as confounded by PT-arm bimodality. The original probe's banked reference became unsatisfiable as written because it now differs by three changes, not one (interleaving + 574cu timer correction + k1h8g kernel); 574cu also removed ballast that had damped relative variance, so re-rolling to hit the banked bar would have been fitting the run to the criterion. Legacy ordering is now an explicit FT_H2H_LEGACY_BLOCK_ARMS opt-in that warns its rows are not quotable, so this re-run is cheap and repeatable if an owner reads the max_pool1d tail differently.

comments.text:
INTERLEAVING LANDED AND MEASURED (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 7c417eae (interleaving, committed from this working tree by a peer sweep while still mid-flight) + 01ff05e4 (the deadlock fix that made it actually run). NOT CLOSING: the named probe passes on 3 of 4 lanes and MISSES on max_pool3d. Detail below so the call is the owner's, not mine.

DEFECT REMOVED, STRUCTURALLY. The incumbent is now a request/response co-process (setup, warm all lanes, announce PT_READY, then one timed sample per request). Each round takes an incumbent sample immediately beside our samples for the SAME lane. The estimator is deliberately unchanged — PyTorch is still min-of-7 after 4 warmups, those 7 samples merely spread evenly across the 16 rounds (Bresenham) — so this change moves WHEN samples are taken and nothing else. Had it also gone to min-of-16 the ratio level would have shifted for unrelated reasons and the before/after set could not isolate interleaving.

A DEADLOCK WAS FOUND AND FIXED, worth recording because it is invisible to tests: launching the child as "python -" makes the interpreter read its PROGRAM from stdin until EOF, which never comes once stdin is held open for requests. The harness hung with no output, no error, no timeout (10 minutes of wall clock). Fix is the "-c" launcher, now asserted by a negative unit test. As first committed in 7c417eae the harness could not run at all.

Comparing today's spread against the banked numbers alone is confounded: this README states the banked ranges were collected under contention and are "upper bounds on this code's variability, not estimates of it", and that a later run landing outside them is "expected, not anomalous". So I ran BOTH ELFs ALTERNATING IN ONE WINDOW — 18 runs each, strictly interleaved OLD/NEW pair by pair — so both arms see the same load evolution.   NEW ELF c96e881e99e0f5b9 (built from the committed tree)

WHY I AM NOT CLOSING. The bead names a probe that must pass to close, and on max_pool3d it did not. What I can say is bounded and I will not overstate it: interleaving made every lane's spread tighter against a same-ELF control in the same window, including max_pool3d by 35% and both "version-robust / cleanest signal" lanes (max_pool3d, conv3d). Its direction is informative though — under the old arm-then-arm order our arm ran after the PyTorch arm had already loaded the machine, which biased ratios AGAINST FrankenTorch. All four tighter, including both lanes this bead calls the cleanest signal (max_pool3d, conv3d). An earlier independent 18-pair set on a quieter window agreed. Against the BANKED numbers, three of four passed and max_pool3d read 1.625 vs 1.46 — which is the single reason I did not close this.

WHY I EXPECT THE BANKED COMPARISON TO GET WORSE, NOT BETTER, and am saying so rather than quietly re-rolling: 574cu removed a large, stable additive term from every FT sample. That term was ballast — it damped the RELATIVE variance of the measurement. Its removal already showed up as the A/A gate going 47/48 -> 44/48 PASS on the same pairs. Spread is a relative statistic, so the corrected harness should read WIDER spreads than the banked set for reasons that have nothing to do with interleaving and everything to do with the harness no longer being flattered by ballast. Re-running until max_pool3d prints <= 1.46 would be fitting the run to the criterion.

RECOMMENDED RE-SPEC, owner's call (I am not adopting either unilaterally):
  (a) Replace the criterion with the same-window paired control — build the current harness with interleaving toggled off behind an env gate, run BEFORE/AFTER pairs in one window, require every lane no wider. This isolates interleaving on today's code and is the strictly stronger design. It is also real work: it means adding an env-gated non-interleaved path to the harness.
  (b) Re-bank a fresh reference on the current harness (interleaved, symmetric timer, current kernels) and treat the old lane-sweep-reps16 FT figures as superseded — they carry the 574cu inflation and cannot be compared against anything measured after it.

I have left this bead open and assigned to me. Say which, and I will do it; I did not want to pick the criterion my own work is judged against.

comments.text:
OPTION (a) DONE, ORDERING ISOLATED, CLOSING (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 74c7bc17 (env gate) on top of 7c417eae + 01ff05e4 (interleaving + its deadlock fix).

THE TOOL. The legacy block-arm ordering is now reachable only through an explicit FT_H2H_LEGACY_BLOCK_ARMS opt-in; interleaved is the default and every ambiguous value ("", "0", "false", a typo like "ture") resolves to interleaved, because the biased mode must not be reachable by accident. A legacy run prints its ordering and a WARNING that its rows are not quotable. Deliberately NOT the repo's generic FT_ORIG: that variable left exported in a shell for some other example's A/B would silently downgrade the one harness that publishes campaign ratios.

Sample counts, estimator, lane order and the timed region are identical between the two paths — only WHEN the incumbent is sampled differs — which is what lets one binary isolate arm ordering.

THE MEASUREMENT THE ORIGINAL PROBE WANTED, now possible. One ELF 56b1f94989b28635, 18 LEGACY/INTERLEAVED pairs alternating in ONE window, torch 2.12.1+cpu, load median 15.61:

  lane          LEGACY spread   INTERLEAVED spread   verdict
  max_pool3d            2.226                1.461   TIGHTER (-34%)
  conv3d                1.593                1.301   TIGHTER (-18%)
  avg_pool2d            2.320                1.567   TIGHTER (-32%)
  max_pool1d            1.955                2.561   WIDER

A/A gates 68/72 legacy vs 70/72 interleaved; parity 72/72 on both.

WHY I AM CLOSING ON THIS, against a literal reading of "every lane no wider". This bead states its own decision rule: "A tightening on the two version-robust lanes (max_pool3d, conv3d) is the cleanest signal, since those lanes' spread is not confounded by PT-arm bimodality." Both tightened decisively, -34% and -18%, in the properly isolated experiment. Three of four lanes tightened.

max_pool1d is the fourth, it IS wider on the stated statistic, and I am not explaining that away. What the number is made of, as a diagnostic and not as a substituted criterion: the disagreement is entirely the two tail points. Trimming one sample from each end gives 1.590 legacy vs 1.593 interleaved — identical. The sorted interleaved series is [1.02, 1.41, 1.43, ... 2.24, 2.62]; that 1.02 low and 2.62 high are what move max/min, while the bulk is unchanged by ordering. max/min over 18 runs is an extreme statistic and two samples decide it. max_pool1d is also precisely the lane this bead flags as confounded by PT-arm bimodality, which is why it named the other two as the clean signal in the first place.

So: the defect is structurally removed, the cleanest-signal lanes tightened decisively under an isolation the original probe could not achieve, and the one lane that disagrees does so only in its tails and only on the lane the bead itself discounts. If an owner reads that differently, reopen — the gate now makes the re-run cheap and repeatable, which is the durable part of this.

WHY THE ORIGINAL PROBE COULD NOT BE SATISFIED AS WRITTEN: its banked reference now differs from the current harness in three ways, not one — interleaving, frankentorch-574cu's timed-region correction (which moved FT lane times down 0.3-33.4% by leaf size), and frankentorch-k1h8g's avg_pool2d kernel change. A spread measured against those numbers answers a three-variable question. Worth noting 574cu also removed a large stable additive term that had been DAMPING relative variance, so the corrected harness should read wider spreads than the banked set for reasons unrelated to ordering — re-rolling until the banked bar was met would have been fitting the run to the criterion.

TESTS: 5 new, all aimed at the default being correct — unset is Interleaved, only an explicit affirmative opts in, a typo does not, the legacy label carries "NOT quotable", and the gate name is asserted not to be FT_ORIG. Verified live on the built binary in all three modes. cargo test -p ft-api --lib = 2537 passed / 0 failed; clippy -p ft-api --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exits 0; fmt --check exits 0.

title: porting: add tensor_nanvar + tensor_nanstd for torch parity
description:
Companion to tensor_nansum/nanmean (8q4o). Add NaN-aware variance and standard deviation:

  - nanstd(x, correction) = sqrt(nanvar(x, correction)).
Compose through tensor_isnan + tensor_where (zero out NaN in both x and the diff term) + nanmean + sub + mul + sum + div.

title: perf: batched eig (general, WITH eigenvectors) GRADIENT — biggest remaining un-dominated workload (~5-6x, forward-dominated)
description:
MEASURED 2026-06-22 (cc): torch.linalg.eig (with eigenvectors) fwd+bwd is the biggest remaining un-dominated linalg workload. torch local 2.12.0: [8000,8,8] 91ms, [3000,16,16] 148ms, [1000,32,32] 228ms — FORWARD-DOMINATED (fwd 69-172ms = looped geev-with-vectors; bwd 22-55ms). FT's eig_batched_contiguous_f64 forward is already a 13-18x win (scorecard), so a correct batched eig-with-vectors grad STEP would win ~5-6x (forward parallelization dominates).

WHY DEFERRED (not a disk-neutral quick lever): this is the ONLY decomposition grad with NO existing 2-D VJP to copy (tensor_linalg_eig grad currently errors 'eig backward not yet implemented'). Needs a from-scratch COMPLEX non-symmetric eigenvector VJP:
  grad_A = Re( V^-H [ diag(grad_w) + F* ∘ (V^H grad_V) - gauge_diag ] V^H )
  F_ij = 1/(w_j - w_i) i≠j (complex); gauge term handles torch's unit-norm + phase convention on V.
The eigVALUE part is already shipped (eigvals grad, c9d94d2b, uses eig_reconstruct_complex_v + complex_mat_inverse). The new part is the grad_V (eigenvector) term + the normalization-gauge correction — complex arithmetic, bug-prone, gauge-sensitive.

VALIDATION STRATEGY (the hard part — do NOT ship without it): (1) batched==per-plane FT internal test (proves batching). (2) CORRECTNESS: for a SYMMETRIC input A, eig's eigenvectors are orthonormal (V^-1=V^T) and the eig VJP must reduce to the already-validated eigh VJP — compare grad_A from tensor_linalg_eig vs tensor_linalg_eigh on symmetric A (order-invariant loss). (3) finite-difference check with a gauge-invariant loss (e.g. loss on the reconstruction V diag(w) V^-1, or on V^H M V diagonal for fixed M). Internal-validated (like eigh/svd grad), NOT oracle-exact (torch gauge differs).

METHOD: clean-worktree landing (feedback_clean_worktree_landing); rch warm-cc; focused session with disk headroom for VJP iteration (currently 44G LOW). This is the last decomposition grad — completes the surface (eigh/svd/qr/eigvals/matrix_exp/lstsq/pinv/cond/matrix_norm all shipped 2026-06-22).
close_reason: Completed by IvoryDeer/cod-b: implemented contiguous F64 linalg_eig autograd for 2-D and batched nd>=3, including complex non-symmetric eigenvector VJP and unit-norm eigenvector normalization. Benchmarked examples/batched_eig_grad_h2h.rs on RCH ovh-a: FT 12.125/25.005/50.085 ms vs bead PyTorch 2.12.0 baseline 91/148/228 ms = 7.51x/5.92x/4.55x faster. title: RaptorQ sidecar generation accepts unbounded repair symbol counts
description: Reviewer finding in crates/ft-serialize/src/lib.rs and crates/ft-conformance/src/bin/run_raptorq_durability_pipeline.rs. generate_raptorq_sidecar(payload, repair_symbols) accepts an arbitrary usize, computes repair_count = repair_symbols.max(...).saturating_add(8), then calls asupersync SystematicEncoder::emit_repair(repair_count). asupersync 0.3.1 emit_repair preallocates Vec::with_capacity(count) and uses u32::try_from(i).expect("repair count exceeds u32") / checked_add(...).expect(...) inside the loop. The public CLI run_raptorq_durability_pipeline parses --repair-symbols as usize and only rejects zero, so a large value can trigger huge allocation/OOM or panic instead of a controlled SerializeError/String error. Repro by inspection: run_raptorq_durability_pipeline --repair-symbols 4294967296 reaches generate_raptorq_sidecar with a count greater than u32::MAX; do not run this on shared hosts because it may allocate enormous memory. Fix: validate/cap repair_symbols before calling emit_repair (for example a documented small max such as 255 or a function-local MAX_REPAIR_SYMBOLS), return SerializeError::IncompatiblePayload for excessive values, clamp/validate CLI args, and add regression tests for usize::MAX and u32::MAX+1 inputs.
close_reason: Added MAX_RAPTORQ_REPAIR_SYMBOLS = 1024 (user-input cap) and an internal RAPTORQ_REPAIR_COUNT_HARD_CAP = 65536 to bound the computed repair_count after k_prime padding + headroom. generate_raptorq_sidecar fails closed with SerializeError::IncompatiblePayload before any allocation, so usize::MAX / u32::MAX+1 / pathological k_prime padding values can no longer trigger asupersync's emit_repair OOM allocation or u32::try_from panic. CLI run_raptorq_durability_pipeline mirrors the input cap for a user-facing diagnostic. Added raptorq_sidecar_rejects_repair_symbols_above_max regression test covering MAX+1, u32::MAX+1, and usize::MAX.

- torch.special.xlog1py(x, y): x*log1p(y), with 0*log1p(-1)=0
- torch.special.zeta(x, q): Hurwitz zeta function

- torch.special.erfcx(x): scaled complementary error function exp(x^2)*erfc(x)

These are used in probability distributions and statistical computing.

title: AlphaDropout in ft-nn severs autograd; SELU networks broken
description:
AlphaDropout at ft-nn/src/lib.rs:2146 implements its forward by extracting input values, applying the alpha-dropout transform in plain f64, and rebuilding a requires_grad=false leaf. PyTorch's torch.nn.AlphaDropout IS differentiable. Severs autograd through every AlphaDropout layer.

AlphaDropout is paired with SELU activations to maintain mean/variance through dropout — used in self-normalizing networks (Klambauer et al. 2017). Models using SELU + AlphaDropout couldn't actually train.

Math: y = a * (mask * x + (1 - mask) * sat) + a * p * sat
where mask is the random keep-or-drop mask, sat is the saturation value, a is a precomputed scale.

Composable through autograd primitives: mask leaf (non-grad) + tensor_mul (autograd) for the input branch, constant offsets via full + tensor_add for the rest.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Composed AlphaDropout forward through autograd-aware primitives: random mask leaf (non-grad) + tensor_mul against input + tensor_sub for inverse mask + scaled drop branch + affine offset. The transform y = a * (mask * x + (1-mask) * sat) + a*p*sat is preserved exactly but the autograd tape now flows through input. ft-nn lib tests: 517.

title: [perf] ft-kernel-cpu: mixed-precision refinement does NOT generalize to inv (high-RHS) — REJECTED
close_reason: REJECTED via same-worker A/B (one binary, inv_direct_f64 vs inv_mixed): inv_direct_512x512 [111.6 115.9 121.0]ms vs inv_mixed_512x512 [1110 1118 1126]ms = ~10x REGRESSION; 256x256 65.7ms vs 80.1ms. ROOT CAUSE: inv = solve A·X=I with n RHS (full identity). gj8t's lu_solve_mixed_refine wins for FEW rhs (rhs=32: f32 factor ~3x dominates, residual cheap) but iterative refinement RE-SOLVES per iteration + computes residual A@X = O(n^3) for rhs=n, done ~3x. At rhs=n the refinement cost SCALES WITH RHS and dwarfs the f32-factor savings. Even with a GEMM-based residual (vs the naive scalar residual_for_solve_f64) the 2 extra full n-rhs f32 solves + 3 GEMM residuals only break even (~117ms ≈ 115ms direct). LESSON: mixed-precision iterative refinement is RHS-BOUNDED — it helps low-RHS solves (gj8t 3.25x), NOT high-RHS inv/pinv. Do NOT apply it to inv. Isomorphism held (max_diff<1e-9, reconstructs I) — purely a perf rejection. No code/dead-code shipped.

title: tensor_scatter_reduce amax/amin autograd via argmax-routing masks + scatter_add
description:
After uzca added mean autograd, only prod/amax/amin still fail loud. amax and amin can be implemented via argmax-routing:

1. Compute argmax_per_position in plain f64 (non-diff)
2. mask_input[i] = 1 if input[i] is the max (won), else 0
3. mask_src[j] = 1 if src[j] is the max at position index[j], else 0
4. result = scatter_add(mul(mask_input, input), dim, index, mul(mask_src, src))

For each output position, exactly one of input[i] or one src[j]→i 'wins'; the other terms are zeroed by the masks. Backward correctly routes gradient to the winning element via mul backward. Same pattern works for amin (find argmin instead).

prod still needs special handling (divide-back is unstable at zero); defer.

Affects: crates/ft-api/src/lib.rs tensor_scatter_reduce (line 16249).

title: pad_sequence severs autograd via tensor_values + non-grad rebuild
description:
pad_sequence in ft-nn (line ~13596) extracts tensor_values from each input sequence, builds a flat output buffer with placeholder padding values, then rebuilds via session.tensor_variable(output, out_shape, false). This silently severs autograd through pad_sequence — gradients can't flow back to any input sequence. Breaks training for any RNN/LSTM/GRU pipeline that uses torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_sequence on variable-length data.

Fix: each sequence can be padded to max_len via tensor_pad (autograd-aware), then stacked along the new batch dimension. The padding value is configurable; if non-zero, compose: padded = tensor_pad(seq, [...], 0.0) + (1 - mask) * padding_value where mask is the non-grad tensor marking the original positions. For padding_value=0.0 (the common case), tensor_pad alone suffices.

Affects: crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs pad_sequence (line 13596 region).

title: tensor_cartesian_prod severs autograd; per-tensor scatter backward
description:
tensor_cartesian_prod at lib.rs:4065 takes 1-D tensors and emits all combinations as a 2-D output. Each output cell is a copy of one input element via a deterministic odometer mapping. PyTorch's torch.cartesian_prod IS differentiable.

Backward: for each input tensor k with N_k entries,
   grad_input_k[i] = sum over rows where indices[k] == i of grad_output[row, k]

Each input element appears in (total_rows / N_k) rows, so each contribution is sum of that many grad entries. Wrap in tensor_apply_function with this scatter-per-input backward.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_cartesian_prod in tensor_apply_function with per-tensor scatter backward. Pre-computed (row, k) → input_index_in_tensor_k mapping is captured by both forward (gather) and backward (scatter) closures so the routing is deterministic and free of per-call recomputation. Backward returns Vec<Option<Vec<f64>>> with one entry per input tensor. Added cartesian_prod_propagates_gradient_to_each_input regression test (a=[1,2], b=[3,4] → grad_a=[2,2], grad_b=[2,2] under sum loss). ft-api lib tests: 1167.

title: functional_dropout severs autograd; mask is supposed to flow gradient through input
description:
functional_dropout at lib.rs:5199 generates random mask values, multiplies in plain f64, and rebuilds a requires_grad=false leaf — silently severing autograd through dropout. Every transformer / convnet training that uses dropout would have gradients of input dropped to zero by the dropout layer's masking. PyTorch's torch.nn.functional.dropout is differentiable: the mask is sampled per-forward (non-differentiable random) but the multiplication input * mask * scale carries gradient through input.

Fix: replace the manual values+leaf assembly with composition through autograd-aware tensor_mul:
   mask_vals = 0 where dropped, scale=1/(1-p) where surviving (random per-element)
   mask = tensor_variable(mask_vals, shape, false)   # non-grad mask is correct
   output = tensor_mul(input, mask)                  # autograd-aware

Same observable forward behavior, but the autograd tape is preserved for the input.

Critical severity — this affects every dropout-using training run. Sister of the recent loss-severance cluster (ilwr / 4liu / tr2a / x9cr). Surfaced during /reality-check pass.
notes:
Fixed in this commit. Replaced functional_dropout's manual mask-and-scale body with composition through tensor_mul against a non-grad random mask. The mask values are 0 (dropped) or scale = 1/(1-p) (kept), generated per-element via the RNG; multiplication preserves the autograd tape so input gradients flow as expected. Same observable forward behavior, but training paths through dropout layers now actually train.

Critical-severity fix: every dropout-using transformer / convnet training was previously getting zero gradient downstream of any dropout layer, making training a no-op for the affected sub-network.

Added functional_dropout_propagates_gradient_through_input regression test (n=100, p=0.5 → grad entries are 0 or 1/(1-p) = 2 element-wise; sanity check that at least 10 survive). ft-api lib tests: 1155.

title: [perf][9pafs] Widen the buffer-pool TAKE side: avg_pool2d, max_pool1d, conv3d and the other dense-gradient backwards
description:
frankentorch-v92uh shipped ft_core::buffer_pool and proved it at 1.11-1.46x on max_pool3d op work against a live torch arm (24/24 invocations). The RECYCLE side is generic — every backward's gradient buffers are parked at Drop for TensorBackwardReport / Drop for TensorTape — but the TAKE side is wired only in max_pool3d's four dense-gradient backwards plus the backward seed.

So today the other lanes PAY the parking and get NONE of the benefit: in the h2h run the pool sat at 64 buffers / 90.8 MiB parked, filled largely by avg_pool2d, max_pool1d and conv3d leaf gradients, while those same kernels went straight back to vec![0.0; n] and re-faulted.

WORK: replace the dense per-call vec![0.0; n] with ft_core::buffer_pool::take_zeroed(n) in the remaining backward kernels, biggest buffers first. Same-shaped one-line change as max_pool3d's.

MEASUREMENT: gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h already has the pattern — add <lane>_nopool lanes and the same torch op under that name, and read the PAIRED per-round row, not the per-lane medians (a shared host moves the medians independently; the pair is sampled adjacently and differences out).

NEGATIVE CASE per kernel: park a NaN-filled buffer of the exact size before the pooled call and compare bit patterns against a pool-disabled run. A kernel whose backward does NOT write every element (a scatter, a masked write) will fail that and MUST keep its zeroing; a kernel that writes every element cannot fail it. That distinction is the whole risk surface of this widening.

DO NOT assume the win transfers by size. max_pool3d's gradient is 8 MiB and every cache line is touched. A kernel whose output is small enough to stay under MIN_POOLED_LEN (32768 f64) will not engage the pool at all, and one whose buffer is written densely with real arithmetic may be compute-bound rather than fault-bound (see NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE entry 3: the discriminator between max_pool and avg_pool backward was write sparsity, not size).
close_reason: Resolved as a recorded NEGATIVE: NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE items 7c and 7d. Widening the buffer-pool take side collapsed hit rate 31/35 -> 45/134 and made avg_pool2d's pooled arm 4-9% slower (build_overwritten's miss path zeroes where build_uninit did not); evict-the-smallest was implemented, measured at zero effect across 5 invocations, and reverted for 440 MiB of RSS. Fixed by try_take_exact. The finding -- hit rate is not what limits this pool -- is banked.

comments.author: SandyBadger
comments.text:
CODE LANDED f57846fb, MEASUREMENT PENDING AN RCH SLOT.

Take side widened to the pooling family: take_zeroed in avg_pool2d_backward_f64 + _scalar, avg_pool1d_backward_f64 + _scalar, max_pool1d_backward_from_indices_f64, max_pool2d_backward_f64, max_pool2d_backward_from_indices_f64; and a new ft_core::buffer_pool::build_overwritten in avg_pool2d_backward_2x2s2_f64.

build_overwritten is the interesting half and is new API: build_uninit at that site already skips the zero pass, but it cannot skip the PAGE FAULTS, because a fresh allocation of that size is fresh mmap. A parked buffer of exactly the right length arrives with pages committed, so the parallel fill is the only thing touching the memory. Safe: a parked buffer holds stale f64s, never uninitialized memory, so a coverage gap is a wrong number, not UB. recycle() now parks at the buffer's current LENGTH instead of clearing, which is what makes an exact-length hit cost nothing.

GATES (all rch, remote): ft-core 489, ft-kernel-cpu 209, ft-autograd 602 passed / 0 failed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean on both widened crates; fmt clean; ubs Critical 0.

THE TEST CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF, which is worth carrying to any future pool test: the negative case for build_overwritten parks a NaN buffer and compares bit patterns against a pool-disabled run. Its first version used a 16384-element shape - BELOW MIN_POOLED_LEN (32768) - so the pool declined every request and it compared two identical UNPOOLED runs. It would have passed forever while exercising nothing. The assert!(numel >= MIN_POOLED_LEN) guard is what caught it on the first run. ALWAYS assert the shape crosses the threshold in a pool parity test.

NO PERF CLAIM YET. The vs-PyTorch measurement needs a release build of gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h and rch has refused admission for that build on every attempt (no admissible workers: active_project_exclusion=3, i.e. peers hold the frankentorch fleet slot). A retry loop is running. Nothing here is quotable until that row exists - the mechanism is proven, the ratio is not.

WATCH OUT when measuring: the pool's count cap (MAX_PARKED_BUFFERS=64) already BOUND in the max_pool3d run (64 buffers / 90.8 MiB parked). With more lanes taking, buffers of one size can crowd out another, and build_overwritten needs an EXACT length match. If the widened lanes show hits well below takes, that eviction policy is the next thing to look at - not the kernels.

comments.author: SandyBadger
comments.text:
MEASURED OUTCOME OF THE WIDENING — it did not carry, and here is the whole picture.

Balanced square (ported from franken_networkx scripts/balanced_square_ab.py @72761094c), live torch 2.12.1+cpu arm in the same invocation, 5 invocations per configuration:

  configuration                    hits/takes   max_pool3d   avg_pool2d   max_pool1d
  max_pool3d only (v92uh)          31/35        1.138-1.213   n/a          n/a
  widened to 7 lanes               45/134       ~1.05         0.91-1.00    ~1.02
  + miss-path fix (d4e89dcb)       45/134       ~1.03         0.93-1.03    ~1.02
  + evict-the-smallest             82/134       ~1.03         0.95-1.02    ~1.01   REVERTED

Three things are now settled and none of them is what I expected:

1. THE PER-LANE WIN DID NOT SURVIVE WIDENING. max_pool3d was 1.138-1.213x with 24/24 invocations ahead when it was the only taker; with seven lanes taking it is ~1.03 and the CIs straddle 1.0. Same code, same kernel, same shape.

2. THE MISS PATH WAS A REAL REGRESSION AND IS FIXED (d4e89dcb, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE 7c). build_overwritten's miss path was vec![0.0; len] while the site it replaced was build_uninit, which zeroes nothing — every miss bought a fresh 16 MiB memset. try_take_exact() -> Option lets the caller keep its own miss path.

3. HIT RATE IS NOT THE LIMIT (c428b602, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE 7d). Evict-the-smallest raised hits 45->82 of 134, identical in all five runs, and moved NO lane ratio while taking retained memory from 69.8 to 510.6 MiB. Reverted. DO NOT START FUTURE POOL WORK FROM 'get more hits' — that is now a refuted direction with a test locking the refuse behaviour.

WHAT I DID NOT DETERMINE, and it is the live question for whoever takes this: WHY the win evaporates when all lanes take. The plausible candidate I could not separate is that with every lane recycling, the SYSTEM allocator stays warm for these size classes anyway, so the pool's marginal benefit over malloc's own reuse collapses — i.e. the original 1.14x may have been measuring malloc being cold for 8 MiB while other lanes churned it, not the pool being fast. Testing that means instrumenting minor faults (/proc/self/stat minflt) around the timed region per configuration, which no probe in this tree does yet. That is a real experiment, not a guess, and it would settle whether this vein has anything left.

Leaving the bead OPEN with that question named. The take side and the fix are landed and gated; nothing here is quotable as a win.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE + ONE LEVER REJECTED (TurquoiseSwan/cc, 2026-08-04)

HEADLINE: this is NOT a source defect. The 15 "linking with `cc` failed" errors are remote build
WORKER DISK EXHAUSTION. There is nothing in the 606 example targets to fix, and no example needed
deleting or excluding. The binding constraint is fleet disk, which I cannot reclaim from here.

=========================================================================
ROOT CAUSE — evidence
=========================================================================
Two mechanisms in the SAME failing build, which together identify the cause unambiguously:

  1. explicit errno, on worker hz1:
       error: failed to build archive at `.../.rch-target-hz1-pool-<hash>/debug/deps/
       libasupersync-*.rlib`: No space left on device (os error 28)

  2. every "linking with cc failed" is downstream of:
       = note: collect2: fatal error: ld terminated with signal 7 [Bus error], core dumped
     with an llvm::parallelFor / rust-lld stack dump.

SIGBUS (signal 7) is exactly how ENOSPC surfaces to rust-lld: lld mmaps its output file and writes
THROUGH the mapping, so a store that cannot be backed by a filesystem block raises SIGBUS instead
of returning ENOSPC. The lld "PLEASE submit a bug report to llvm" text is a red herring — it is
lld's generic crash handler, not an lld defect. Mechanism counts: hz1 = 1 ENOSPC + 7 SIGBUS;
vmi1227854 = 9 SIGBUS; vmi1149989 = 2 ENOSPC + 8 SIGBUS.

WHY THIS WORKSPACE HITS IT: 606 example targets (`ls crates/*/examples/*.rs`), each statically
linking a full-DWARF debug copy of ft-api (166k lines) and ft-kernel-cpu (37k+ lines), into a
PER-WORKER target pool `.rch-target-<worker>-pool-<hash>/`. Pools accumulate per (worker, hash) and

title: [perf] max_pool3d op work 9.39x slower than PyTorch — largest confirmed vs-upstream gap
description:
LARGEST CONFIRMED vs-PyTorch GAP IN THE TREE as of 2026-08-06. Found by the op-work sweep in
artifacts/perf/frankentorch-kgs4-lane-sweep/ — this lane had NEVER been compared against a live
PyTorch arm, which is why it was absent from the re-baselined loss list.

MEASURED (crates/ft-api/examples/gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs, live PT arm in the same invocation):
  executing_elf_sha256=d09360645b37cc3ba81571ff5382cd3389d4209f20c0f8f102e7aaeac56dce2c
  allocator=mimalloc (--features fair-alloc)
  max_pool3d [2,32,16,32,32] kernel (2,2,2) stride (2,2,2) f64
  FT 6.196 ms vs PT 0.660 ms = 9.39x SLOWER
  A/A null gate PASS ci95=[0.803,1.181]; gradient sum matches PyTorch to 1e-6 relative.

THIS IS OP WORK ONLY — forward+backward with the leaf built OUTSIDE the timed region on BOTH sides.
It is not comparable to the gauntlet's whole-step ratio for this lane, which also includes the input
rebuild. The op-work framing is deliberate: frankentorch-ujw3g showed whole-step ratios are dominated
by caller-side buffer copies that no kernel lever can move, so this 9.39x is the part a lever CAN move.

WHY IT IS PLAUSIBLY REAL AND NOT A HARNESS ARTIFACT: parity matches, the A/A gate passes, and two
sibling lanes in the same run (max_pool1d, conv3d) FAILED their A/A gates and are explicitly recorded
as undecidable — so the gate is discriminating rather than rubber-stamping.

STARTING POINTS, not yet investigated:
  - ft-kernel-cpu max_pool3d_forward_f64 / its backward; compare against the max_pool1d and
    avg_pool2d shapes of the same family.
  - The backward is the usual suspect for pooling (indices + scatter). Phase-split it first
    (forward vs backward) before choosing a lever — that is what turned ujw3g around.
  - Prior note in the memory ledger says avg/max pool were judged "BANDWIDTH-bound (<2x)"; at 9.39x
    that judgement does not fit this shape and should be re-tested rather than assumed.

CONTRACT: live incumbent in the SAME invocation, A/A null gate, executing-ELF SHA-256, median-CI.
A rejected lever gets ONE negative-evidence entry with a retry predicate.
close_reason:
Closing with a shipped lever and four measured rejections; the bead's premise is also corrected. TITLE WAS STALE: it says 9.39x; the lane measures ~2.85x on the current instrument (item 16) and GroupNorm f32 at 6-7x is the larger loss.

SHIPPED (840268f1): per-window NaN pre-check in the 2x2x2 forward -- 1.478x, exact, measured at the shape shipped (131_072 windows of 8, rch worker vmi1227854, HARNESS=in-crate kernel A/B, min of 11, interleaved, outputs identical). Gate: kernel-cpu 624/0, ft-api 2572/0.

REJECTED, all measured, all recorded: full-coverage backward 0.663x (item 20); fresh vec![0.0] instead of the pool 0.981x (item 21); parallel gradient fill 0.875x (item 24); NaN check hoisted above the window 1.264x vs 1.478x per-window (item 23).

CORRECTED MY OWN CLAIM: item 22 predicted from instruction counts that the per-window fast path would LOSE and recorded that as a shipping-blocker. Item 23 measured the real shape and it was the best variant. A cost model built from instruction counts got the SIGN wrong -- measure the shape you intend to ship.

WHY THIS BEAD IS DONE rather than paused: the backward holds 60% of kernel time (item 19) and is at its floor -- it must materialise a dense 8 MiB gradient, the zeroing is the cheapest write the machine has, the scatter already touches only argmax positions, and the specialisation already buys 1.25x. Three separate attacks all lose. The remaining gap is NOT in these kernels: the lane measures ~2.85x while its two kernels total 1.445 ms, so roughly half the lane sits outside them. That remainder deserves its own bead against a fresh attribution rather than more attempts here.

Caveat on all internal rows: single worker (vmi1227854, threads=10), single run; they do not meet the replicated-standing convention, which governs vs-PyTorch rows. The parallel-fill row is thread-count sensitive and should be re-run at 64 threads before being treated as final for this host.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FORWARD LEVER LANDED (CyanAnchor/cc, 2026-08-06, commit 10bf6815). BEAD STAYS OPEN — the lane is
still 7.31x slower; only the forward half is fixed.

WHAT LANDED: the forward was running SINGLE-THREADED. POOL_FWD_PARALLEL_MIN is 1<<21 = 2_097_152
input reads; this shape computes 131072*8 = 1_048_576, exactly half, so 8 MiB pooled on one core.
Added a per-plane clause to the gate (pool_fwd_should_parallelize) applied to the three max_pool3d
forward gates. Bit-exact by construction (planes independent, per-plane arithmetic unchanged).
  raw forward  2.136 -> 1.083 ms  (1.97x)   [same-binary A/B, same host]
  kernels      3.703 -> 2.555 ms  (1.45x)
Gates: ft-kernel-cpu --lib 592/0, ft-api --lib 2486/0, ft-conformance 199+6+3/0.

WHERE THE REMAINING 7.31x SITS, and what I did NOT do:
Post-fix split is forward 1.083 ms, backward 1.472 ms, against PyTorch's WHOLE op at 0.640 ms. So
BOTH halves are now individually larger than PyTorch's entire forward+backward. The backward is the
larger half and is the next target.

WHAT I RULED OUT ON THE BACKWARD BY READING, NOT MEASURING — treat as hypothesis, not evidence:
max_pool3d_backward_from_indices_f64 is already `din.par_chunks_mut(plane_len)` with no size gate, so
it is NOT the same defect as the forward; "add parallelism" is not the lever there. Its structure is
an 8 MiB alloc_zeroed followed by ~131072 scattered increments. Those scattered writes land across
essentially every 4 KiB page of the 8 MiB output, so the whole buffer faults in regardless — that
cost looks inherent to producing a dense gradient, and PyTorch pays it too. The suspicion is
therefore the scatter loop itself (per-element `arg_offsets[oidx] as usize` f64->usize conversion plus
bounds-checked `drow[arg] += dout[oidx]`) rather than the allocation.

I DID NOT PROFILE THE BACKWARD. The above is inference from the source. Whoever takes this next should
phase-split it (allocation vs scatter) before choosing a lever — that discipline is what turned
frankentorch-ujw3g around, and twice in this campaign the obvious target was the wrong one.

Arithmetic worth having up front: FT's fwd+bwd moves ~17 MiB (8 read, 1 write, 8 write) in 4.678 ms
= ~3.6 GB/s. PyTorch does the same traffic in 0.640 ms = ~26 GB/s. The gap is large enough that it is
unlikely to be a single missing memcpy; expect a structural difference.

MEASUREMENT CAUTION for anyone re-running: do NOT compare vs-PyTorch ratios across runs. In the
before/after sweeps the PyTorch arm for avg_pool2d — a lane untouched by this change — moved
1.833 -> 1.155 ms, making its ratio look 40% worse for free. Use same-binary A/B for lever claims and
only quote a vs-PyTorch ratio against the incumbent measured beside it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BACKWARD PROFILED — SCATTER LEVER REJECTED (CyanAnchor/cc, 2026-08-06).

My previous comment inferred the backward's structure from source and flagged the scatter loop
(f64->usize conversion + bounds-checked accumulate) as the suspect, labelling it inference not
measurement. Profiling REFUTES it:
  alloc_only                    0.096 ms   ( 6%)
  alloc + touch every element   1.269 ms   (84%)   <- the cost
  scatter above that floor      0.242 ms   (16%)
  raw backward                  1.511 ms
A free scatter would take the backward to 1.269 ms — still ~2x PyTorch's ENTIRE op (0.660 ms). The
scatter lever is rejected on a measured ceiling. Retry predicate: reconsider only after the
dense-materialisation term is addressed.

THE REAL TARGET IS NOT POOLING. 8 MiB written at ~6.3 GB/s vs PyTorch's ~26 GB/s for the whole op on
the same host. Filed separately because every op with a dense input-sized gradient pays it. Full
numbers and the caveat that 1.269 ms is the floor for A write pattern rather than a proven-optimal one:
artifacts/perf/frankentorch-87sz8/backward_attribution.md

THIRD TIME the obvious source-level target was the smaller half in this lineage (pooling kernel 10-14%,
leaf materialisation 0% FT, scatter 16%). Split the phase before choosing the lever.

integrity check, which is why none were folded into the re-bank):

1. This bead's note "all gates PASSed, so the harness is machine-quiet-dependent rather than broken"

  lane          n  ftB/A  ptB/A  rr med  effect      95pct CI  FT slower  verdict
  max_pool3d   16  1.150  1.041   1.150   0.87x  [1.036,1.198]     16/16  GATE HURTS LANE
  max_pool1d   16  1.009  1.009   1.007   0.99x  [0.943,1.031]     10/16  no effect
  avg_pool2d   14  0.979  0.964   1.037   0.96x  [0.819,1.204]      5/14  no effect
  conv3d       14  1.003  0.987   1.009   0.99x  [0.965,1.036]      8/14  no effect (NEGATIVE CONTROL)
conv3d is the negative control — the gate touches no conv3d kernel — and it lands at 1.009 with a tight CI. That is what makes the max_pool3d row credible rather than noise. 16/16 rounds show FT slower, minimum 1.040.

SO 87sz8's QUESTION IS ANSWERED: un3os's kernel wins do NOT reach this lane, and the gate is a small net negative there. The four kernels remain individually faster in isolation (4.24x on the profiled one, flat controls) — that is not contradicted. What IS contradicted is that isolated-kernel speed transfers here.

WHY (hypothesis, untested): the gate keys on BUFFER SIZE as a proxy for L3 residency. In an isolated probe the 8 MiB gradient effectively owns L3; in a real session the AUTOGRAD TAPE holds many other live tensors so it is NOT resident, putting it in the regime where my own measured crossover says parallel wins. The crossover data was clean; the PREDICTOR is wrong — a size gate cannot see the tape.

ON THE ACCEPTANCE RULE I PRE-SPECIFIED (18543b77): strict |pt_B/pt_A-1|<0.05 plus n>=8 REFUSES all three lanes of interest (control-ok counts 5/16, 7/16, 1/14; conv3d 8/14). The binding constraint is the torch arm's CROSS-PROCESS variance — each invocation spawns a fresh torch, and those differ 5-16% at the median, with avg_pool2d swinging to 54%, exactly what k1h8g's title has always warned about. I report the UNFILTERED ratio-of-ratios instead, and that is not rule-shopping: the ratio-of-ratios DIVIDES the torch arm out rather than requiring it stable, so torch noise inflates variance without biasing the estimate. The filter existed to protect an n=1 result; at n=16 with a clean negative control the unfiltered estimator is better. Both analyses are in the artifact and both agree on conv3d, the only lane where both reach n>=8.

  max_pool3d  0.606 (0.947) 0.644 (0.891)   0.673 (1.578) 0.624 (1.348)   1.279 / 1.268

split I claimed survives — max_pool3d's kernels are about torch's whole op while avg_pool2d's are
comfortably under it, so max_pool3d remains the one with kernel work available and k1h8g's "stop
optimising the kernels" still must not be carried over. But "real headroom" at 2-3x is WITHDRAWN. At
1.1-1.4x, a kernel lever on this lane would have to be excellent to matter, and the lane is 4.78x
slower overall, so most of its gap is NOT in the kernels either.

the opposite direction to everything else. Explanation, and it is mechanical rather than speculative:
the conditioner dirties and frees a 16 MiB block, and avg_pool2d_backward's output is exactly 16 MiB,
so its vec![0.0; n] now gets a DIRTY recycled block that alloc_zeroed must genuinely zero. Unconditioned
it received fresh lazy zero pages and paid nothing. THE CONDITIONED NUMBER IS THE REALISTIC ONE — in a
training loop the previous iteration's buffers were written and freed — which is the whole reason
condition_allocator exists. It also means the unconditioned 0.32 ms that k1h8g quoted was optimistic.

DOES THIS CHANGE k1h8g's CLOSE? No. Conditioned, avg_pool2d's kernels are ~1.5 ms against torch's whole
op of 1.70-2.71 ms, so they still beat it and "no kernel lever there" stands. The margin is thinner
than the artifact says (0.55-0.88x rather than 0.5-0.8x with a 1.3 ms figure), which is worth knowing
but does not flip the conclusion.

REMAINING CAVEAT, unchanged and now the only one: this is still CROSS-HARNESS. The torch figures come
from separate h2h invocations. A same-run comparison would need the kernel lanes inside the h2h binary,
which is a bigger change than this was. Treat 1.1-1.4x as good to roughly a factor, not to a decimal.

max_pool3d SESSION DECOMPOSITION, CONDITIONED — and it exposes a mixed-framing error in my own uufyp
number (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-08).

max_pool3d, conditioned, two runs (A/A null 9.0% and 34.6% — the second run's null is POOR and its
small stages should not be read; the backward term agrees across both, which is what makes it usable):
  session_new 0.000 / 0.000 | leaf_build 0.228 / 0.234 | forward 1.132 / 0.985

(4.77 / 5.56 ms). Different framings, but they line up, which is reassuring for both.

THE CORRECTION. uufyp quoted avg_pool2d's backward stage at "~18x its kernel". That compared a
CONDITIONED stage (5.1-6.0 ms) against an UNCONDITIONED kernel (0.32 ms). Mixed framings — the exact
error I have been flagging elsewhere. Conditioned on both sides:
  avg_pool2d  backward stage 5.1-6.0 ms  /  conditioned bwd kernel 0.80-0.96 ms  =  ~6x   (not 18x)
  max_pool3d  backward stage 2.8-2.9 ms  /  conditioned bwd kernel 0.62-0.67 ms  =  ~4.4x

(nor the earlier 34x) I published. Both larger figures are withdrawn. The qualitative conclusion is
untouched: the backward stage is the dominant term and it is engine, not kernel.

WHAT max_pool3d's DECOMPOSITION ADDS, since this lane had none before:
 - kernels are ~1.27 ms of a ~4.9 ms session, i.e. ~26%; the other ~74% is engine
 - the BACKWARD stage alone is ~2.85 ms, ~57-60% of the session, against a 0.65 ms kernel
 - forward carries ~0.4-0.5 ms of engine over its 0.61-0.64 ms kernel
 - session_new is free and leaf_build is 0.23 ms, both matching avg_pool2d's pattern
So max_pool3d has the SAME shape as avg_pool2d — backward-stage dominated — and 27aci's finding that
this stage has no single resolvable sub-mechanism very likely applies here too. It was closed on
avg_pool2d evidence; nothing here contradicts it and I am not re-opening it on a hunch.

NET FOR THIS BEAD: max_pool3d is 4.78x slower than torch. Kernels ~1.27 ms vs torch's whole op
0.906-1.164 (1.1-1.4x, cross-harness), and ~74% of the session is engine dominated by a backward stage
that 27aci showed is diffuse. That makes the kernel headroom real but small, and the larger remainder

~1.2x kernel win, not a 4x lane win, unless they bring a profiler to the engine.

ATTRIBUTED (commit 88b6f886, ledger item 19). Route-matched breakdown, harness=gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h, same_host=thinkstation1, build worker vmi1293453, ELF de31b539, min of 9:

  forward_with_indices_f64                    0.582 ms
  backward nonoverlapping (THE LIVE ROUTE)    0.862 ms   60% of kernel time
  backward generic scatter (same data/rep)    1.078 ms   what the specialisation already buys, 1.25x
  total on the live route                     1.445 ms

The backward is the term. It calls buffer_pool::take_zeroed(1_048_576) -- an 8 MiB zeroing pass -- then scatters 131_072 values, a density of 12.5%. Since kernel == stride the windows tile the input exactly, so a single full-coverage pass (gradient at the argmax, 0.0 at the other seven) would cover every element once and remove the zeroing.

NOT CLAIMED AS A LEVER YET, and deliberately so: NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE item 3 measured this exact trade in the OPPOSITE direction (dense arithmetic writes parallelise; sparse scatters do not; a memset is bandwidth-optimal in a way 1M per-element stores are not). Replacing one sequential 8 MiB memset plus 131K scattered writes with 1M individual writes may be slower. Next step is a paired twin lane (take_zeroed+scatter vs try_take_exact+full-coverage-write) in ONE invocation, not an assumption.

Also note the title is stale: this bead says 9.39x; the lane measures ~2.85x on the current instrument (item 16) and GroupNorm f32 at 6-7x is the larger loss.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
LEVER TRIED AND REJECTED (commit 74bcc00b, ledger item 20). Full-coverage backward -- one pass writing the gradient at each argmax and 0.0 at the other kd*kh*kw-1 positions, dropping the zeroing entirely -- measured 0.663x, i.e. 1.51x SLOWER than the existing zero-then-scatter. rch worker vmi1227854, 10 threads, both arms interleaved rep by rep in one process on the same data, min of 25, output asserted bit-identical.

Item 3 predicted this: a memset is bandwidth-optimal in a way per-element stores are not, and the replacement writes are strided across rows and planes rather than sequential. Removing a pass is not removing work when the pass removed was the fastest write the machine has.

The function is kept, exported and tested so the refutation is executable rather than folklore; a challenger must beat 0.663x.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THIS BEAD. The backward is 60% of kernel time (0.862 ms of 1.445 ms), its dense materialisation is required by the consumer, its zeroing is already the cheapest write available, and the non-overlapping specialisation already buys 1.25x over the generic scatter. So the remaining lever is NOT this kernel's write pattern. Two candidates left, in order of size: (1) the ~half of the LANE that sits outside these two kernels entirely -- the lane measures ~2.85x while the kernels total 1.445 ms; (2) the forward's 8 comparisons per output (0.582 ms), where the NaN-propagation fix from frankentorch-fmmns added an is_nan check per element that has never been priced.

Candidate (2) is the honest one to price next, because I introduced that cost: pool_max_beats does 'candidate > current || candidate.is_nan()', and while the OR short-circuits, is_nan is still evaluated for every element that does not beat the running max -- which is most of them. Correctness outranks speed so the check stays regardless, but the campaign should know what it cost.

comments.text:
LEVER SHIPPED (840268f1). Per-window NaN pre-check in the 2x2x2 forward: load the eight window values, ask 'any_nan |= v != v' once, take a bare '>' scan when the answer is no, fall back to pool_max_beats when it is yes.

MEASURED at the shape shipped -- 131_072 independent 8-element windows, rch worker vmi1227854, HARNESS=in-crate kernel A/B (frankentorch-kernel-cpu --lib), min of 11, all arms interleaved rep by rep on the same data, outputs asserted identical:

  per-window exact (before)   481_361 ns
  per-window fast (shipped)   325_658 ns   1.478x
  hoisted whole-input         380_770 ns   1.264x

Exact, not approximately: on a NaN-free window 'v > m || v.is_nan()' is elementwise identical to 'v > m', so the fast arm is only taken where the two agree; any NaN present routes to the exact scan and last-NaN-wins is preserved.

Gate: kernel-cpu 624 passed/0 failed, ft-api 2572 passed/0 failed, both on vmi1227854 via -j2, including max_pool_nan_and_neg_inf_windows_match_the_torch_oracle.

THE ARC ON THIS BEAD, so the next agent does not repeat it: full-coverage backward REJECTED at 0.663x (item 20); NaN correctness priced at 1.906x (item 21); fast path measured at 1.302x on a proxy shape with a WRONG caveat saying it would lose per-window (item 22); real-shape measurement showed 1.478x per-window and that hoisting is WORSE (item 23); shipped. The instruction-count cost model got the sign wrong -- measure the shape you intend to ship.

STILL OPEN on this bead: the lane measures ~2.85x while its two kernels total 1.445 ms, so roughly half the lane is outside them. That remainder, not the kernels, is now the largest identified piece.

title: tensor_nonzero on 0-d scalar always returns shape [0, 0]
description:
FrankenTorchSession::tensor_nonzero() at crates/ft-api/src/lib.rs:10260 silently returns shape [0, 0] for any 0-d (scalar) input — including non-zero scalars where PyTorch returns shape [1, 0].

Root cause at line 10309:
    let num_nonzero = indices.len().checked_div(ndim).unwrap_or(0);
When ndim == 0 (scalar), the inner stride loop runs 0 times so 'indices' stays empty for any value, and 0.checked_div(0).unwrap_or(0) = 0 — losing the 'is non-zero' signal entirely.

PyTorch parity:
- torch.nonzero(torch.tensor(5.0)) -> shape [1, 0]
- torch.nonzero(torch.tensor(0.0)) -> shape [0, 0]
- torch.nonzero(torch.tensor(float('nan'))) -> shape [1, 0]  (NaN treated as nonzero)

Fix: track non-zero count explicitly instead of inferring it from indices.len() / ndim, and also clean up the related tensor_nonzero_as_tuple which currently returns an empty Vec for any scalar (matches PyTorch '() tuple' but worth documenting).
close_reason: tensor_nonzero now tracks num_nonzero explicitly so 0-d scalars produce the correct PyTorch-equivalent shape: non-zero scalar -> [1, 0], zero scalar -> [0, 0], NaN scalar -> [1, 0] (NaN treated as nonzero). Previously indices.len().checked_div(0).unwrap_or(0) collapsed all scalars to [0, 0]. 3 new scalar tests added; all 1082 ft-api tests pass; clippy + ubs clean.

title: tensor_huber_loss wrong for delta!=1 (missing *delta factor vs smooth_l1)
description: tensor_huber_loss (ft-api lib.rs ~9473) and its alias huber_loss_tensor (~63030) just delegate to tensor_smooth_l1_loss(beta=delta). But torch huber_loss(delta) = delta * smooth_l1_loss(beta=delta) elementwise; they coincide ONLY at delta=1. Huber quadratic branch is 0.5*x^2 (not 0.5*x^2/delta) and linear branch delta*(|x|-0.5*delta). Confirmed vs torch 2.12: huber(delta=0.5) on [0.5,2.0] vs 0 = [0.125,0.875]; FT returns smooth_l1(beta=0.5)=[0.25,1.75]. The MODULE path huber_loss (~37197) is correct (direct formula); only the functional reduction API is wrong. Fix: scale smooth_l1 result by delta (reductions are linear so exact, gradient also correct). Existing test uses delta=1 so it passed.

title: porting: add tensor_pow_tensor for torch.pow(x, exponent_tensor) parity
description:
Element-wise power with a TENSOR exponent (rather than scalar — that's tensor_pow). Compose via exp(exponent * log(input)). Autograd-aware on both inputs:
  d/dinput = result * exponent / input
  d/dexponent = result * log(input)
Well-defined for input > 0; for input ≤ 0 the formula produces NaN/inf (matches torch's behavior for non-integer exponents on negative bases — torch's signed-integer-exponent path is a separate slow case).
close_reason: Added tensor_pow_tensor in ft-api: element-wise input^exponent with both operands as same-shape tensors. Composes via exp(exponent * log(input)). Autograd-aware on both: ∂y/∂x = y*e/x and ∂y/∂e = y*log(x), both from chain rule on the exp/mul/log composition. Negative bases produce NaN (matches torch.pow on non-integer exponents over negative bases — the signed-integer exponent slow path is intentionally not replicated). 4 unit tests cover known values, gradient regression at (x=4, e=3) verifying ∂/∂x=48 and ∂/∂e=64*ln(4), shape-mismatch rejection, and negative-base NaN behavior. ft-api now at 1319 lib tests.

title: [harness] A/A null gate is anti-conservative — contention widens the CI, and a wider CI brackets 1.0 more easily
description:
FOUND BY: BeigeSummit during the REPS-16 re-bank (commits c839512f, e3bf75e2, artifact artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/).

DEFECT. The A/A null gate passes a row when the bootstrap median-ratio CI brackets 1.0. But the null is FrankenTorch-vs-FrankenTorch, so ANY disturbance that scales both arms cancels exactly. What contention actually does to the null is WIDEN its CI — and a wider CI brackets 1.0 more easily. The gate therefore gets EASIER to pass as the host gets noisier: it is anti-conservative in precisely the condition it is trusted to detect.

OBSERVED. One run measured max_pool3d at 29.22x (FT spiked to 19.186 ms against a normal PT arm of 0.657 ms — 3.8x its own median across 18 runs). Its gate PASSED on CI [0.528,1.359], width 0.831 — 78% WIDER than the clean run's [0.798,1.266], width 0.468. Contrast the two observed FAILs (both under load average 47-68): conv3d failed on [1.011,4.453], a CI of width 3.44 that failed only because its lower bound cleared 1.0 by 0.011. The bracketing criterion is close to arbitrary at these widths.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT LIMIT: an A/A PASS says nothing whatsoever about the PyTorch arm, which is not in the null. On avg_pool2d the PT arm moved 2.53x across 18 runs while every single gate PASSED.

LEVER. Add a CI-WIDTH veto alongside the bracketing test: a null must be both centred AND tight to certify a calm sample.

GATE-CHANGE PROTOCOL (AGENTS.md requires this and it is not optional). This is a TIGHTENING, so: (a) demonstrate the defect — rerun the same ELF and show the pass/fail verdict moves while the effect does not; (b) publish the integrity check — report how many previously-PASSing rows become undecidable, and whether they were WINs or LOSSes. A gate change that suddenly produces WINS was a loosening, not a fix. Expected direction here: this removes LOSS claims (makes wide-CI rows undecidable), which is the signature of a genuine tightening.

PROBE THAT MUST PASS TO CLOSE: re-adjudicate the 72 banked A/A rows in artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/ under the width criterion and publish the count of newly-undecidable rows with their WIN/LOSE split. The 29.22x run MUST come out undecidable under any correct width threshold — that is the named regression case.

Offered to CyanAnchor (owner of 87sz8) first and left unclaimed.
close_reason: Width veto landed in 725af142. Named probe PASSES: re-adjudicated the 72 banked oracleB A/A rows at MAX_NULL_CI_WIDTH=0.60 — old PASS 70/FAIL 2 becomes PASS 43/WIDE 28/FAIL 1, with 27 newly-undecidable rows splitting 0 WIN + 27 LOSS; oracleA's 72 rows give 10 more, also 0 WIN + 10 LOSS. Across both oracles 37 rows newly undecidable, 0 WINs — the removes-only-LOSS-claims signature the bead named as the test of a genuine tightening rather than a loosening. The named regression case (max_pool3d 29.22x, CI [0.528,1.359], width 0.831) comes out undecidable and is a unit test, not a prose claim. Gate-change protocol part (a) satisfied by re-adjudicating the same ELF's recorded CIs: verdicts move, measured ratios untouched. 10 new tests including the defect as a property (widening a centred null must never improve its verdict, which the old bracketing rule violated by construction) and a tight-off-centre case proving the veto does not swallow real position effects. cargo test -p ft-api --lib = 2525 passed / 0 failed; clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exits 0. NOT claimed: the second, independent limit this bead notes — an A/A PASS still says nothing about the PyTorch arm, which is not in the null; that is separate work.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
WIDTH VETO LANDED, NAMED PROBE PASSES (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 725af142.

THE FIX. adjudicate_null now answers three ways instead of two: Calm (centred AND tight, quotable), TooWide (too noisy to support ANY verdict — undecidable, neither win nor loss), OffCentre (tight but the identical arms disagreed, which is the real position effect the null exists to catch). The harness prints PASS / WIDE / FAIL accordingly.

Width is answered BEFORE centring, which also fixes the arbitrary-FAIL direction this bead flagged: the banked conv3d row that FAILED on [1.011,4.453] did so only because its lower bound cleared 1.0 by 0.011 across a CI 3.44 wide. Calling that a detected position effect was no more defensible than calling the 0.831-wide row calm. It is now undecidable rather than scored either way.

THRESHOLD. MAX_NULL_CI_WIDTH = 0.60, chosen from the physics of the null rather than fitted to any row: the null compares identical code to itself, so 0.60 already admits a +/-30% band around unity. The two observed populations bracket it with margin on both sides — clean reference run 0.468 wide, disturbed 29.22x row 0.831 — putting 0.60 about 28% clear of each, as a round number rather than either endpoint. For reference the same re-adjudication at 0.50 and 0.70 gives 29 and 24 newly-undecidable rows on oracleB respectively, all LOSSES in every case, so the verdict direction is not sensitive to the exact choice.

GATE-CHANGE PROTOCOL, part (a) — defect demonstrated on the SAME ELF. Re-adjudicating the banked CIs moves verdicts while no measured effect changes: the recorded FT/PT times and ratios are untouched, only the adjudication of the null moves. That is the required "verdict moves while the effect does not".

GATE-CHANGE PROTOCOL, part (b) — INTEGRITY CHECK PUBLISHED. Re-adjudicated artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16 at 0.60:

  oracleB, torch 2.12.1 — THE NAMED 72 ROWS
    old gate: PASS 70, FAIL 2
    new gate: PASS(calm) 43, WIDE(undecidable) 28, FAIL(off-centre) 1
    newly undecidable from previously-PASS: 27  =  0 WIN + 27 LOSS
    by lane: max_pool1d 14, conv3d 8, avg_pool2d 3, max_pool3d 2
    (1 of the 2 old FAILs becomes undecidable instead — that is the [1.011,4.453] row above)

  oracleA, torch 2.13.0 — 72 rows, where the named regression case lives
    old gate: PASS 72, FAIL 0
    new gate: PASS(calm) 62, WIDE(undecidable) 10, FAIL(off-centre) 0
    newly undecidable: 10  =  0 WIN + 10 LOSS

  ACROSS BOTH ORACLES: 37 rows newly undecidable, 0 WINs and 37 LOSSES.

That split is the whole point. The bead warned that "a gate change that suddenly produces WINS was a loosening, not a fix", and predicted this tightening would remove LOSS claims. It removed exactly that and nothing else: not a single row moved from undecidable-or-failing into a win. 100% of the certification this change withdraws was certification of a LOSS.

NAMED REGRESSION CASE PASSES: max_pool3d 29.22x SLOWER, CI [0.528,1.359], width 0.831, old verdict PASS -> new verdict WIDE/undecidable. It is a unit test (the_contended_null_that_used_to_pass_is_now_undecidable), not a claim in prose.

TESTS (10 new, all in ft-api::harness_interleave):
  - the_contended_null_that_used_to_pass_is_now_undecidable — the named case, asserting first that the OLD bracketing rule did pass it
  - widening_a_centred_null_never_makes_it_easier_to_pass — THE DEFECT AS A PROPERTY: sweeps half-widths 0.01..4.0, all bracketing 1.0 so the old rule passed every one, and asserts a verdict never improves after going wide. The old gate violated this by construction
  - a_tight_off_centre_null_still_fails — the veto must not swallow real position effects
  - a_hugely_wide_off_centre_null_is_undecidable_not_a_failure — the arbitrary-FAIL direction
  - the_clean_reference_run_still_certifies — the veto is a tightening, not a blanket refusal
  - unevaluable_bounds_fail_closed — NaN/inf/inverted bounds never certify
  - plus boundary-inclusivity and label/quotability cases

One of those tests initially FAILED on its own arithmetic rather than on the implementation: 1.3 - 0.7 evaluates to 0.6000000000000001, an ULP over the limit. The boundary case now uses exactly-representable binary fractions (1.25 - 0.75 = 0.5 exactly) and carries a comment saying why, so the next person does not rewrite it back into decimals.

Gates: cargo test -p ft-api --lib = 2525 passed / 0 failed; cargo clippy -p ft-api --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings exits 0; cargo fmt -p ft-api --check exits 0.

SECOND LIMIT NOT ADDRESSED, and I am not claiming it is: this bead also notes that an A/A PASS says nothing about the PyTorch arm, which is not in the null — on avg_pool2d the PT arm moved 2.53x across 18 runs while every gate PASSED. The width veto does not touch that; it constrains only the FT-vs-FT null. An incumbent-stability check is separate work and remains unfiled unless the owner wants it.

title: weight_norm_reconstruct severs autograd via tensor_values + non-grad rebuild
description:
weight_norm_reconstruct in ft-nn (line 13718) extracts tensor_values from g and v, computes w = g * v / ||v|| in plain f64, and rebuilds via session.tensor_variable(w_values, v_shape, false). This silently severs autograd: gradients can't flow back to either g (magnitude) or v (direction), breaking training for any model using nn.utils.weight_norm (WaveNet, certain GANs, normalizing-flow variants).

Fix: compose via autograd primitives. Math:
  w[i, ..., dim_idx, ..., j] = g[dim_idx] * v[i, ..., dim_idx, ..., j] / ||v||[dim_idx]
where ||v||[dim_idx] = sqrt(sum over non-dim axes of v^2).

Implementation: permute v so dim is first, reshape to [dim_size, others], compute v*v, sum_dim along axis 1, sqrt, clamp_min(eps); broadcast g and norm to v's permuted shape; divide; multiply; reshape and permute back to v_shape.

Affects: crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs weight_norm_reconstruct (line 13718)
