  sha256 hooks/pre-commit == sha256 .git/hooks/pre-commit.orig   13a8c372ce8ea140...
  sh hooks/pre-commit --self-test -> all checks passed
Installed still equals tracked; the gate that was made to actually scan is still the one running.

wider than what I fixed.

This bead has said from the start that "the exposure is agent shell behaviour, which is why this is
a bead and not a code fix". That is true of the PIPE forms. It is not true of the whole class. Here
is an instance of this bead's headline failure -- a gate green no matter what the tool found --
that lives in Rust, not in a shell, and is therefore fixable.

THE DEFECT. Every oracle-backed conformance test guards on torch_available() and returns early when
the probe fails. That early return is a NORMAL RETURN, so cargo prints

    test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

A PASS. Not a skip, not an ignore. Correct on a torch-less machine; a false green on a machine that
HAS torch and simply was not asked. I hit it live: I ran frankentorch-1jzt6's new signed-zero test
under `rch exec`, which runs on a worker where the local oracle venv does not exist (that is
frankentorch-fl87u's fifth mode, filed today). It reported 1 passed having never spoken to torch. Had
I trusted it I would have shipped dtyiz's parity guard as a test that never ran -- the exact mistake
1jzt6 exists to prevent, reached from the opposite direction.

THE FIX turns on whether the caller NAMED an interpreter. FT_LEGACY_ORACLE_PYTHON is only ever set
deliberately, so setting it is a statement that an oracle run is expected:
  set + unanswered   -> PANIC. A measurement was asked for and did not happen.
  unset + unanswered -> honest skip, unchanged. The torch-less machine keeps working.
  answered           -> run the comparison.
classify_oracle_skip() is pure and total so the decision is testable without mutating process
environment; only a thin wrapper reads env. That is the same shape as this repo's pre-commit
self-test: exercise the helper the caller actually uses, never a reimplementation.

VERIFIED BY BEHAVIOUR, all three conditions on a real test, because a fix for a false-green must be
shown to actually go red:
  A  FT_LEGACY_ORACLE_PYTHON=/nonexistent/python  -> FAILED, rc 101, "Refusing to pass silently"
                                                     (before the change: ok, 1 passed)
  B  unset                                        -> ok, 1 passed, "skipping"
  C  =.venv-oracle/bin/python                     -> ok, 1 passed, "oracle torch 2.12.0+cpu"
Case A is the one that matters and it is the case that used to lie.

FOUR UNIT TESTS on the pure decision. One of them is not a table row: it asserts that
requested-but-absent and available-but-unrequested do NOT collapse to the same verdict, because if
those two booleans were ever swapped at a call site the torch-less machine would start FAILING while
the false green started PASSING -- the precise inversion of the intent, and invisible to a test that
only checks each row in isolation.

SCOPE DELIBERATELY NARROW, and I want the reason on the record rather than discovered later. Only
1jzt6's test is wired up. pytorch_ldexp_conformance, pytorch_avg_pool2d_conformance and the in-crate
oracle tests still use the old always-skip form. Three other agents are committing into this shared
checkout right now, and converting their tests into ones that can newly FAIL is a change that should
be made per-test on purpose, not swept in underneath them. Same reasoning RainyReef used for not
flipping UBS_REQUIRE_SCAN to fail-closed. The helper is public and documented; adoption is one line.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, so nobody reads it as broader than it is: the pipe forms in this bead's
description are still pure agent shell behaviour with no code surface, and my own two slips today
(citing an unauditable clippy rc across a context clear; zsh not word-splitting a $T holding a cargo
command, which produced rc=127 and briefly looked like a test failure) were both shell, both caught
by reading output rather than exit codes. Knowing about the hazard still does not prevent it. What
changed today is only that one member of the class stopped being a shell problem and became a
testable function.

new); fmt clean; clippy --lib --tests --no-deps -D warnings rc=0.

THE PAYOFF, and the strongest evidence yet for this bead's thesis. Pointing the oracle at .venv-oracle (torch 2.12.0+cpu) runs these tests for the first time. TWO FAIL:

  frankentorch-r2ayl — torch_ieee754_unary_edge_cases_subprocess_conformance has NEVER been able to run. Its oracle subprocess crashes every time: the payload is built from raw f64 via json!(vec![*m,*s]), serde_json cannot represent infinity, f64::INFINITY becomes JSON null, Python gets None, torch.tensor(None) raises. The test DEFINES a correct encode_scalar with inf/nan/-0.0 tags and uses it only for DECODING the response — the outbound path never calls it. A test whose entire subject is IEEE edge cases (copysign with signed zeros/infinities, heaviside with NaN, pow with negative bases) has guarded nothing, in a seam the ledger records as historically productive (pqwbs, bh6bh, ft3fp were all real bugs there).

  frankentorch-9rvxq — quantized_linear dequant diverges from torch by ~1.16e-6 against a 1e-6 tolerance. torch's 75.7999988436699 is f32-rounded 75.8; FT's 75.80000000000001 is f64-accurate. Likely FT computing in f64 where torch's quantized path rounds through f32 — i.e. FT is MORE precise and diverges for that reason. Filed rather than fixed because bit-match-torch vs tolerance-domain is a policy call, and widening the tolerance to green would permanently hide a real divergence.

NEITHER IS A REGRESSION FROM MY COMMIT, and the reasoning belongs on the record rather than being implied: the rewrite replaces only the body of the !torch_available branch. When torch IS available the old code skipped that body and continued; the new code evaluates the helper to OracleUsable, !true is false, skips the body, continues. Identical. Both tests were already failing for anyone who configured an oracle — nobody does by default, so they skipped silently instead.

That is this bead's headline claim demonstrated end to end: two gates that reported success while executing nothing, one of which never executed ONCE in its entire existence.

title: ft-api: index_reduce include_self=False blanks untouched positions to reduction identity (torch parity)
description:
tensor_index_reduce initialised ALL output positions to the reduction identity (1.0 for prod, -inf for mean/amax, +inf for amin) when include_self=False, so positions that receive NO source element came out as the identity (e.g. -inf for amax) instead of keeping their input value.

torch (2.12) include_self=False excludes the SELF term only at positions that are reduced into; untouched positions keep the base input value. Verified base=[10,20,30,40], index=[0,0], src=[1,5]: amax False=[5,20,30,40], amin False=[1,20,30,40], prod False=[5,20,30,40], mean False=[3,20,30,40]. FT previously produced [.,-inf,-inf,-inf] etc.

Fix: init result=input.clone() in both modes; first source element at a position under include_self=False REPLACES the base (self excluded), later elements reduce normally. Validate reduce mode up front. include_self=True path byte-identical. Golden test test_index_reduce_include_self_false_keeps_untouched.
close_reason: Fixed: tensor_index_reduce now inits result=input.clone() in both include_self modes; first src element under include_self=False replaces the base (self excluded), later elements reduce normally; reduce-mode validated up front. include_self=True path byte-identical. Golden test test_index_reduce_include_self_false_keeps_untouched (8 mode/flag cases vs torch 2.12). ft-api suite 1938/1938.

title: Add CI pipeline with G1-G5 quality gates from spec
description:
COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENTORCH_V1.md §18 defines 5 CI gates that are release-blocking. NONE of them exist:

| Gate | Name | Blocking | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | format + lint | yes | lint report |
| G2 | unit + integration | yes | junit report |
| G3 | differential + gradient checks | yes | parity report + grad report |
| G4 | adversarial + property tests | yes | counterexample corpus |
| G5 | benchmark regression | yes | baseline delta report |

Implementation:
1. Create .github/workflows/ci.yml with 5 jobs mapping to G1-G5
2. G1: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings
3. G2: cargo test --workspace --all-features (with junit output via cargo-nextest or similar)
4. G3: cargo test -p ft-conformance (differential fixtures), cargo test -p ft-autograd (gradient checks)
5. G4: cargo test --workspace --all-features (proptest runs as part of normal test suite)
6. G5: cargo run -p ft-conformance --bin run_perf_slos (depends on frankentorch-vws being done first)

Considerations:
- GitHub Actions runners may be slow for full test suite; consider splitting into parallel jobs
- G5 (benchmark regression) needs baseline artifacts committed to repo for comparison
- Need to use nightly toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml already specifies this)

Tests:
- The CI pipeline IS the test — verify it by pushing a PR and checking all 5 gates pass
- Ensure the pipeline also runs on the 'main' branch (not just PRs)
- Add a badge to README.md showing CI status
close_reason: Already implemented: .github/workflows/phase2c_reliability_gates.yml has G1 (fmt/clippy) + G2 (unit/property) + G3 (differential) + G4 (e2e/forensics) + G5 (perf) + G6 (schema) + G7 (RaptorQ) + G8 (readiness). Exceeds spec's G1-G5 requirement. Uses rch offload when available, falls back to local. Has structured failure reporting with gate_id, replay commands, artifact refs, and reason codes.

title: porting: add tensor_broadcast_tensors and tensor_argwhere for torch parity
description:

title: tensor_cross is severed-autograd: bilinear backward, easy fix
description:
tensor_cross at lib.rs:3354 extracts a_values + b_values, computes the cross product elementwise, and rebuilds a requires_grad=false leaf. PyTorch's torch.cross is differentiable.

Cross product is bilinear:
   c = a × b   where c_0 = a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1, c_1 = a_2 b_0 - a_0 b_2, c_2 = a_0 b_1 - a_1 b_0

Under chain rule with upstream grad_c:
   grad_a = b × grad_c
   grad_b = grad_c × a

Equivalent (and easier to implement) componentwise:
   grad_a_i = sum_j (∂c_j/∂a_i) * grad_c_j
The Jacobian is 3×3 and antisymmetric in a swap of (a, b).

Fix: wrap in tensor_apply_function with the bilinear backward. Inputs are [3]-vectors so cost is constant per call. Save a and b for backward.

Surfaced during /reality-check pass scanning for the values-then-non-grad-leaf pattern after closing tw0y.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_cross in tensor_apply_function with the bilinear backward grad_a = b × grad_c, grad_b = grad_c × a. Both inputs are saved for backward (each is a 3-vector). Added cross_propagates_gradient_through_a_and_b regression test (a = e_x, b = e_y, c = a × b = e_z; sum loss → grad_a = [1, 0, -1], grad_b = [0, 1, -1], asserts to 1e-12). ft-api lib tests: 1144.

title: tensor_vander is severed-autograd: polynomial backward [child of severed-autograd cluster]
description:
tensor_vander at lib.rs:3958 builds a Vandermonde matrix where row i column j is x[i]^exp(j). The forward extracts values, computes powers in plain f64, and rebuilds a requires_grad=false leaf. PyTorch's torch.vander is differentiable.

Forward:
   output[i, j] = x[i]^exp_j
where exp_j = j if increasing else cols-1-j.

Backward:
   d output[i, j] / d input[k] = δ_ik * exp_j * x[i]^(exp_j - 1)
   grad_input[i] = sum_j grad_output[i, j] * exp_j * x[i]^(exp_j - 1)

Special case: when exp_j == 0, the contribution is 0 (the constant term has no gradient). Save x for backward; or just regenerate x.powi calls in the backward closure.

Surfaced during /reality-check pass scanning for severed-autograd patterns.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_vander in tensor_apply_function with polynomial backward: grad_input[i] = sum_j grad_output[i, j] * exp_j * input[i]^(exp_j - 1). The constant column (exp == 0) is skipped explicitly since d x^0 / dx = 0. Captured rows / cols / increasing via closure. x is saved for backward. Added vander_propagates_gradient_via_polynomial_backward regression test (x = [2, 3] with N=4 decreasing → analytical [17, 34] = 3x^2 + 2x + 1 evaluated at x=2 and x=3, asserts to 1e-12). ft-api lib tests: 1147.

title: conv2d (+conv1d/3d/grouped/dilated/transpose) double-backward ERRs — blocks gradient-penalty/WGAN-GP
description:

conv2d 2nd-derivative (create_graph / Hessian) ERRs:
  "create_graph for this custom function requires a create_graph backward
   (register via apply_function_with_create_graph)"
loss=sum(conv2d(x,w)^2), Hessian over x. torch gives a clean Hessian
(diag=[0.32,0.4,0.08,0,0.4,0.8,0.72,0.32,0.16,0.48,0.72,0.4,0.08,0.08,0.08,0.08],

`tensor_apply_function_f64_borrowed_inputs` (the fused col2im+matmul conv-backward
custom op) which has NO create_graph backward, so the 2nd backward fails. The
NON-f64 fallthrough composed path (pad+unfold+permute+reshape+matmul) IS cg-correct,
but f64+grad takes the fused op. Same systemic pattern as 1avc3 (custom ops lacking
cg backward). create_graph is a per-backward-event flag, NOT knowable at conv's
forward, so cannot conditionally route at forward.

IMPACT: real — gradient-penalty / WGAN-GP / any conv-through-double-backward training
errors. Likely affects conv1d/conv3d/grouped/dilated/conv_transpose too (all route
through the same fused custom-op grad fast paths). f32 conv grad path (de615991) is the
f32-output custom op, same gap.

(A) [proper, keeps perf] give the fused conv2d grad custom op a create_graph backward
    via tensor_apply_function_with_create_graph: the cg closure builds dinput/dweight
    from DIFFERENTIABLE tape ops (the same col2im-via-pad + matmul composition the
    composed path uses) so the 2nd derivative flows. Substantial (conv backward is
    col2im + correlation); 1avc3 recipe applied to conv. Must stay bit-exact to the
    current 1st-order grad on the non-cg path.
(B) [simple, perf regression] route the f64 conv GRAD path through the composed
    op-graph (cg-correct) instead of the fused custom op — loses the fused-conv-grad
    perf win (de615991 f32 11.8x + the f64 one). Correctness > that perf? owner call.
VERIFY: examples/conv2d_hessian_probe.rs must match torch (above). Then extend to
conv1d/3d/grouped/dilated/transpose. ft-autograd/ft-api are cc's lane (conv KERNEL is
BlackThrush-reserved, but this fix is ft-api dispatch + the cg closure, no kernel change).

title: [perf][svd] replace Gram-Schmidt basis completion with the existing blocked orgqr — LAPACK's algorithm, not a faster loop
description:
The full_matrices basis completion is still GRAM-SCHMIDT over standard basis vectors. That is
not how LAPACK or PyTorch build a full U, and FrankenTorch already owns the machinery to do it
the LAPACK way. This is the next structural lever on the vectors phase, after 264q0 (cursor) and
tfnap (skip zero columns) took the constant factors out of the wrong algorithm.

WRITTEN UNDER A BUILD FREEZE. Nothing here is compiled, gated or measured. The numbers below are
either quoted from banked rows or are asymptotic arguments, and are labelled as such.

WHAT WE DO NOW. `complete_orthonormal_basis_f64` picks a standard basis vector e_s, orthogonalizes
it against every set column of U, keeps it if the residual survives, and repeats until U is full.
264q0 added a cursor so seeds are not re-tried; tfnap skips the still-zero columns in the sweep.
Both are real (131x and at least 1.73x) and both optimize a Gram-Schmidt loop that LAPACK does
not run at all.

WHAT LAPACK/PyTorch DO. gesdd/gesvd never complete a basis by orthogonalizing seeds. The full
orthogonal factor comes from the accumulated Householder reflectors, expanded by dorgqr/dorgbr —
blocked, GEMM-bound, and with no search, no rejection and no per-column sweep.

THE LEVER, and it needs no new numerical code. U_k (m x k) is already orthonormal, so a
Householder QR of U_k yields Q = [U_k', U_perp] whose trailing m-k columns are an orthonormal
basis for the null space — exactly the completion. FrankenTorch already has:

    qr_householder_panel_blocked(r_mat, m, n, k, qcols) -> Vec<f64>
        "Reduces r_mat in place and returns Q (m x qcols) via a reverse dorgqr"
        (blocked compact-WY, GEMM trailing/Q updates)

so completion becomes: run it on a copy of U_k with `qcols = m`, and take columns k..m.

TAKE ONLY THE TRAILING COLUMNS. Q's first k columns are U_k up to per-column SIGN, and adopting
them would require propagating those signs into V to keep U S V^T intact. The trailing columns
are orthogonal to span(U_k) by construction whatever the signs, so using ONLY those and leaving
the existing U columns untouched avoids the whole issue. Do not "simplify" this by adopting all
of Q.

WHY THIS IS POLICY-LEGAL, which is the part that makes it takeable at all: the completion columns
are ARBITRARY — any orthonormal basis for the null space is a correct SVD — and eigen/SVD VECTOR
outputs are governed by the ratified reconstruction+orthogonality tolerance of 1e-9 (bead qgce4),
NOT by bit-exactness. A different completion is therefore a legal answer, not a parity break.
This is the one place in the campaign where "parity absolute" does not bind, and it is why this
lever is available where an elementwise one would not be.

EXPECTED MAGNITUDE, asymptotic and NOT measured. Gram-Schmidt completion costs O(m) sweeps of
O(m * u_cols) for the m-k missing columns; a blocked orgqr forming m columns from k reflectors is
O(m^2 k) in GEMMs. At the 256x32 headline shape tfnap's own timing has the completion still at
19.0-25.5 ms after both prior levers. An orgqr expansion at that shape is a few GEMMs on a
256x256; single-digit milliseconds is the plausible target, so the expected win is large but is a
PREDICTION and this campaign's predictions have a poor record (item 29: two of three wrong).
Measure before claiming anything.

GATE BEFORE LANDING:
  - reconstruction ||A - U S V^T|| and orthogonality ||U^T U - I|| within the ratified 1e-9, on
    the shapes 264q0 already uses, INCLUDING the rank-deficient ones where completion columns are
    interleaved among real singular vectors rather than trailing.
  - the existing bitwise tests for the cursor and zero-skip must be re-scoped, not deleted: they
    compare Gram-Schmidt against Gram-Schmidt and are meaningless once the algorithm changes.
    Keep them guarding the old path if it is retained as a fallback.
  - explicit zero-column and all-zero-U cases: if k == 0 there are no reflectors to expand and the
    completion is the whole identity basis.

MEASURE ON A PAIRED LANE, not across binaries: put the old and new completion behind a runtime
toggle and sample them adjacently with an A/A control, which is the design that certified 4/4 on
a loud host where vs-incumbent rows certified 0/4 (item 32).

COORDINATION: the SVD thread is pane 1.2's. This bead is filed as research for whoever holds it,
not claimed. The 44-62% vectors attribution it builds on is theirs (commit 8b9430bc).

title: [test][conformance] two metamorphic properties assert float-exact reorder invariance that does not hold — the suite's green was seed-dependent
description:
Two properties in ft-conformance's fuzz suite assert invariance under reordering that floating-point addition does not provide. Both surfaced on 2026-08-09 and both are PRE-EXISTING.

  fuzz_metamorphic_sum_permutation_invariant   (~lib.rs:24535)
      sum permutation invariance: 1.0322580645161192 vs 1.0322580645161405
      diff = 2.1316282072803006e-14

  fuzz_metamorphic_index_add_sum_and_identity  (~lib.rs:22375)
      sum(index_add) = -1.6847826086956488 but sum(input) + sum(src) = -1.684782608695654
      diff = 5.329070518200751e-15  against  tol = 5.237356442253462e-15

Float addition is not associative, so summing the same values in a different order legitimately gives a different result. The first property asserts permutation invariance outright; the second uses a tolerance that is simply too tight for the accumulated cancellation (it missed by ~2%).

HOW THEY APPEARED, stated precisely because the causal story matters: they were exposed by frankentorch-z11ev, which rewrote 11 generators from generate-then-filter to construct-by-length. That perturbs proptest's RNG STREAM -- different generators draw a different sequence -- so different cases get explored. Verified that neither property is touched by that diff (zero name matches). The change EXPOSED these; it did not cause them.

★ THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION, which is larger than either bug: this suite has been reporting 241/0 and that was PARTLY LUCK OF THE SEED. Two of its properties assert things that are not true and passed only because the previous draw sequence never happened to hit a counterexample. A property suite whose greenness depends on the seed is not a gate; it is a sampler that has been getting away with it. This is the same suite that, when finally run at all, turned out to be hiding two real parity bugs (frankentorch-oo3pd).

DISCOVERABILITY PROBLEM: proptest has pinned both failing seeds in crates/ft-conformance/proptest-regressions/lib.txt, which is GITIGNORED (.gitignore:62). So they now reproduce deterministically for me and may not reproduce at all for anyone else. Whoever picks this up should either un-ignore that file for this crate, or re-derive the counterexamples.

FIX SHAPE -- and it is a JUDGEMENT CALL, not mechanical. Do NOT simply widen the tolerances until green; that is how the four pre-fix properties in oo3pd survived for months. Decide per property what invariant is actually true of floating-point reduction: for sum permutation, either drop the exactness claim and assert a condition-number-scaled bound, or restrict generation to exactly-representable values where the invariance IS real. The second option is stronger: it keeps a bit-exact assertion and makes it true, rather than loosening an assertion until it stops complaining.
close_reason: Fixed in 97cf5326: both properties made TRUE and bit-exact by switching inputs to dyadic (/32.0) rather than widening tolerances. Verified 241/0 across four independent seed runs; the pinned counterexamples now pass.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED in 97cf5326, and fixed the STRONGER way: both properties are now BIT-EXACT and TRUE, rather
than tolerated.

Both were one tolerance-widening away from "green" -- sum_permutation missed by ~5%, index_add by
~2%. I did the opposite. The inputs divided by 31.0 and 23.0, neither a power of two, so values were
not exactly representable and the sums genuinely depended on addition order: the properties were
asserting something FALSE. Both now divide by 32.0, an exponent shift, so every value is an exact
multiple of 1/32 and at most 16 of them stay far inside f64's exact-integer range. Every partial sum
is exact IN ANY ORDER (index_add's other operand was already exact, multiples of 1/4), so the
invariants hold bit-for-bit and both assertions compare bits with ZERO tolerance.

That is strictly stronger than before: a one-ULP difference is now a real defect instead of
something a rounding budget absorbs. Widening the tolerances would have bought a green run and
destroyed the distinction permanently -- the same move that let four pre-fix properties survive for
months in frankentorch-oo3pd.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NO LONGER TESTED: float rounding behaviour under reordering. That was never
what these properties were for. They check STRUCTURAL identities -- sum is permutation-invariant,
index_add preserves the total -- and testing a structural claim on values where it is exactly true

title: [parity][activations] NaN GRADIENT disagrees with torch in 7 ops (relu, relu6, celu, selu, hardswish, hardsigmoid, threshold) — VERIFIED RED
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-15 by a populated probe, not by source reading. Probe: activation_gradients_at_nan_match_torch in crates/ft-api/src/lib.rs, run on rch worker vmi1293453, exit=101 (RED as intended).

SEVEN ops disagree with torch 2.12.1+cpu at x = NaN, upstream gradient 3.0:

  op            FrankenTorch    torch
  relu          NaN             3.0
  relu6         0.0             3.0
  celu          NaN             3.0
  selu          NaN             3.1521029620664414   (= 3.0 * SCALE)
  hardswish     NaN             3.0
  hardsigmoid   0.5             0.0
  threshold     0.0             3.0

CONTROLS THAT PASSED (proving the harness is not simply failing everything): elu, hardtanh, softplus, leaky_relu.

*** MY SOURCE-READ PREDICTIONS WERE WRONG TWICE. *** The original filing of this bead listed 5 ops from reading the backward closures. The probe found 7, and two of my calls were wrong in OPPOSITE directions:
  celu      — I wrote 'not observable'. True at x=0 (both branches give derivative 1.0), FALSE at NaN, where it is broken.
  threshold — I wrote 'already correct'. It is correct at the x=t boundary and WRONG at NaN.
This is the a1nz2 lesson again: read the source to form a hypothesis, run a probe to learn the answer. Do not fix from the table in a bead description — including this one.

THE UNDERLYING RULE. torch does not write these as 'pass-through if in range'. It tests the ZEROING condition, which NaN FAILS, so NaN lands on the pass-through branch:
  torch.ops.aten.threshold_backward(tensor([1.0]), tensor([nan]), 0) -> [1.0]   while (nan > 0) is False
Per-op target shape (NaN must fail the first test):
  relu         x <= 0 ? 0 : go
  relu6        (x <= 0 || x >= 6) ? 0 : go
  threshold    x <= t ? 0 : go
  hardswish    x < -3 ? 0 : (x <= 3 ? go*(2x+3)/6 : go)      <- note the ORDER; NaN must fall past both
  hardsigmoid  (x > -3 && x < 3) ? go/6 : 0                  <- NaN fails, gives 0, which is what torch wants
  celu         x < 0 ? go*exp(x/alpha) : go
  selu         x < 0 ? go*SCALE*ALPHA*exp(x) : go*SCALE
The two ops that already PASS do so by accident of exactly this ordering (elu tests x <= 0, hardtanh tests the zeroing pair), which is the confirmation that the shape is the mechanism.

SITES. Each op has TWO backward paths and both must change or double-backward diverges:
  ft-autograd/src/lib.rs ~12308 relu, ~12794 hardswish, ~12818 hardsigmoid  (first-order)
  ft-autograd/src/lib.rs ~16376 relu, ~17557 hardswish, ~17593 hardsigmoid  (create_graph)
  ft-api/src/lib.rs      ~19100 relu6, ~21690 selu, ~21738 celu, ~22974 threshold
threshold and celu are COMPOSED (tensor_gt + tensor_where / full_like+exp), so their NaN behaviour comes from the MASK, not from a scalar closure — changing them means changing which compare builds the mask, and tensor_where's NaN semantics must be checked rather than assumed.

Relu additionally has an EXPLICIT is_nan() special case returning NaN — deliberate, so check the history behind that line before flipping it.

NOT YET DONE: the fix. The probe is written and RED; it is the gate for the fix.
close_reason:
REFUTED, not fixed. Landed as 7fee785d.

The lever was 'make FrankenTorch's NaN gradients match torch'. It is ILL-POSED: torch's NaN gradient depends on the LENGTH OF THE TENSOR, so there is no single answer to match.

Measured on torch 2.12.1+cpu, NaN in slot 0, upstream 3.0:
                  n=1    n=2    n=4  |  n=8   n=16   n=64
    relu6           3      3      3  |    0      0      0
    celu            3      3      3  |  nan    nan    nan
    selu        3.152  3.152  3.152  |  nan    nan    nan
    hardswish       3      3      3  |  nan    nan    nan
    elu             3      3      3  |  nan    nan    nan
    hardtanh        3      3      3  |    0      0      0
  relu, hardsigmoid, threshold: stable across every width.

IT IS THE VECTORISED KERNEL AND THE DTYPE PROVES IT: the flip is at n=8 for f64 and n=16 for f32 — it tracks a fixed vector BYTE width, not an element count. It does not depend on WHERE the NaN sits (slots 0,3,7,8,63 of an n=64 tensor all agree). Same op, same input, two answers depending on whether that element landed in a vectorised body or a scalar tail.

Consequence: matching n=1 guarantees disagreeing at n>=8 and vice versa. Any 'NaN parity fix' would have been a coin flip dressed as a correctness fix, defensible right up until someone tested the other width. NO OP WAS CHANGED.

THREE TRAPS WORTH KEEPING (all in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md):
  1. A ONE-ELEMENT PROBE IS NOT AN ORACLE for a vectorised library. My first probe used n=1 throughout and produced a confident, wrong, seven-row table that I had already written into this bead as fact.
  2. aten.hardswish_backward called DIRECTLY returns a THIRD answer (1.0, pass-through) where the n=8 autograd path returns nan. Calling the aten op to 'check what torch really does' measures a different code path than autograd runs.
  3. My source-read predictions were wrong in BOTH directions: celu filed as 'not observable' (true at x=0, FALSE at NaN) and threshold as 'already correct' (true at x=t, FALSE at NaN). The probe found 7 ops, not the 5 I predicted.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: the RED parity probe converted into a GREEN determinism test, activation_gradients_at_nan_are_shape_independent, comparing n=1 against n=2/4/8/16/64/257 across 12 activations rather than against a hardcoded table. FrankenTorch IS shape-independent at NaN — the property the Deterministic Autograd Contract requires and the one torch lacks — and the test exists so nobody later 'fixes' these ops toward either of torch's two answers.

GATES: cargo test -p frankentorch-api --lib activation_gradients_at_nan -> 1 passed / 0 failed, REAL_EXIT=0, rch worker vmi1293453 (also 1/0 on vmi1152480 before a formatting fix). fmt clean for the changed file. No timed rows banked.

SCOPE: this refutes NaN-gradient parity ONLY. The zero-boundary work stands — rrelu was a real defect, is fixed in dcc6a1f5, and torch is self-consistent at zero across every width (full suites 2563/0 ft-api + 779/0 ft-nn on vmi1153651).

title: Make Optimizer::set_momentum return Result instead of silent no-op
description:
## Context
The stub/placeholder audit (2026-04-02) found that `Optimizer::set_momentum(&mut self, _momentum: f64)` in ft-optim/src/lib.rs:111 has an empty body `{}`. This is the ONLY empty function body in the entire codebase.

The paired `get_momentum()` default returns `None`, which is correct. But `set_momentum()` silently discards the value with no feedback — a caller setting momentum on an Adagrad optimizer (which does not support momentum) gets no error and no indication that their intent was ignored.

## Problem
Silent data loss violates the principle of least surprise. In PyTorch, calling an unsupported setter is either a no-op with a warning or raises an error depending on the optimizer. FrankenTorch should be at least as explicit.

## Plan
1. Change signature to `fn set_momentum(&mut self, _momentum: f64) -> Result<(), AutogradError>`
2. Default implementation returns `Err(optimizer_hparam_error("this optimizer does not support momentum"))`
3. SGD (and any other momentum-supporting optimizer) overrides to actually set the value and return `Ok(())`
4. Update all callers to handle the Result
5. Add a test verifying that non-momentum optimizers reject set_momentum

## Acceptance Criteria
- `set_momentum` on Adagrad/RMSprop/RAdam returns descriptive Err
- `set_momentum` on SGD succeeds
- All existing optimizer tests pass
- Zero empty function bodies remain in the codebase

## Dependencies
None — this is an independent API change within ft-optim.
close_reason: Optimizer::set_momentum now returns an explicit unsupported-feature error by default, SGD implements Result-based momentum updates, OneCycleLR handles failures visibly, and ft-optim tests plus workspace check/clippy passed via rch

title: perf(kernel): rank the ~75 dead-zero-init sites by the measured predictor, A/B only the top
description:
Items 26-28 measured the uninit first-touch lever paying 1.27-1.49x on max_pool1d and NOTHING
on avg_pool2d — same lever, same binary, same invocations. The mechanism is now named
(NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE item 28d) and this bead is to USE it rather than re-derive it per site.

THE PREDICTOR: zeroed BYTES ACTUALLY MEMSET, per unit of kernel work.

    max_pool1d   2 x 8*64*4096 f64 = 32 MB   2 comparisons per output          PAYS  1.27-1.49x
    avg_pool2d   1 x 8*64*32*32   =  4 MB   4 reads, 3 adds, 1 divide          DOES NOT

Two terms make it more than a ratio of sizes:

  - "ACTUALLY MEMSET" is load-bearing. `vec![0.0; n]` is a calloc; served by a fresh mmap the
    kernel supplies zero pages for free and the lever is worth exactly zero. Only zeroing
    served from recycled dirty arena memory is a real memset. That depends on the process's
    allocation history and is invisible to any ELF hash — it is why item 25 measured this
    same lever at nothing across two binaries and item 26 measured it at 1.36x within one.
  - The replacement is not free. `build_uninit` still allocates; it removes the write pass,
    not the allocation.

WHAT TO DO, in this order:

1. Rank the remaining ~75 `let mut out = vec![0.0...` sites in ft-kernel-cpu by output bytes
   divided by arithmetic per output element. Cheap: it is a read of each kernel, no builds.
   The attention (around lines 4194-4773) and normalization (5265-5900) families are the bulk.
2. Take only the top of that ranking — the large-output, trivial-per-element kernels. Anything
   doing transcendentals, divisions or multi-pass reductions per output is predicted NOT to pay
   and should be left alone.
3. For each candidate, A/B it with the existing machinery rather than assuming: the toggle is
   `ft_kernel_cpu::set_pool_output_zeroed` (an AtomicBool so a lane can flip arms in-process)
   and the wrappers are `build_pool_output` / `build_pool_output_pair`. Add a `_zeroed` twin
   lane, and ALWAYS run the A/A control with `FT_POOL_ZEROED_OUTPUT=1` — adding a twin lane
   moved a base lane 2x on its own once already, so the A/A is what separates a lever effect
   from an ordering effect.
4. Bank each with two runs, worst bound quoted, and expect the bound to drift DOWN as runs
   accumulate.

DO NOT sweep the 75 sites. That is the explicit anti-goal. The one lane measured before the
mechanism was understood produced a banked negative that was wrong, and the one measured after
produced a replicated negative that was right; the difference was measuring rather than
assuming. A site that does not clear the predictor should be left exactly as it is — the dead
init is real but worthless there, and churning it costs review attention and risks a coverage
mistake for nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: a ranked list of the ~75 sites with the ratio computed, the top N A/B'd with A/A
controls, and every result banked whichever way it reads. A turn that measures three sites and
finds all three worthless is a SUCCESS for this bead, not a failure.
notes:
FIRST REGISTERED PREDICTION MADE AND REFUTED. NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE item 29.

Predicted group_norm f32 would PAY (25.7 MB zeroed, a few SIMD ops per element -- the max_pool1d profile). Measured, paired, same toggle and A/A control: 1.024x [0.991,1.040] and 0.996x [0.983,1.014], both bracketing 1.0 and indistinguishable from the A/A at 0.979x [0.960,1.004]. max_pool1d read 1.368x/1.463x in the SAME invocations, so the mechanism was live. REFUTED.

prelu never got tested: it has NO dead init (par_iter().map().collect() writes each element once). The screen ranks SHAPE; the site must also have the defect, and the most favourable shape in the sweep did not.

NEAR-MISS WORTH THE BEAD'S ATTENTION: my first refutation was measured on group_norm_forward_f32_scheduled, which the lane never executes -- ft-api dispatches to _with_cpg2_stats when cpg == 2, and the lane's 64 channels over 32 groups make cpg 2. That false version was consistent, replicated, tight, had a passing A/A, and reached the same conclusion the correct measurement later reached. Converting the real path moved the estimate 0.976-0.988 -> 0.996-1.024. PROVE THE PATH EXECUTES BEFORE MEASURING IT; a dispatch on a shape parameter is where a plausible conversion lands in a dead sibling.

REVISED SCOPE for this bead: bytes-per-work is a SCREEN, not a predictor. It says where the lever COULD matter; only a paired A/B with an A/A control says whether it does. Two of three predictions so far were wrong in ways source reading could not catch. The ranking is still worth computing to choose what to A/B, but NOTHING should be converted on the strength of the ranking alone -- which is the sweep this bead exists to prevent. Remaining candidates are the attention (~30 sdpa sites) and normalization families; expect most to be worthless and bank them as such.
close_reason:
SCREEN RUN OVER THE WHOLE CRATE; the vein is exhausted and the screen's main value was telling us where NOT to touch. NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE item 30.

879 zero-init sites in ft-kernel-cpu. 79 of them ACCUMULATE into the buffer (dweight[j] += ..., p_col_sum[j] += ...), so the zeros are LOAD-BEARING and removing them is a correctness bug producing wrong gradients, not a speed-up. Spot-checked three, all genuine. The crate-wide sweep this bead was filed to prevent would have written 79 bugs into backward kernels.

Of the 170 chunked/iter_mut candidates, none sits on a live h2h lane -- they are dominated by backward kernels (batch_norm, sdpa x4, layer_norm x3, conv/depthwise/conv_transpose, rms_norm) plus transpose_batched_materialize_f32 which already uses the lever. Each would need a lane, a build, an A/B and an A/A to evaluate.

MEASURED RECORD: max_pool1d PAYS 1.27-1.49x (4 binaries); avg_pool2d NOTHING (replicated, A/A passing); group_norm f32 NOTHING (replicated, prediction refuted); prelu N/A (no dead init -- collect() writes once). One win in four, and it is the site with both the largest zeroed-bytes-per-work ratio AND a buffer pool behind it keeping memory dirty.

CLOSING rather than grinding: the remaining candidates have LOWER ratios than the two that already measured at nothing, and the host is one large build from its disk floor. The lever stays available -- build_pool_output / build_pool_output_pair / set_pool_output_zeroed extend to any kernel for free -- and the right time to reach for it is when a lane is ALREADY being measured for another reason and the site happens to have a large output with trivial per-element work. Do not re-derive the screen; its answer will not change without new measurements.

title: [parity][in-place] extend the in-place sweep to the scalar-arg and binary forms (add_, mul_, clamp_, pow_)
description:
Round 2 of frankentorch-q06x9, which pinned 16 UNARY in-place ops against their out-of-place siblings and found no drift. 16 of 222 ops are covered; the scalar-arg and binary forms are the bulk of the remainder and are the ones with an extra argument to get wrong.

SAME CERTIFICATE, no oracle: after a.foo_(k), a must hold bit-for-bit what b = x.foo(k) produced. FrankenTorch is its own reference.

WHY THE ARGUMENT MATTERS, and it is not hypothetical — q06x9 hit exactly this: tensor_hardtanh_ takes (target, min, max) while tensor_hardtanh hardcodes torch's -1/1 defaults. The two forms of the 'same' op did not have the same signature, so a naive sweep would have compared hardtanh_(t, 0, 0) against hardtanh(x) and either failed spuriously or, worse, passed while measuring different ops. Every pair in this round needs its arguments matched deliberately and the match recorded.

CANDIDATES: add_/add, sub_, mul_, div_, pow_, remainder_, fmod_, atan2_, clamp_/clamp_min_/clamp_max_, add_scalar_, mul_scalar_, leaky_relu_ (slope arg), elu_ (alpha), softshrink_/hardshrink_ (lambda), threshold_ (threshold+value).

BINARY FORMS NEED A SECOND OPERAND that also straddles boundaries — not just the target. A binary op can branch on either side (div by zero, pow with negative base and fractional exponent, atan2 quadrant selection, remainder sign), so the second operand needs its own boundary set rather than a constant.

INPUTS as in q06x9: to_bits() comparison, signed zeros, NaN, infinities, subnormals, each op's own thresholds, at 600_000 elements so the parallel paths run.

EXPECT SOME LEGITIMATE EXCLUSIONS and record them with a reason rather than asserting: an in-place op whose out-of-place sibling has a different dtype policy, or which is defined only for a narrower input domain, is not a mismatch. q06x9's hardtanh signature difference is the template for how to handle these.

A NEGATIVE RESULT IS A FINE OUTCOME and ships the gate anyway, per q06x9 / 5237b / h37tn / 1knqk.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS IT: rch refuses ft-conformance test jobs on 6/10 workers (frankentorch-1v8kz). Use -j2.
close_reason:
REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED. Landed 06e60164 (a peer committed the shared worktree and swept my fix + tests in under this bead's name; content verified present in HEAD).

THE BUG: tensor_hardshrink_ used '|x| > lambd ? x : 0', which returns 0.0 for NaN because NaN.abs() > lambd is false. tensor_hardshrink uses '(x >= -lambd && x <= lambd) ? 0 : x', where both compares are false for NaN so it falls through and KEEPS NaN. The two forms of one op disagreed at every NaN position in a 600k tensor (indices 12, 300012, 599992 — reproducible, not a fluke).

TORCH IS THE ARBITER AND AGREES WITH THE OUT-OF-PLACE FORM: F.hardshrink(tensor([nan]), 0.5) = nan, bits 0x7ff8000000000000, measured on torch 2.12.1+cpu. So out-of-place was right, in-place was wrong.

★ THE LESSON, which is sharper than the bug: tensor_hardshrink's own comment ALREADY warned about this exact difference — 'This differs from |x| > λ ? x : 0 ONLY at NaN — NaN is not inside (both compares false) so torch KEEPS NaN, verified bit-exact vs torch.nn.functional.hardshrink.' Someone identified the trap, wrote it down, avoided it in the out-of-place form — and the in-place sibling walked straight into it anyway. A COMMENT ON ONE FUNCTION DOES NOT PROTECT ITS SIBLING. Only a test that compares them does. That is the argument for this whole in-place sweep, made by the codebase itself.

FIX: the range predicate in the in-place form too. Identical for every finite input; the entire behavioural change is at NaN.

ROUND 2 ADDS 12 PAIRS: mul_scalar, pow, clamp, leaky_relu, elu, softshrink, hardshrink, threshold (scalar-arg) and add, mul, div, atan2 (binary). The binary arm uses a SECOND operand that straddles boundaries in its own right, offset from the left-hand side, so pairs like (0.0, NaN) and (inf, 0.0) are hit rather than only the diagonal (NaN, NaN).

TWO SIGNATURE TRAPS handled deliberately — the same shape q06x9 hit with hardtanh: leaky_relu_ takes an explicit slope where leaky_relu hardcodes 0.01, and elu_ takes alpha where elu hardcodes 1.0. Passing anything else compares two DIFFERENT ops and can pass while measuring nothing.

ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, named in the source rather than silently dropped: tensor_add_scalar_ exists in-place with NO out-of-place tensor_add_scalar to compare against, unlike mul_scalar which has both. Whether that missing out-of-place form is a surface gap is a separate question worth someone's attention.

GATES: cargo test -j2 -p ft-conformance --test inplace_matches_out_of_place -> 4 passed / 0 failed, REAL_EXIT=0, rch worker vmi1227854. BEFORE the fix the same command was 3 passed / 1 failed on rch worker hz2, naming hardshrink and the three indices. rustfmt clean. No timed rows banked.

COVERAGE NOW: 28 op pairs pinned (16 unary from q06x9 + 12 here) of 222 in-place ops. Remaining: the matmul family (addmm_, baddbmm_, addbmm_, addmv_, addr_) and the addc* forms, which need more care than a one-argument sweep.

title: decision: ratify tolerance-parity for GEMM/matmul value outputs (unblocks z6sjf packed-panel GEMM)
description:
RESOLVED AS MOOT 2026-06-16 (cc): re-examined the actual matmul parity tests — no
owner policy decision is needed. matmul is ALREADY held to TOLERANCE-PARITY, not
bit-exact-to-a-fixed-reference:
- prop_matmul_matches_naive_triple_loop (ft-kernel-cpu/src/lib.rs ~34078) asserts the
  kernel vs the textbook triple loop within 1e-9*(1+|acc|), NOT bit-exact.
- the *_bit_exact matmul tests (dgemm_bt_matches_materialized_transpose_bit_exact;
  functional_linear_*_matches_transpose_path_bit_exact) compare two CODE PATHS that
  both route through the gemm kernel — a consistent kernel swap keeps them mutually
  equal (a straight-k accumulation kernel gives identical results for A@B^T via the
  bt-strided read and via the materialized transpose).
- no fixed-reference bit-exact matmul golden (sha / expected-array) exists.
So the de-facto matmul policy is already tolerance 1e-9; the packed-panel GEMM
(z6sjf) does NOT need a parity-policy ratification. Closing this escalation. The real
z6sjf challenge is ENGINEERING (a safe-Rust microkernel competitive with
matrixmultiply's AVX2 per-core throughput), not policy.
close_reason: done

title: [perf] avg_pool2d op work ~4-6x slower than PyTorch (PT arm swings run-to-run — quote same-run pairings only)
description:
Second-largest confirmed vs-PyTorch gap as of 2026-08-06, found by the op-work sweep in
artifacts/perf/frankentorch-kgs4-lane-sweep/. This lane had never been compared against a live PyTorch
arm, which is why it was absent from the re-baselined loss list.

MEASURED (crates/ft-api/examples/gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs, live PT arm in the same invocation):
  executing_elf_sha256=d09360645b37cc3ba81571ff5382cd3389d4209f20c0f8f102e7aaeac56dce2c
  allocator=mimalloc (--features fair-alloc)
  avg_pool2d [8,64,64,64] kernel (2,2) stride (2,2) f64
  FT 7.864 ms vs PT 1.833 ms = 4.29x SLOWER
  A/A null gate PASS ci95=[0.717,1.131]; gradient sum matches PyTorch to 1e-6 relative.

OP WORK ONLY — forward+backward with the leaf built OUTSIDE the timed region on BOTH sides, so this is
the part a kernel lever can actually move. Not comparable to the gauntlet's whole-step ratio.

NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH avg_pool1d, which is the informative part: frankentorch-ujw3g measured
avg_pool1d op work at ~1.18x (near parity) on [8,64,8192]. Same op family, same kernel/stride, and 2-D
is 4.29x. That asymmetry is the lead — whatever avg_pool1d does well, the 2-D path is not doing. Read
the two implementations against each other before profiling from scratch.

Prior memory-ledger note says avg/max pool are "BANDWIDTH-bound (<2x)". At 4.29x that does not fit
this shape; re-test rather than assume.

CONTRACT: live incumbent in the SAME invocation, A/A null gate, executing-ELF SHA-256, median-CI.
close_reason:
CLOSING AS NOT ACTIONABLE AS A KERNEL BEAD — the gap is real but has no kernel lever (YellowBrook/cc,
2026-08-08). Artifact: artifacts/perf/frankentorch-k1h8g/final_standing.md

CURRENT STANDING, replacing this bead's stale "4-6x" title:
  vs PyTorch (op work)     2.20x / 2.33x slower   h2h, torch 2.12.1, A/A PASS
  FT's two kernels         ~1.3 ms                pool_kernel_vs_tape_probe raw lanes
  PyTorch's WHOLE op       1.70 / 2.71 ms         same h2h runs
FrankenTorch's avg_pool2d KERNELS are already faster than PyTorch's ENTIRE op, forward and backward
included. Make both kernels infinitely fast and the lane barely moves.

THE CHAIN, in order:
  zoqws  - the contended-first-touch model for the dense gradient write REFUTED in situ; its landed
           lever was a 1.118x regression and was reverted.
  un3os  - the real kernel effect found (sparse scatter into an L3-resident buffer; serial beats 64
           threads) and shipped at 1.4-2.2x per kernel...
  8obhh  - ...then REVERTED: at the LANE it was a 1.13x LOSS (pooled n=31, CI [1.042,1.198], 31/31
           rounds, clean conv3d negative control). A buffer-size gate cannot see the tape's working set.
  o5t00  - the same gate on avg_pool's own backward measured as an active ~1.27x loss, so the lever was
           never available to this lane regardless.
  uufyp  - the session is ~55-60% one stage, tensor_backward, at ~18x its own kernel (after correcting
           a 2x allocator-conditioning inflation that I had published as 34x and withdrew).
  27aci  - all five named sub-mechanisms inside that stage eliminated. The cost is DIFFUSE.

WHAT CLOSING DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It does NOT mean the lane is fast: it is 2.2-2.3x slower than
PyTorch and that stands in the ledger unchallenged. It DOES mean there is no kernel work left worth
doing here, and the remainder is engine overhead spread thin enough that no stage-granularity probe can
resolve it. Advancing it needs instruction-granularity profiling (perf/flamegraph, which nothing in
this tree does) or a decision to ledger the bound.

FOR WHOEVER PICKS THE LANE UP:
 - do NOT optimise avg_pool2d_forward_f64 or avg_pool2d_backward_f64; not the constraint, and o5t00
   already measured one gate on the backward as a loss;
 - do NOT add a sixth speculative sub-mechanism to 27aci's list; five were tested, bring a profiler;
 - the one concrete untested item is the full-size -0.0 canonicalization pass in
   accumulate_tensor_gradient_owned. It exists only so the owned path bit-matches the borrowed path, so
   removing it is a PARITY decision before a perf one, and autograd correctness outranks kernel speed;
 - the harness now carries condition_allocator() and an A/A null lane. Reuse them. They exist because
   two byte-identical lanes once read 83% apart and a later probe measured its own lane ordering as a
   6.5x effect.

Title left as written rather than edited: it records what was measured when filed, and the current
standing lives in the artifact.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TITLE CORRECTED (CyanAnchor/cc, 2026-08-06). Was '4.29x slower'; now '~4-6x, PT arm swings run-to-run'.

WHY A RANGE RATHER THAN A NEW SINGLE NUMBER. Three same-run pairings exist for this lane and they
disagree because the PyTorch arm moves, not because FrankenTorch does:
  FT 7.864 / PT 1.833 = 4.29x   (first sweep)
  FT 6.928 / PT 1.155 = 6.00x   (quiet post-fix sweep)
  FT 9.579 / PT 2.044 = 4.69x   (deliberate-load run)
FT sits in 6.9-9.6 ms; PyTorch swings 1.155-2.044 ms, a 1.77x spread that drives almost all of the
ratio movement. Replacing '4.29x' with '6.00x' would just have re-committed the same mistake at a
different point in the noise band, so the title now carries the band and the reason.

This is the tracker-title half of the standing rule now at the top of docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md: a
stale figure in a TITLE regenerates forever through  and , because those surface the
title and never the artifact banner that corrects it. Ledger corrections are necessary but not
sufficient.

The tighter, more quotable number for this lane is the KERNEL comparison, which does not depend on the
whole-op PT arm: avg_pool2d kernels measured 1.46-1.66x PyTorch's whole op across runs (raw_fwd ~0.90 ms,
raw_bwd 1.79-3.23 ms). And per frankentorch-zoqws the backward is dominated by the dense-gradient write
rather than by pooling logic, so this bead's lever probably is not in avg_pool2d at all.

comments.author: BeigeSummit
comments.text:
EVIDENCE for this bead's open question, from the REPS=16 re-bank (BeigeSummit).
Commits c839512f, e3bf75e2. Artifact + raw logs: artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/.
executing_elf_sha256=7286dcfc85bc6c77caff8b434be4429f05a4261e75fd011f1b0dc70d54fb982c.

This bead's title suspected the PT arm swings run-to-run from two runs. 36 same-ELF runs CONFIRM it,
and localise the movement to the incumbent:

CERTIFIED STANDING (18 runs, torch 2.12.1): avg_pool2d FT 8.011 ms vs PT 1.149 ms = 6.87x SLOWER
[3.09-8.07]. Ratio spread 2.61x. Gates 18/18 PASS, parity 18/18 match.

THE MOVEMENT IS NOT OURS. Our arm is the STABLEST thing in the set — FT spread 1.18x across 18 runs.
The PyTorch arm spread 2.53x on the same runs. Per-run PT (ms), run order, torch 2.12.1:
  1.381 1.095 1.106 1.131 1.021 1.034 2.098 1.162 1.804
  1.119 1.097 2.581 1.116 1.257 1.308 1.816 2.042 1.136
That bimodality (~1.1 ms mode and ~2.0-2.6 ms mode) is the entire source of the 3.09-8.07x ratio
spread. The prior 4.29x -> 6.00x "40% regression" on this lane was a PT-arm draw, not a change in us.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: avg_pool2d is NOT quotable as a point estimate. Quote "6.87x, high
variance, PT-arm-driven [3.09-8.07]" or quote the range. Do not compare it to any ratio from a
different run.

VERSION SENSITIVITY — new, and it matters for how this bead is scoped. Same ELF against torch 2.13.0:
avg_pool2d reads 4.21x, not 6.87x, because PyTorch 2.13.0 is 1.82x SLOWER than 2.12.1 on this op here
(PT median 1.149 -> 2.089 ms) while our arm moved <3%. So this lane's headline number depends on which
torch is the incumbent. Record the torch version in provenance before quoting any target for it.
avg_pool2d and max_pool1d are the two version-SENSITIVE lanes; max_pool3d and conv3d are robust.

NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD. It asks for a perf lever on avg_pool2d; I delivered measurement, not a lever.
What this changes is the scoping: the lane is a real ~6.9x loss against the canonical oracle, but any
lever's effect must be demonstrated same-run against a PT arm that itself moves 2.5x, so an FT-side
A/B is the only defensible proof here — a vs-PT delta across runs will be dominated by the incumbent.

HARNESS CAVEATS that bound the above (both unclaimed, both need their own integrity check):
- The A/A gate is anti-conservative under contention: it is FT-vs-FT, so contention WIDENS the null CI
  and a wider CI brackets 1.0 more easily. A run reading 29.22x on a sibling lane PASSED its gate.
  Gate on CI width, not bracketing.
- The arms are NOT interleaved: the whole PT arm completes (gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs:196) before the
  first FT lane (:264). 18 reps + median is what makes this usable, not the contention preflight.

comments.author: BeigeSummit
comments.text:
SCOPING UPDATE — the banked avg_pool2d range is contention-inflated, so its floor is lower than banked.

The 18-run range [3.09-8.07x] was collected on a host shared with a live agent swarm (a neighbouring
project's oracle cycling between idle and 6900% CPU; load average moved between 6 and 69). A probe run
on the QUIETEST window of that session (load ~6, shipped ELF
934f2538e733cda6cda6493115fc13ce3bf6d0411502c4be5d7fa08e0ea81a3f, torch 2.12.1) read avg_pool2d at
2.79x — BELOW the banked range — with the other three lanes all in range.

One run is not a measurement and this does NOT refute the bank. What it establishes is direction: the
one lane that broke out did so DOWNWARD, on the quietest host of the session, exactly as a
contention-widened range predicts. So this lane's true floor is below 3.09x, and the banked 6.87x
median should be read as contention-inflated rather than as a target.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD, on top of the FT-side-A/B point already recorded: RE-MEASURE avg_pool2d on
a quiet host before scoping any lever off its numbers. This lane has THREE independent sources of
width — a bimodal PyTorch arm (2.53x spread across 18 runs), a contended host, and non-interleaved
arms (frankentorch-6atx2) — and not one of them is a property of FrankenTorch. Sizing a lever against
6.87x risks sizing it against the host.

Recorded in artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/ (README range caveat +
wnku0_version_provenance_probe.md) and promoted to the ledger's standing header.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
LEVER LANDED, MEASURED, STILL A LOSS (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: cd0eb75b.

HEADLINE, honestly: avg_pool2d FT 7.396 -> 4.938 ms = 1.50x faster; vs PyTorch 3.79x SLOWER -> 2.83x SLOWER. That closes about a third of the gap, not the gap. The lane remains a confirmed loss and the bead stays open for the rest.

MEASUREMENT met this bead's contract. Interleaved arms (frankentorch-6atx2) with the A/A width-veto gate (frankentorch-8ieqm), live PyTorch in the SAME invocation, 12 BEFORE/AFTER pairs alternating in ONE load window so both ELFs see the same machine state:
  BEFORE ELF c96e881e99e0f5b9   AFTER ELF 2af564260a7fb55d   torch 2.12.1+cpu, mimalloc
  A/A gate 12/12 PASS on both arms; gradient parity 48/48 match on both arms
  host load across pairs: min 5.60, max 14.17, median 6.61
  PT arm median 1.954 -> 1.746 ms, i.e. the incumbent moved 1.12x between arms — which is exactly the run-to-run swing this bead's title warns about, and why the FT-vs-FT speedup (1.50x) is the quotable number and the vs-PT ratios are quoted as a pair from the same window rather than across sessions.
  CONTROL LANES, same runs: max_pool1d 0.97x, max_pool3d 1.05x, conv3d 0.98x. Unchanged controls are what say this is the kernel and not the host.

PROFILE FIRST — and the instrument mattered. Sampling was unavailable: perf_event_paranoid=4, samply refuses without sudo, and that is a system-wide change on a host shared with other agents, so I did not make it. Callgrind ran but is the WRONG instrument for a rayon path: it serialises threads, so idle workers spinning in steal loops retire instructions and Stealer::steal came out 30.6% Ir with crossbeam_epoch::pin 27.9%. Those are artifacts of the tool, not costs, and no lever was aimed at them. Direct phase partition named the frame (new example crates/ft-api/examples/avgpool2d_profile.rs):
  raw fwd kernel   0.600 ms
  raw bwd kernel   1.436 ms
  raw fwd+bwd      2.854 ms  (43% of session)
  session          6.562 ms
    fwd call       1.147 ms  (17%)
    sum            0.118 ms  ( 2%)
    backward       3.170 ms  (48%)  <-- dominant
    grad fetch     1.599 ms  (24%)

THE LEVER. avg_pool2d_backward_2x2s2_f64 allocated vec![0.0f64; numel] = 16 MiB and scattered into it with +=. But 2x2 windows at stride 2 with no padding TILE the input: every element belongs to exactly one window, so the scatter already writes each element exactly once and never accumulates. The zero-fill was dead work, paid SERIALLY on the calling thread (recycled allocator pages are a real memset, not lazy zero pages), which also denied the parallel scatter its page first-touch. Now built through the existing build_uninit helper so the parallel fill is the sole writer and first-toucher. No new unsafe. Internal effect: raw bwd 1.436 -> 0.274 ms (5.2x), backward phase 3.170 -> 1.272 ms, session 6.562 -> 4.616 ms.

BIT-EXACT ON PURPOSE: stores are 0.0 + g, not bare g, because the two differ at g == -0.0 (0.0 + -0.0 is +0.0; a bare store keeps -0.0), and LLVM cannot fold the add for that same reason. The pre-existing bit-exact test passes unchanged; two new tests pin the odd-extent fallback (uninit + non-tiling extents would leave garbage where +0.0 belongs) and the -0.0 case.

THE PRIOR 'BANDWIDTH-BOUND, <2x' NOTE WAS RIGHT TO BE RE-TESTED, as this bead instructed. The gap was not the pooling arithmetic at all; it was a dead 16 MiB memory pass. That is why avg_pool1d sat near parity while 2-D did not: the 1-D backward writes a much smaller buffer, so the same dead zero-fill was proportionally invisible.

WHAT REMAINS, for whoever takes the rest (2.83x):
  1. tape/apply_function overhead is now 78% of the session (3.58 of 4.62 ms) — the kernels are only 22%. The remaining lever is in ft-api/ft-autograd, not in the pooling kernels.
  2. the forward call still costs 1.49 ms against a 0.65 ms raw kernel.
  3. the same dead-zero-fill pattern likely exists in other pool backwards (max_pool2d/3d, avg_pool3d) wherever windows tile exactly — worth a grep for vec![0.0 followed by a full-coverage scatter.

SEPARATE HARNESS DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE, and it affects every lane in this harness. The 1.599 ms 'grad fetch' above is the harness's own checksum — report.gradient(x).iter().sum() over 2M f64, a serial dependent-add chain — and it sits INSIDE the FrankenTorch timed region. The PyTorch arm's timer stops BEFORE its equivalent: 'return (time.perf_counter()-s)*1e3, x.grad.sum().item()' evaluates the elapsed term first, so torch's grad sum is outside its measurement. The two arms are therefore not timing the same work, and roughly 1.6 ms of every FrankenTorch lane figure here is checksum rather than op work — which inflates every lane's ratio, this one included. Deducting it would put this lane nearer 1.9x than 2.83x, but I am NOT quoting that as the result: fixing the harness is a gate change needing its own before/after set and its own bead, so it is recorded rather than folded in.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SECOND LEVER: THE NO-GRAD PATH WAS COPYING ITS WHOLE INPUT (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: c791cf17. Bead stays open.

THE FINDING: for the same kernel and shape, the INFERENCE path was ~5x SLOWER than the TRAINING path. Measured [8,64,64,64] k(2,2) s(2,2) f64:
  no-grad forward   8.081 ms -> 1.051 ms   = 7.7x faster
  raw kernel, unchanged control, same runs   0.670 -> 0.718 ms
  session wrapper term (nograd fwd - raw fwd)  7.411 -> 0.282 ms
The control is what makes it attributable: the raw kernel is untouched by this change and did not move, while the term the change targets collapsed.

CAUSE: the no-grad fast path read its input via tensor_values, which returns an OWNED Vec — copying the full 16 MiB input before pooling it. The grad path immediately below never did, because apply_function hands its closure BORROWED slices. The "fast path" was the slow one. Now reads through values_borrowed, scoped so the borrow ends before tensor_variable needs &mut self.

HOW IT SURFACED, because the method is the transferable part: 574cu established the gradient checksum is teardown, so avgpool2d_profile now excludes it from op work and splits the remainder three ways — session wrapper, autograd graph forward side, backward side. A single undifferentiated "tape overhead" number cannot show a no-grad forward that is slower than the grad forward. The split can.

WHERE THE TIME NOW IS at that shape — op work 2.694 ms (checksum excluded):
  raw kernels                    1.046 ms  (39%)
  session wrapper                0.282 ms
  autograd graph, forward side   0.042 ms
  BACKWARD side                  1.308 ms  <- essentially the whole remaining overhead
So the next lever is the backward tape path, and it lives in ft-autograd, not ft-api. The forward side is now within 0.3 ms of the raw kernel and is not worth further attention.

NOT CLAIMED: any movement in the vs-PyTorch lane ratio. That harness runs with requires_grad and therefore takes the GRAD path, which this does not touch. This is an inference-path win measured internally FT-vs-FT and it is NOT a campaign number. The lane's standing is unchanged at 1.87x SLOWER under the symmetric timer.

NOT DONE: the f32 no-grad path in the same function has the identical shape (tensor_values_f32 also returns an owned Vec). It is UNMEASURED, so I did not change it — shipping an unmeasured edit beside a measured one is how the two get conflated in the next person's summary. Cheap follow-up for whoever wants it: the profile example takes a dtype switch in about ten lines.

PROCESS NOTE, recorded because it is exactly frankentorch-imtpq and I had just finished writing that bead's fix: my first attempt at this commit ran `git commit ... 2>&1 | tail -2` and then checked $?, which reports TAIL's status. It printed "commit: 0" while the commit had actually FAILED on a ubs timeout, and only `git log` showed the real state. Re-run unpiped with UBS_SKIP=1 (the documented workaround for the 6.7 MB lib.rs) it succeeded. The hazard survives knowing about it.

F32 NO-GRAD PATH FIXED TOO, AND THE BACKWARD REMAINDER IS SOMEONE ELSE'S BEAD (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 06edca18.

F32 FOLLOW-UP, the one c791cf17 deliberately left unfixed as unmeasured:
  no-grad f32 forward   1.336 ms -> 0.724 ms   = 1.84x faster
  session wrapper (nograd f32 - raw f32)   0.845 -> 0.174 ms  (-79%)

After both forward fixes the op-work split at [8,64,64,64] f64 is: raw kernels 1.046 ms, session wrapper 0.282, autograd graph forward 0.042, BACKWARD 1.308 — the backward is essentially the entire remaining overhead. zoqws (P1, in_progress, BeigeSummit) is exactly that lever: it measures "alloc + touch every element" at 1.269 ms of a 1.511 ms backward, 84%, and states it applies to "every op whose backward returns a dense gradient the size of its input". I am not duplicating it, and I would recommend NOT filing pooling-specific backward work here — when zoqws lands, this lane inherits the win.

SO WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS BEAD is only the vs-PyTorch standing itself: 1.87x SLOWER under the symmetric timer (574cu), down from the 4-6x this bead was filed at. comments.text:
PARTITION FIGURES CORRECTED — conclusion stands, absolute numbers were ~2x understated (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

Propagating the methodological correction recorded on frankentorch-we7ry (894d3295): min-of-N is the wrong statistic for a session-minus-kernel decomposition, because the arms differ in allocation behaviour and min systematically selects the iteration where the allocator recycled a warm block. The partition I recorded on this bead was min-based.

Re-read at MEDIAN, same harness, same shape [8,64,64,64] f64:

                      recorded (min)    median      
  raw fwd                0.647 ms       1.110 ms
  raw bwd                0.274 ms       0.354 ms
  raw fwd+bwd            1.046 ms       2.201 ms
  fwd call               1.486 ms       1.334 ms
  loss_sum               0.095 ms       0.367 ms
  backward               1.272 ms       4.208 ms
  op work (fwd+sum+bwd)  2.694 ms       5.909 ms
  overhead share            61%            63%

WHAT CHANGES: the absolute figures roughly double. 'Backward 1.308 ms of overhead' should read closer to 3.85 ms (backward 4.208 minus raw bwd 0.354).

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and this is the load-bearing part: every qualitative conclusion holds. The overhead share is 63% at median vs 61% at min. The backward side is still essentially the ENTIRE remaining overhead — the forward side now measures -0.019 ms, i.e. indistinguishable from zero after the two borrow fixes. So 'the next lever is the backward tape path, and it lives in ft-autograd not ft-api' stands, and so does 'the remainder is zoqws, do not duplicate it'.

AND IT STRENGTHENS THE zoqws LINK: part of that backward gap is precisely the allocation-pattern effect the we7ry correction identified — the backward allocates a dense 16 MiB gradient while the session holds other buffers live, so it cannot recycle. That is zoqws's cold-page first-touch wall by another route, which is further reason not to open a pooling-specific backward lever here.

Nothing landed on this bead needs reverting. The 1.50x avg_pool2d kernel win (cd0eb75b) and the two no-grad borrow wins are same-phase A/Bs with one edit as the only variable, so the statistic choice does not bias them.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
UNINIT-BUFFER SAFETY GUARDS ARE MUTATION-VERIFIED (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). No code change; verification only.

Closing a gap in my own work. The highest-stakes change I made in this bead is routing avg_pool2d_backward_2x2s2_f64 through build_uninit — an UNINITIALIZED buffer whose soundness depends entirely on two guards and the two tests that are supposed to protect them. I mutation-verified tests elsewhere this session (harness_interleave, both BatchNorm reference tests, the hook self-test) and did NOT verify these two, which are the ones where a tautological test would be worst: a silently-passing test over uninit memory is how unsoundness ships.

Verified now, by planting the failure each guard exists to prevent:

  GUARD 1 — exact tiling (`ih == 2*oh && iw == 2*ow`), which routes non-tiling
  extents to the zero-initialized path because with an uninit buffer the untouched
  last row/column would be garbage.
      planted: replaced the condition with `if true`, so odd extents take the
               uninit path
      result:  avg_pool2d_2x2s2_backward_odd_extent_leaves_exact_zero_edges FAILS
               "ih=6 iw=9: untouched last column must be +0.0, got -0.375"
      i.e. the test observes ACTUAL UNINITIALIZED MEMORY leaking into the output.
      That is exactly the unsoundness the guard prevents, and the test catches it.

  GUARD 2 — storing `0.0 + g` rather than a bare `g`, which preserves bit-exact
  agreement with the accumulate form it replaced (they differ at g == -0.0).
      planted: bare `g`
      result:  avg_pool2d_2x2s2_backward_negative_zero_upstream_stays_positive_zero
               FAILS "element 0: -0.0 upstream must accumulate to +0.0, got -0
               (bits 0x8000000000000000)"
      so the sign bit really is observable and the add really is load-bearing —
      LLVM is not folding it away, which was the assumption the comment rests on.

Both restored; `git diff --stat` is empty, so the tree is byte-identical to the committed state, and all three avg_pool2d 2x2s2 backward tests pass again.

WHY THIS MATTERED MORE THAN THE USUAL TEST HYGIENE: everything else I verified this session guards a correctness or measurement claim. These two guard MEMORY SAFETY. If either test had been tautological, the uninit optimisation would have looked tested while being unsound for non-tiling shapes — and the failure mode is garbage floats in a gradient, which is precisely the class this project says outranks kernel speed.

Nothing to fix. Reporting a verification that could have gone the other way.

comments.text:
CURRENT STANDING RE-MEASURED — the title is stale (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Measurement only; no code change.

This bead is titled "avg_pool2d op work ~4-6x slower than PyTorch". That number predates two changes that moved it — the dead 16 MiB zero-fill removed from the backward kernel (cd0eb75b) and the timed-region asymmetry fixed in frankentorch-574cu — so the title now overstates the gap by more than 2x. Re-measured on the current tree so the ledger says what is true today.

  ELF 8d331f498a69d515, torch 2.12.1+cpu, mimalloc (fair-alloc), 12 runs,
  interleaved arms, A/A width-veto gate, host load median 28.90 (BUSY).

  lane          quotable   FT med    PT med    standing
  avg_pool2d       10/12    3.483     1.729    FT 2.01x SLOWER
  max_pool1d       11/12   12.438     8.292    FT 1.50x SLOWER
  max_pool3d       11/12    3.752     0.806    FT 4.66x SLOWER
  conv3d           12/12   19.227     6.223    FT 3.09x SLOWER
  gradient parity 48/48 match.

QUOTED OVER A/A-PASS ROWS ONLY. My first pass took medians over all 12 rows per lane, which violates this harness's own printed rule ("quote a lane only if its A/A gate says PASS"). Recomputed over passing rows: avg_pool2d moved 1.96x -> 2.01x, which is small but is the difference between following the rule and not. The discarded rows are UNDECIDABLE, not slow — the A/A gate widened under load, which is exactly what frankentorch-8ieqm's width veto exists to catch, and it caught them.

THE HOST WAS BUSY, load 20.6-34.9 across the runs, roughly double the window where the 1.87x figure was taken. That is the honest reason 2.01x and 1.87x differ; it is not a regression, and I am not presenting either as more true than the other. Both are same-window, same-ELF, symmetric-timer measurements; they differ by host state, which is a property of this machine and not of the kernel.

SO: this lane sits around 1.9-2.0x SLOWER, not 4-6x. The remaining gap is still the backward tape path — raw kernels are 34% of op work at median, the backward side is essentially all of the rest — and that is frankentorch-zoqws's dense-gradient-write wall, already owned and quantified. Nothing in this bead is actionable until that lands.

NOT RENAMING THE BEAD. The title is a historical record of what was measured when it was filed, and rewriting it would erase the fact that the number moved and why. The current standing lives here instead.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE KERNELS ARE NOT THE GAP — THIS BEAD IS MIS-SCOPED AS A KERNEL PROBLEM (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-08). Artifact: artifacts/perf/frankentorch-k1h8g/kernels_are_not_the_gap.md. Follow-up: frankentorch-uufyp.

pool_kernel_vs_tape_probe at current HEAD (ELF 044e002e, post-8obhh revert), 15-rep medians, three runs, load ~10-13:
  lane        raw_fwd            raw_bwd            kernels            session              tape overhead
  max_pool3d  1.355/0.828/0.828  1.526/1.638/1.513  2.881/2.467/2.342  7.565/7.866/6.443    62% / 69% / 64%
  avg_pool2d  1.304/1.029/1.001  0.413/0.333/0.321  1.716/1.362/1.322  18.548/17.714/17.693 91% / 92% / 93%

avg_pool2d's TWO KERNELS TOGETHER ARE ~1.32 ms. The same-day h2h puts PyTorch's WHOLE avg_pool2d op at 1.701 ms (load 86) and 2.705 ms (load 8). So FT's kernels are ALREADY AT OR BELOW PyTorch's entire op, forward and backward included. Make both kernels infinitely fast and the session arm still costs ~16.4 of ~17.7 ms.

CONSEQUENCES: (a) no kernel lever can close this lane; (b) o5t00's negative result was not a near miss — the L3 scatter gate targeted a term worth ~7% of this lane; (c) it is consistent with 8obhh, where the tape's live working set is what invalidated a buffer-size cache predictor.

CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS IT, stated before anyone acts: tape_overhead here is NOT purely the autograd tape. The probe's own note says the session arm also builds the leaf and sums the returned gradient. At [8,64,64,64] f64 that is a 16 MiB leaf copy plus a 16 MiB gradient reduction plus a fresh session, per iteration — which is why this probe's session (17.7 ms) is far larger than the h2h's op-work for the same lane (3.7-6.3 ms, leaf outside the timer on both sides). THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME MEASUREMENT AND MUST NOT BE DIFFERENCED. What survives is the ratio both agree on: op-work FT ~3.7 ms against ~1.3 ms of kernels, i.e. kernels are roughly a third — matching this bead's own earlier '34% of op work' note.

SO: stop optimising avg_pool2d kernels. Split tape_overhead into session construction / leaf materialisation / tape proper / gradient reduction FIRST — filed as uufyp — because attacking 'the tape' as a unit would be the same error as attacking 'the dense write'. Also check project_gmuml_tape_retention (session tape never frees nodes) before treating a large constant per-session cost as new.

title: porting: add tensor_hypot for torch.hypot parity
description: torch.hypot(x, y) = sqrt(x² + y²), the L2 length of (x, y). Common in geometric computations and useful for distance / vector-length operations. Compose via tensor_mul + tensor_add + tensor_sqrt. Autograd-aware. Backward: ∂hypot/∂x = x / hypot, ∂hypot/∂y = y / hypot — falls out of the chain rule on the composition.
close_reason: Added tensor_hypot in ft-api. Composes through tensor_mul + tensor_add + tensor_sqrt. Autograd-aware: ∂hypot/∂x = x/hypot, ∂hypot/∂y = y/hypot via chain rule on the composition. 3 unit tests cover Pythagorean triples, analytic gradient regression on the (3,4,5) triangle, and shape-mismatch rejection. ft-api now at 1257 lib tests.

title: ft-api: index_add + index_put(accumulate=true) f16/bf16 — per-add HALF rounding kernel
description: Verified semantics (torch 2.12, 200 trials): index_add and index_put accumulate=true on half use PER-ADD half rounding — out_half = round_to_half(f32(out_half) + f32(src_half)) applied sequentially in index order, narrowing to half after EACH add. This DIFFERS from scatter_add (fp32-accumulate-then-narrow, shipped 219ba55c). So index_add CANNOT compose through the now-f16 scatter_add (that path gives fp32-acc = wrong). Needs a dedicated per-add-half kernel/path: iterate src in index order, for each maintain the running half value, upcast both to f32, add, narrow to half, store. Then relax the tensor_index_add gate (api lib.rs ~27461) + tensor_index_put accumulate=true half handling. Currently both correctly REJECT half (own gates). Golden: 1.0 + 10*f16(0.0003) -> 1.0 (per-add) NOT 1.0029 (fp32-acc). torch venv at /tmp/torchvenv for golden generation.
notes: index_add f16/bf16 DONE (dcb2b2e2, torch-exact per-add-half via apply_function, golden test across dim=0/dim=1/bf16-drift). REMAINING: index_put(accumulate=true) f16/bf16 — same per-add-half semantics (verified peradd over 200 trials), but needs replicating index_put's indexing in an apply_function forward: per-add narrow in i-ascending order over the loop 'for i in 0..n_indices { base=sum(idx[d][i]*stride[d]); for s in 0..suffix { out[base+s]=narrow(out[base+s]+val) } }' (kernel ref: index_put_tensor_contiguous_f64, ft-kernel-cpu:7391). Edge cases to golden: scalar_broadcast (values.len()==1), suffix>1, multi-index-dim, WRAPPED indices (normalize_wrapped_index_value, NOT strict), and backward (grad_input passthrough + grad_values gather with scalar-broadcast summation — see TensorNodeOp::IndexPut backward). API branch point: tensor_index_put, currently reads half vals via values_lossy_f64 then tape.index_put errors for half+accumulate. torch venv reinstall: python3 -m venv /tmp/torchvenv && /tmp/torchvenv/bin/pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu (~2min).
close_reason: COMPLETE. index_add (dcb2b2e2) + index_put(accumulate=true) (ec19ea0d) f16/bf16 both SHIPPED with torch-exact per-add-half rounding. Verified vs torch 2.12 across duplicates/suffix>1/scalar-broadcast/multi-index-dim/negative-index/drift. The whole f16/bf16 accumulation cluster (started in uv4l) is now done: scatter_add=fp32-acc, index_add+index_put-accumulate=per-add-half. ft-api 1917 + ft-autograd 436 pass.

title: ft-api missing index_select_, gather_, take_ (in-place indexing ops)
Padding modules sever autograd via tensor_values + non-grad rebuild
description:
ReflectionPad1d, ReflectionPad2d, ReplicationPad1d, ReplicationPad2d, ReplicationPad3d, CircularPad1d, CircularPad2d in ft-nn all extract tensor_values from input, manually permute/copy to a new layout, then rebuild via session.tensor_variable(values, shape, false). This silently severs autograd through every padding module — gradients can't flow back to the input. Breaks training for any model using reflection/replication/circular padding (CNNs, U-Nets, GANs, audio models).

Fix: replace each implementation with a tensor_index_select-based composition that is autograd-aware. The padding operation is mathematically just a structured gather along the spatial dimension(s); index_select handles the gather-then-scatter backward correctly. For multi-dimensional pads (2D/3D), apply index_select sequentially along each axis.

Affects:
- crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs ReflectionPad1d::forward (line 12510)
- crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs ReflectionPad2d::forward (line 12594)
- crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs ReplicationPad1d::forward (line 12704)
- crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs ReplicationPad2d::forward (line 12784)

title: [perf][no-gaps] ft-kernel-cpu: 2-D M×N tiled GEMM parallelism (cut row-split full-B re-streaming)
description: Square dgemm row-split makes every thread re-stream all of B from DRAM -> bandwidth-saturates at ~3.5x even on 16 cores. 2-D M×N tiling (p×q≈√T blocks) cuts total A+B DRAM traffic from (T+1) to (2√T) units. Bit-exact (K never split). Same-process A/B @10thr: 1.54x@512, 1.20x@1024, 1.09x@2048; scales with core count (4x traffic cut at 64 cores).
