title: [parity] tensor_pow_tensor computes exp(e·ln x) — returns NaN for EVERY negative base (torch: -8), plus ULP error on small integer powers
description:
tensor_pow_tensor (the TENSOR-exponent pow) computes x^e as exp(e·ln x). That is wrong against
torch in two distinct ways, one severe:

MEASURED END-TO-END through FrankenTorchSession vs torch 2.12.0+cpu, f64 -- not inferred from
source, because inferring behaviour from source is the error this repo's ledger opens with:

  tensor_pow_tensor diverges from torch on 5 of 8 cases:
    case 1 (2, 3):   got 7.999999999999998, torch 8
    case 2 (3, 2):   got 9.000000000000002, torch 9
    case 5 (-2, 3):  got NaN,               torch -8
    case 6 (-2, 2):  got NaN,               torch 4
    case 7 (-8, 1):  got NaN,               torch -8

SEVERE: EVERY NEGATIVE BASE RETURNS NaN. ln(x) is NaN for x<0, so (e·ln x).exp() is NaN for the
whole negative half-line regardless of exponent. torch.pow(-2, 3) = -8. This is not a rounding
question -- it is a total loss of the negative domain in a core op.

LESSER but pervasive: small integer powers are off by an ULP. 2^3 -> 7.999999999999998,
3^2 -> 9.000000000000002. Spot-checked further outside the test: 10^2 -> 100.00000000000004,
5^3 -> 124.99999999999994; 2^10 happens to land exactly (power of two). So the common case --
squaring and cubing -- is wrong in the last place essentially always.

BOTH CODE PATHS ARE AFFECTED, which is the part worth reading carefully before assuming this is a
fusion bug. crates/ft-api/src/lib.rs tensor_pow_tensor has a no-grad f64 fast path that fuses
`(e * x.ln()).exp()` in one parallel pass, and a composed fallback that does tensor_log ->
tensor_mul -> tensor_exp. The fused path's comment claims bit-exactness and IS CORRECT: it is
bit-exact TO THE COMPOSED PATH. The composed path is itself the bug. Deleting the fusion would
change nothing.

★ This is the fused==composed trap already recorded on frankentorch-lerp-fma-parity: a lock test
asserting fast-path == slow-path passes forever while both are wrong versus real torch. The comment
even says "Bit-exact:" and enumerates the correspondence -- to the wrong reference. Self-consistency
is not parity. Same family as frankentorch-dtyiz (four accumulators agreeing on a non-torch value)
and frankentorch-1jzt6.

WHY IT SURVIVED: torch.pow has at least two FrankenTorch entry points and only this one is wrong.
The ledger records powf_torch_signed_zero_f64/_f32 as the torch-correct helper (built for pqwbs,
pow(-inf, non-integer) -> NaN), which suggests the SCALAR-exponent path already uses a real powf.
The tensor-exponent path never did. That is the multi-entry-point divergence pattern this repo has
hit before (huber_loss module vs functional, one_hot tensor_ vs session.).

FIX SHAPE: route both paths through the existing torch-correct powf helper rather than exp/ln. In
the fused path this is a one-line change inside the closure and PRESERVES the parallel single pass,
so the perf rationale for the fusion survives intact -- powf is if anything cheaper than ln+mul+exp.
Keep the 0^0 -> 1 rule. Then verify the special cases the ledger already pinned (pow(-inf, finite
non-integer) -> NaN; float_power(-0.0, 0.5) -> +0 per vgj2) still hold, since those were fixed in
the powf helper and this path never had them.

★ EXPECT COLLATERAL: per the ledger's own gotcha, a real fix that changes a value WILL break tests
that asserted the OLD wrong value. Grep every pow/float_power test and run the full workspace, not
just ft-api. Do NOT relax an assertion to keep something green without deciding it against torch.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, worth recording: torch_ieee754_unary_edge_cases_subprocess_conformance had never
executed once (frankentorch-r2ayl -- its oracle payload serialized infinities to JSON null and
crashed the subprocess, while the test reported "1 passed" via the silent-skip path of
frankentorch-imtpq). Repairing the payload made it run for the first time and it found this
immediately. The test had ZERO negative-base pow cases, so I added three; two of the five
divergences are only visible because of that addition.
close_reason: Fixed in bd2696de: TensorTape::pow_tensor (powf forward, analytic backward, recursive create_graph) with both ft-api paths routed through it. ieee754 oracle test passes vs torch 2.12.0; workspace 5555/0; zero collateral.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION ANALYSIS — the fix is BIGGER than it looks, and the obvious small version is WRONG (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-08). No code change; I am not half-landing this.

WHY THE ONE-LINE FIX IS A TRAP. The bead's own 'FIX SHAPE' says route both paths through powf and calls the fused path a one-liner. The fused path IS a one-liner — swap (e * x.ln()).exp() for x.powf(e) in the closure, keeping the parallel single pass. The COMPOSED path is not: it is a TAPE GRAPH (tensor_log -> tensor_mul -> tensor_exp -> where-mask), which is where its autograd comes from for free. You cannot 'route it through powf' because there is no pow-with-TENSOR-exponent tape op. Confirmed: ft-autograd has pow(input, exponent: f64) at 2871 (scalar node) and 6738 (tensor node) — both take a SCALAR f64 exponent and both already use the torch-correct powf_torch_signed_zero_f64. No tensor-exponent sibling exists.

SO FIXING ONLY THE FAST PATH WOULD MAKE THE TWO PATHS DISAGREE ON VALUE: no-grad (-2)^3 = -8, requires_grad (-2)^3 = NaN, same op, same inputs. That is precisely the hazard frankentorch-dtyiz records — 'DO NOT remove it from one accumulator only; partial removal makes two paths disagree, which is worse than the current uniform divergence.' The same rule applies here in the same direction. Fix both or fix neither.

WHAT THE REAL FIX REQUIRES: a new tensor-exponent pow tape op — NodeOp variant, dispatch, forward via powf, backward with d/dx = e*x^(e-1) and d/de = x^e*ln(x), AND a create_graph arm. That last one is not optional: frankentorch-double-backward-custom-op-vein records that fused fast paths shipped without a create_graph backward are exactly how second-order breaks, and a new op with a hand-written backward is the same shape.

A CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE I CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: keep the graph and fix negative bases inside it via exp(e*ln|x|) with a sign correction for odd integer exponents (expressible in existing autograd-aware ops: abs/log/mul/exp/where/eq). It would recover the negative half-line without a new op, but it does NOT fix the ULP error — exp(e·ln x) is still not powf for positive x — so the fast and composed paths would STILL disagree, just more subtly. Rejected for the same reason as the partial fix.

BLAST RADIUS TO EXPECT: the ledger's gotcha applies with force here. pow is old and widely used; a value-changing fix WILL break tests asserting the current wrong outputs. Grep every pow/float_power test across the workspace, not just ft-api, and decide each against torch rather than relaxing it. Note tensor_pow (SCALAR exponent) is already torch-correct via powf, so any test that looks 'inconsistent' between the two entry points after the fix is probably the tensor-exponent one finally becoming right.

RECOMMENDATION: take this with fresh context. It is a real op build-out plus a workspace-wide value-change sweep, not an afternoon patch. I am leaving it OPEN and unassigned rather than starting it and stopping halfway in a checkout three other agents are committing into.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DE-RISKED A TRAP ON THE WAY IN (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-08). Related fix: 51f4b175 (frankentorch-ut5sy). Not progress on this bead's fix — progress on not implementing it wrongly.

While sizing this bead I found ft-autograd's cg_pow, which is exactly what an implementer reaches for here: already named pow, already took a TensorNodeId exponent, already does the correct elementwise b.powf(e). It was a trap. It recorded the node as TensorNodeOp::Pow { exponent: exp_data[0] }, collapsing the exponent tensor to its first element — so building v8f5k on top of it would have produced a correct forward with silently wrong gradients for every element but the first. No shape error, no dtype error.

It is now `cg_pow(base, exponent: f64)`, which cannot express the wrong thing.

SIZING, recorded so the next attempt does not re-derive it. A real tensor-exponent pow needs:
  1. TensorNodeOp::PowTensor { input, exponent } — both TensorNodeId
  2. a forward on TensorTape (the arithmetic is trivial: elementwise powf, as cg_pow already demonstrates)
  3. a first-order backward arm: d/dx = grad·e·x^(e-1), d/de = grad·x^e·ln(x)
  4. a create_graph arm — NOT optional. The current composed log/mul/exp path DOES support second order today, so an op without a cg arm would be a capability regression, not just a gap. cg_mul/cg_log/cg_pow/cg_accumulate all exist to build it from.
  5. op-name maps (2 sites) and the dependency-counting arms, which currently group Pow with SINGLE-input ops — PowTensor has two and must join the two-input group instead. This is the easiest site to miss.
  6. ft-api tensor_pow_tensor routed to it, both the fused no-grad path and the composed fallback, together — per this bead's existing note, fixing one alone makes no-grad and requires_grad disagree on the VALUE of (-2)^3.
Then a workspace value sweep: pow is old and widely used, and per the ledger a value-changing fix breaks tests pinning the old wrong number.

Still open, still unassigned, still wants a fresh session.

comments.text:
★ MY OWN IMPLEMENTATION ANALYSIS ON THIS BEAD OVERSTATED THE WORK. Correcting it with measurement
(YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-09). No fix landed this turn; scope re-derived.

WHAT I WROTE EARLIER: that fixing this needs a new TensorNodeOp::PowTensor variant threaded through
~6 match sites (forward, first-order backward, create_graph arm, two op-name maps, and the
dependency-counting arms that currently group Pow with SINGLE-input ops), plus an ft-api rewire and
a workspace value sweep. I called it a fresh-session job and deferred it five times on that basis.

TWO THINGS I HAD WRONG.

1. WHICH PATH IS LIVE — measured by SENTINEL, the method that finally cracked frankentorch-a1nz2
   after source-reading gave me three confident wrong answers there. I made the fused no-grad f64
   closure in tensor_pow_tensor return a poison value and ran the ieee754 oracle test:

     case 0 (0, 0):   got -4242
     case 1 (2, 3):   got -4242
     case 2 (3, 2):   got -4242
     case 3 (4, 0.5): got -4242
     case 4 (0, 1):   got -4242
     case 5 (-2, 3):  got -4242

   Every failing case goes through that ONE closure. So the no-grad half of this bug is a one-line
   change inside it: `(e * x.ln()).exp()` -> `x.powf(e)`, keeping the 0^0 -> 1 rule. Not a rewire,
   not a new op.

2. NO NEW TAPE OP IS NEEDED AT ALL. I asserted there is no pow-with-tensor-exponent tape op and
   concluded one had to be built. But ft-autograd already exposes the generic custom-function
   mechanism WITH second-order support:

     apply_function_with_create_graph                        (ft-autograd ~8801)
     apply_function_with_create_graph_borrowed_inputs        (~9098)
     apply_function_f32_output_with_create_graph_borrowed_inputs  (~9299)

   and tensor_pdist already uses that family for its fused grad path, so the pattern is established
   in this exact file. A tensor-exponent pow is: forward = elementwise powf; backward =
   d/dx = g*e*x^(e-1) and d/de = g*x^e*ln(x); create_graph closure = the same built from cg ops.
   No NodeOp variant, no match arms, no dependency-group edit — which is where I had put most of
   the risk.

WHY THE create_graph VARIANT IS MANDATORY, unchanged from before: the current composed log/mul/exp
path DOES support second order today, so a custom function without a create_graph closure would be
a capability REGRESSION, not merely a gap. That is the frankentorch-double-backward-custom-op-vein
failure mode exactly, and it is why the plain apply_function is the wrong one to reach for here.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: fix BOTH paths together. The fused no-grad path and the composed grad path
must not disagree on the value of (-2)^3 (frankentorch-dtyiz). And expect collateral: pow is old and
widely used, so a value-changing fix will break tests pinning the current wrong numbers -- grep every
pow/float_power test and decide each against torch rather than relaxing it.

REVISED SHAPE, for whoever takes it:
  1. fused closure: x.powf(e) with the 0^0 rule.       (one line)
  2. composed path -> apply_function_with_create_graph with the three closures above.
  3. verify the ledger's pinned specials still hold: pow(-inf, finite non-integer) -> NaN (pqwbs),
     float_power(-0.0, 0.5) -> +0 (vgj2).
  4. workspace value sweep.
Materially smaller than what I filed. I am not starting it at the end of a long session, but the
next agent should not inherit my inflated estimate.

comments.text:
AN OBSTACLE IN THE REVISED PLAN, and it is one I created myself (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-09).
Verified in source, no fix landed.

My re-scope above says: implement tensor-exponent pow via apply_function_with_create_graph, with
  forward      = elementwise powf
  backward     = d/dx = g*e*x^(e-1),  d/de = g*x^e*ln(x)
  create_graph = the same, built from cg_* ops
Steps 1 and 2 hold. Step 3 -- the create_graph closure -- has a snag.

THE SNAG: that closure needs x^(e-1) where e is a TENSOR. The available primitive is

    fn cg_pow(&mut self, base: TensorNodeId, exponent: f64)      (ft-autograd 18976)

which takes a SCALAR exponent. It used to take a TensorNodeId -- I changed it to f64 in 51f4b175
(frankentorch-ut5sy) because it silently collapsed a tensor exponent to element 0 and produced wrong
gradients. That change was right and I would make it again, but it means there is now NO
tensor-exponent pow primitive available to a create_graph closure. Confirmed: 26 cg_* helpers
exist, none of them a tensor-exponent pow.

TWO WAYS OUT, and the obvious one is a trap:

  (a) Compose it as cg_exp(cg_mul(e_minus_1, cg_log(x))). DO NOT. That is exp(e*ln x) again --
      the exact bug this bead exists to fix -- reintroduced in the SECOND derivative. f and f'
      would be correct for negative bases while f'' silently returned NaN. That is worse than the
      current uniform wrongness, because it is a divergence that only appears under create_graph
      and would pass every first-order test.

  (b) Have the create_graph closure call the SAME custom function recursively, so the inner
      x^(e-1) is itself a tensor-exponent pow node with its own create_graph closure. Not circular
      in practice -- each level is one more node -- but it needs a termination argument and
      careful review, and it is the part of this bead that actually deserves fresh attention.

There is a third option worth weighing: reintroduce a tensor-exponent cg pow primitive, correctly
this time (recording the exponent tensor rather than collapsing it), which is close to the tape-op
work I originally scoped and then talked myself out of. If (b) proves awkward, that is where this
lands, and my original estimate would have been closer to right than my revision.

SO THE HONEST SCOPE IS BETWEEN MY TWO ESTIMATES: much smaller than "new NodeOp across 6 match
sites", but not the one-line-plus-boilerplate my re-scope implied. First-order (forward + backward)
is genuinely small and could ship on its own IF the create_graph story is settled first -- it must
not ship without it, because the composed path supports second order TODAY and losing that is a
regression, not a gap.

Recorded so the next agent hits this before writing code rather than halfway through.

comments.text:
THE BLOCKER I RECORDED LAST TURN DISSOLVES. Measured, not read (YellowBrook/cc, 2026-08-09).
No code landed; this is the third scope revision on this bead and the first one backed by numbers.

WHAT I SAID: the create_graph closure needs x^(e-1) with a TENSOR exponent, cg_pow now takes a
scalar (my own ut5sy change), composing it from cg_exp/cg_log would reintroduce exp(e*ln x) in the
second derivative, and therefore a tape-level tensor-exponent primitive has to be built first.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: the closure does not need pow at all.

    x^(e-1) == x^e / x == y / x        where y is the OUTPUT node, which the closure already has.
    so  dy/dx = e * x^(e-1) = e * y / x
        dy/de = x^e * ln(x)  = y * ln(x)

Both are mul/div/log — all of which exist as cg_* helpers. Verified against libm on 7 cases
spanning positive, negative and fractional exponents:

    x=2  e=3    e*x^(e-1)=12.0   e*y/x=12.0
    x=3  e=2               6.0            6.0
    x=-2 e=3              12.0           12.0
    x=-2 e=2              -4.0           -4.0
    x=0.5 e=4              0.5            0.5
    x=4  e=0.5            0.25           0.25
    x=-8 e=1               1.0            1.0
    0 mismatches.

ONE EDGE CASE, named so it is not discovered the hard way: at x == 0 the y/x form is 0/0 = NaN,
while the true derivative is finite for e >= 1 (0 for e=3, 1 for e=1) and +inf for e < 1. The
closure must mask x == 0 rather than divide blindly. Note this is a SECOND-order-only concern: the
first-order backward is raw Vec<f64> and can call powf directly, where the edge is not a problem.

(not an ft-api one) using apply_function_with_create_graph, and let the create_graph closure call it
RECURSIVELY for the inner x^(e-1). The closure is handed &mut TensorTape, so a public TensorTape
method is reachable from it. I had dismissed recursion as unavailable; it is available, I was
looking at ft-api rather than the tape.

  1. fused no-grad closure: x.powf(e) keeping the 0^0 -> 1 rule.     (one line, path confirmed live

  2. composed path -> apply_function_with_create_graph, three closures:
       forward      elementwise powf
       backward     raw powf: g*e*x^(e-1), g*x^e*ln(x)

title: [perf][9pafs] Ship the caching allocator as the DEFAULT product path: safe f64 buffer-recycling pool in ft-core, wired through the backward
description:
frankentorch-9pafs proved a caching allocator is the single largest residual lever (2.86x on an avg_pool1d train step; the gauntlet scorecard puts 40-73% of residual vs-PyTorch loss on the MISSING caching allocator rather than on FT compute) and then closed on a DEMO: crates/ft-api/examples/pure_rust_caching_alloc_demo.rs sets #[global_allocator], which is a measurement binary, not the product.

This ships it as the product path without hijacking the process-global allocator (option C of 1ji9l stands: a library must never set #[global_allocator]).

LEVER: ft_core::buffer_pool, a bounded process-global free list of Vec<f64>, 100% safe Rust, no unsafe, no C. take_filled/take_zeroed are observably identical to vec![v; n]; recycle() parks a buffer instead of returning multi-MiB blocks to the system allocator (which unmaps them, so the next backward re-faults every page).

TAKE side: the backward seed buffer (ft-autograd) and the max_pool3d dense-gradient backwards (ft-kernel-cpu, the measured 7.31x lane).
RECYCLE side: Drop for TensorBackwardReport and Drop for TensorTape, with Arc::try_unwrap deciding which of the two co-owners (05upk shares leaf grads) may park.

NEGATIVE CASE the tests must fail a naive implementation on: a pool that hands a parked buffer back WITHOUT re-filling passes every length/shape check while returning the previous pass's values in the 7/8 of the gradient the scatter does not write. Covered by ft-core buffer_pool::tests::take_zeroed_scrubs_a_dirty_recycled_buffer and by ft-kernel-cpu max_pool3d_backward_bits_survive_a_dirty_pooled_buffer (a NaN-poisoned buffer is parked before the pooled call).

MEASUREMENT CONTRACT: gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h gains a max_pool3d_nopool lane that runs the identical work with the pool disabled, and the incumbent driver gains the same torch op under that second name. One binary, one invocation, one live torch arm -> the ratio-of-ratios is the lever, PT(nopool)/PT(pooled) is a free ~1.0 control, and each lane keeps its own A/A gate.
close_reason:
SHIPPED c56b338c. ft_core::buffer_pool (bounded, safe, no unsafe, no #[global_allocator]) + take side in ft-autograd's backward seed and max_pool3d's four dense-gradient backwards + recycle side at Drop for TensorBackwardReport / Drop for TensorTape.

CITED EVIDENCE, all in artifacts/perf/frankentorch-v92uh/:
- 24 of 24 independent h2h invocations put the pool ahead against a LIVE torch 2.12.1+cpu arm sampled in the same invocation. Load ~20: median 1.138x, best clean row 1.114x [1.018,1.281]. Load ~65: median 1.213x, best clean row 1.459x [1.149,1.743]. p ~ 6e-8 on the sign alone.
- The pool provably SERVED the lane rather than sitting inert: buffer_pool hits=31 misses=4 in every one of the twelve final runs, and 35 takes is exactly the 3 warmups + 16 rounds x 2 calls the wiring predicts.
- Parity: three tests, each written to fail a pool that skips the refill (a max-pool scatter writes 1 element in 8, so stale data would survive every length and shape check). ft-core take_zeroed_scrubs_a_dirty_recycled_buffer; ft-kernel-cpu max_pool3d_backward_bits_survive_a_dirty_pooled_buffer (parks a NaN buffer first); ft-autograd backward_gradients_are_bit_identical_with_and_without_the_buffer_pool (also asserts the hit count rose, so it cannot pass with the lever short-circuited).

NOT DONE, and deliberately left for a separate lever: the take side is wired only in max_pool3d. avg_pool2d, max_pool1d and conv3d already PARK buffers (the recycle side is generic) but cannot yet TAKE them. Filed as follow-up.

title: ft-api: var/std lack multi-dim reduction + internal var_dims mis-broadcasts & wrong denom clamp
description:
torch.var/std accept dim as a list. FT had only single-dim public var/std; the internal var_dims/std_dims helpers (a) subtracted a SQUEEZED mean so they mis-broadcast for any non-trailing reduced dim, and (b) clamped the divisor at max(1) instead of torch's max(0) (so correction>=N gave a finite value, not +inf).

Added tensor_var_dims/tensor_std_dims(input, dims:&[i64], correction, keepdim): keepdim mean (broadcasts), joint sum-of-squares (reduce_over_dims_joint, ~1 ULP of torch), divisor max(0, N-correction) (=> +inf when correction>=N, matching torch DOF clamp). Autograd-aware (d var/dx = 2(x-mean)/div). Rewrote internal var_dims/std_dims to delegate (fixes both latent bugs; no external callers).

Verified vs torch 2.12 harmonic [3,4,5] dims[0,2]: var c1/c0, std c1, keepdim [1,4,1], corr>=N -> inf, grad. Goldens var_std_over_multiple_dims_torch_golden + var_dims_propagates_gradient. ft-api var/std tests green (isolated).
close_reason: Shipped tensor_var_dims/tensor_std_dims (joint, keepdim-mean broadcast, max(0) denom clamp); rewrote internal var_dims/std_dims to delegate (fixes mis-broadcast + denom bug). Golden vs torch 2.12. New tests pass isolated + scoped.

title: ft-nn CELU forward severs autograd
description: Reviewer finding in crates/ft-nn/src/lib.rs. Recent commits fixed SELU, Threshold, Hardtanh, Unfold, and Fold to compose through autograd-aware primitives, but CELU::forward at lines 3673-3690 still calls session.tensor_values(input), computes outputs in plain f64, and returns session.tensor_variable(output, input_shape, false). Repro by code inspection: create a requires_grad=true input, call CELU::new(alpha).forward(...), reduce output with tensor_sum, then tensor_backward; tensor_gradient for the CELU input will be absent/zero because the output is a fresh requires_grad=false leaf. This silently breaks training through CELU and violates the deterministic autograd contract. Fix: implement CELU via differentiable primitives, e.g. x_pos = relu(input), x_scaled = input / alpha, neg_branch = alpha * (exp(x_scaled) - 1) selected where input < 0, or an equivalent tensor_where/tensor_exp composition, and add a regression test asserting CELU input gradients match the analytical derivative.
close_reason: CELU::forward now composes through tensor_where(input >= 0, input, alpha * (exp(input/alpha) - 1)) using tensor_div / tensor_mul / tensor_exp / tensor_sub primitives — all autograd-aware. Added celu_propagates_gradients regression test asserting analytical d CELU/dx (1 for x>=0, exp(x/alpha) for x<0) plus celu_rejects_zero_alpha guard.

title: Fix gaussian_nll_loss autograd via tensor primitives [child of 2med]
description:
gaussian_nll_loss at lib.rs:10398 computes:
  loss_i = 0.5 * (log(var_clamped_i) + (input_i - target_i)^2 / var_clamped_i)
plus optional 0.5 * log(2pi) constant.

Composable through tensor_clamp_min + tensor_log + tensor_sub + tensor_mul + tensor_div + scalar add for the optional constant. All three of input / target / var are differentiable in PyTorch's gaussian_nll_loss.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Composed gaussian_nll_loss through clamp_min/log/sub/mul/div/mean primitives. Added gaussian_nll_loss_propagates_gradient_through_input_and_var test (input=2, target=1, var=4 → grad_input = 0.25, grad_var = 0.09375).

title: CPU round kernels use half-away instead of PyTorch half-even

Affected file: crates/ft-kernel-cpu/src/lib.rs. Fix: use round_ties_even for scalar, f64 tensor, and f32 tensor round kernels, and add explicit tie-even tests covering negative zero.

title: ft-api tensor_nan_to_num silently severs autograd on tracked input
description: tensor_nan_to_num at crates/ft-api/src/lib.rs:13938+ extracts values via self.tensor_tape.values(input)?, replaces NaN/±inf with constants, and creates a new leaf via self.tensor_tape.leaf(values, shape, false). No requires_grad guard. If input.requires_grad == true, the user expects gradients to flow through non-NaN/inf positions (NaN/inf positions go to zero — those values were replaced by constants, so backward should be 0 there). Current behavior silently produces requires_grad=false leaf, breaking backward through any model that uses nan_to_num for masked-loss or numerical-stability purposes. Same severed-autograd pattern as the cov / corrcoef / mode / quantile family fixed under frankentorch-1tax. Fix by composing through tensor_isnan + tensor_isinf + tensor_where so gradients flow correctly to non-replaced positions.
close_reason: Fixed tensor_nan_to_num severed-autograd on F64. Replaced the values-extract-and-rebuild-leaf path with autograd-aware composition: tensor_eq (vs +inf and -inf constant tensors) + tensor_isnan + chained tensor_where calls. Order matters: replace +inf, -inf first (NaN passes through eq checks per IEEE 754), then NaN — final isnan catches it. Gradients now flow through finite, non-NaN positions and are zero at replaced positions, matching torch.nan_to_num's backward semantics. F32 path: added requires_grad guard that fails loud (tensor_where dispatches in F64 only, so the F32 autograd composition would type-mismatch). 2 new regression tests in ft-api: nan_to_num_propagates_gradient_through_finite_positions, nan_to_num_f32_with_requires_grad_fails_loud. ft-api now at 1217 lib tests.

title: ft-api: linalg_eigh full autograd backward (eigenvalues + eigenvectors)
description: eigh failed loud on requires_grad (multi-output was thought to need a tape primitive). Solved WITHOUT one: build two independent single-output apply_function nodes from the same input; the engine sums their grad_A contributions (accumulate is +=). Eigenvalue node: grad_A=V diag(grad_l) V^T. Eigenvector node: grad_A=sym(V (F . (V^T grad_V)) V^T), F_ab=1/(l_b-l_a). Both FD-verified (eigenvector loss is gauge-invariant sum_k (c^T v_k)^2). frankentorch-rl4g.

title: [measure] load-delta predicts certification: 7 runs separate cleanly at +26% vs +69%, so admissibility is checkable from the run's own record
description:
Seven invocations of the h2h harness on thinkstation1 this session, same harness (gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs), same incumbent family, 32 rounds each. Sorting them by how much the 1-minute loadavg MOVED across the run separates certified from non-certified perfectly:

  load start -> end      delta    outcome
   8.63 ->  9.25         +  7%    max_pool3d_nopool QUOTABLE            (y4nj9)
  23.05 -> 29.09         + 26%    prelu_noshortcut + group_norm QUOTABLE (vhgue)
  12.96 -> 21.97         + 69%    0 of 14 quotable
   7.10 -> 12.25         + 72%    0 of 14 quotable                       (b8mo7)
   8.10 -> 16.75         +107%    0 of 14 quotable
   8.42 -> 17.24         +105%    0 of 14 quotable
  16.70 -> 36.89         +121%    0 of 14 quotable

TWO CERTIFIED AT <=+26%. FIVE FAILED AT >=+69%. No overlap, and a wide gap between 26 and 69 with nothing in it.

WHY THIS IS MORE USEFUL THAN 'MEASURE WHEN QUIET': absolute load does NOT predict the outcome and actively misleads. The best run started at 23.05 — the HIGHEST starting load of the seven — and certified two lanes, while a run starting at 7.10, the second LOWEST, certified nothing. Anyone waiting for a quiet machine on this box is waiting for the wrong thing, and on a host with three unrelated processes pinning a core each for 15 hours, quiet never arrives.

THE MECHANISM, already established but now quantified: the harness samples both arms in a balanced square (ABBAABBA). A square cancels a STABLE offset — that is what it is for — but it cannot cancel a RAMP, because the later cells of the square are systematically slower than the earlier ones. The A/A null is precisely the instrument that detects this, which is why it is the null that fails and not the ratio.

WHAT TO DO WITH IT:
  1. PRE-FLIGHT is cheap but imperfect. Sampling /proc/loadavg before the run does not predict the next four minutes — the 1-minute average is exponentially weighted and lags, and a peer build starting at minute one still ruins the sweep. I tried this repeatedly and it failed as often as it worked.
  2. POST-HOC ADMISSIBILITY IS THE REAL WIN and it costs nothing. The run already knows its own load delta. A run whose load moved >= ~+50% can be discarded on sight, BEFORE reading its ratios, which removes the temptation to look at a tempting point estimate and then decide whether to trust it. That ordering matters: judging admissibility from a number you have already seen is not a gate.
  3. RECORD LOAD DELTA AS A PROVENANCE FIELD alongside worker, harness and ELF. It is the one field that says whether the instrument was steady while it measured.

CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the claim: seven runs, one host, one harness. The +26/+69 boundary is where the gap happens to fall in this sample, not a measured threshold — the honest reading is 'small deltas certified, large ones did not, and the crossover is somewhere in between'. It should be re-derived if the host, the round count or the lane set changes.

NOT PROPOSED: automatically discarding runs inside the harness. That is a change to MossyOtter's instrument and would need its own agreement; this bead records the empirical relationship so the decision can be made on evidence.
close_reason:
LANDED b30db5f1. An empirical, immediately usable admissibility criterion, derived from seven runs rather than proposed.

THE DATA — seven h2h invocations on thinkstation1 this session, same harness, 32 rounds each, sorted by how far the 1-minute loadavg MOVED across the run:
   8.63 ->  9.25   + 7%   max_pool3d_nopool QUOTABLE                (y4nj9)
  23.05 -> 29.09   +26%   prelu_noshortcut + group_norm QUOTABLE    (vhgue)
  12.96 -> 21.97   +69%   0 of 14
   7.10 -> 12.25   +72%   0 of 14                                   (b8mo7)
   8.10 -> 16.75  +107%   0 of 14
   8.42 -> 17.24  +105%   0 of 14
  16.70 -> 36.89  +121%   0 of 14
Two certified at <=+26%, five failed at >=+69%. No overlap, nothing in the gap.

★ ABSOLUTE LOAD DOES NOT PREDICT THE OUTCOME AND ACTIVELY MISLEADS. The best run STARTED at 23.05 — the highest starting load of the seven — and certified two lanes, while a run starting at 7.10, the second lowest, certified nothing. Every attempt I made to 'wait for a quiet moment' was optimising the wrong variable, and on this host (three unrelated processes pinning a core each for 15 hours) quiet never arrives at all.

MECHANISM, already known and now quantified: the balanced square cancels a STABLE offset — that is its purpose — but cannot cancel a RAMP, because its later cells are systematically slower than its earlier ones. The A/A null is precisely the instrument that detects that, which is why the null fails rather than the ratio simply looking wrong.

★ THE USABLE PART IS AN ORDERING CHANGE, AND IT IS FREE. Pre-flight is cheap but unreliable: the 1-minute loadavg is exponentially weighted, so it describes the minute that just passed rather than the four ahead, and a peer build starting at minute one still ruins the sweep — I tried it repeatedly this session and it failed about as often as it worked. POST-HOC admissibility is the win. The run already records its own load delta, so a run that moved >= ~+50% can be discarded BEFORE its ratios are read. That ordering is the entire point: judging admissibility from a number you have already seen is not a gate. Load delta belongs next to worker, harness and ELF as a provenance field — it is the one field that says whether the instrument held still while it was measuring.

BOUNDED, because seven runs on one host with one harness is not a law: the +26/+69 boundary is where the gap happens to fall in this sample, NOT a measured threshold. The honest reading is 'small deltas certified, large ones did not, crossover somewhere between'. Re-derive if the host, round count or lane set changes.

NOT PROPOSED: making the harness auto-discard runs. That is MossyOtter's instrument and would need its own agreement; this records the relationship so the decision can be made on evidence rather than taste.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CAMPAIGN: certification has looked like luck all session. It is not — it is a measurable property of each run, knowable from the run's own record, and cheap to apply.

title: Validate performance SLOs from spec against actual measurements
description:
COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENTORCH_V1.md §17 defines 8 performance budgets that have NEVER been measured:

| Path | Workload | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| elementwise forward | 100M elements | p95 <= 200 ms |
| backward pass | representative autograd graphs | p95 <= 1.35x forward baseline |
| matmul core | medium dense matrices | p95 <= 240 ms |
| optimizer step | 10M params Adam | p95 <= 130 ms |
| checkpoint save/load | 2 GB model state | throughput >= 350 MB/s |
| memory footprint | training step profile | peak RSS regression <= +8% |
| allocation churn | backward-heavy trace | alloc count regression <= +10% |
| tail stability | benchmark families | p99 regression <= +7% |

The spec's M4 milestone (Hardening) requires performance gates to pass. Currently we have exactly one benchmark (scalar DAC microbench, p95=4698ns) which doesn't cover any of the 8 SLOs.

Implementation plan:
1. Create a benchmark binary in ft-conformance (or a new crate) that runs each of the 8 workloads
2. For each: run 100 iterations, compute p50/p95/p99, compare against the budget
3. Emit structured JSON results to artifacts/phase2c/performance/
4. Create a gate script that reads the JSON and fails if any SLO is exceeded
5. Document whether FrankenTorch meets, exceeds, or fails each budget

Key consideration: We're CPU-only and pure Rust with no BLAS — we may not meet matmul or elementwise budgets for 100M elements. That's OK — the goal is to MEASURE and know where we stand, then document realistic budgets.

Tests:
- Benchmark binary should be runnable via: rch exec -- cargo run -p ft-conformance --bin run_perf_slos
- JSON output should be machine-readable and diffable
- Gate script should exit 0 (pass) or 1 (fail) with human-readable report

title: measure: discard the first run after idle — the harness self-loads ~20, so a quiet host FAILS the drift gate
description:
Measured instrument finding that changes how every timed run in this project should be scheduled,
and a correction to a bound I banked myself.

THE MEASUREMENT. Five back-to-back runs of one binary, nothing changed between them:

    q1     9.10 -> 27.96  (+207%)   LOAD-DRIFTED
    q2    25.19 -> 33.56   (+33%)   LOAD-DRIFTED
    q3    32.89 -> 31.69    (-4%)   PASS
    q4    32.31 -> 32.81    (+2%)   PASS
    q5    29.88 -> 60.55  (+103%)   LOAD-DRIFTED (external interference)

The two that passed are the two that STARTED at ~32, which is the level the harness itself
sustains while running. Load decays to 8-12 within minutes of the last run, so ~20-24 of that is
the sweep's own 64-thread burst.

THE RULE: fire one warm-up run, DISCARD IT UNREAD, and measure from the second onward. The drift
gate is relative (max 1.25x), so the harness's own +20 is fatal from an idle start (9 -> 28 is
+207%) and negligible from its own steady state (32 -> 32). Waiting for a quiet host makes the
gate HARDER to pass. The discard is fixed in advance and unconditional, so it is a scheduling
rule and not a filter on results.

THIS CORRECTS frankentorch-5q3io, which is mine. That bead bounded the harness's self-load at
~+0.62 absolute and used it to argue self-load was under 10% of the signal in every failing run.
It is now off by more than an order of magnitude, because the sweep has GAINED LANES since --
max_pool1d_zeroed, avg_pool2d_zeroed, group_norm_f32_zeroed, avg_pool1d, avg_pool1d_zeroed, five
of them mine. A self-load bound is a property of the harness at a point in time, not a constant,
and nothing in the row format records lane count, so it rotted silently while gates kept citing
it.

WHAT SURVIVES: the load-delta criterion itself. External load change still predicts
certification. What does NOT survive is "the harness's own contribution is negligible".

WHAT THIS EXPLAINS IN HINDSIGHT: this session's certifications came at starting loads of 20-38
(h2, h4, h6, u2, u4); the failures clustered on runs started from a quiet box. I read that at the
time as a busy host being unlucky. It was the reverse.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - the harness prints a warm-up-run marker, or the runbook states the discard-first rule, so it
    is not re-derived by the next person;
  - 5q3io's self-load bound is re-derived at the CURRENT lane count and the stale figure is
    marked, not silently replaced;
  - consider recording lane count in the row provenance, since it is the variable that
    invalidated the old bound and is invisible in every banked row.

title: tensor_block_diag is severed-autograd: linear backward [child of d180/cross/i4rd cluster]
description:
tensor_block_diag at lib.rs:3852 places each input tensor as a block on the diagonal of a larger zero-initialized matrix. PyTorch's torch.block_diag is differentiable. Forward is purely linear in each input — output[row, col] = block_k[r, c] when (row, col) is in block k's region, 0 otherwise.

Backward extracts each block from the corresponding region of grad_output:
   grad_block_k[r, c] = grad_output[row_offset_k + r, col_offset_k + c]

Wrap in tensor_apply_function with a Vec<Option<Vec<f64>>> backward that splits grad_output into per-input blocks. Shapes need to be reconstructed during backward; closure can capture (block_rows, block_cols, total_rows, total_cols) tuples.
notes: Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_block_diag in tensor_apply_function with per-block extraction backward. Pre-computed (rows, cols, row_offset, col_offset, original_shape) for each input is captured by both the forward and backward closures so the same coordinate-mapping is used in both directions. Backward returns a Vec<Option<Vec<f64>>> with one entry per input, each containing the corresponding sub-region of grad_output. Added block_diag_propagates_gradient_through_each_block regression test (two 2x2 blocks A=[[1,2],[3,4]], B=[[5,6],[7,8]] in a 4x4 output, weighted-sum loss with weights 0..15 → grad_a = [0,1,4,5], grad_b = [10,11,14,15]). ft-api lib tests: 1146.

QR VJP grad_A=(grad_Q+Q copyltu(M)) R^-T, M=R grad_R^T - grad_Q^T Q is linear in (grad_Q,grad_R), so split across two independent apply_function nodes (engine sums). Helper qr_backward_tall. Reduced QR, m>=n, full-rank R. FD-verified via linear loss <Q,Wq>+<R,Wr>; bit-exact value parity. frankentorch-rl4g.

title: [perf] ft-kernel-cpu: parallelize softmax/log_softmax dim family (left serial vs torch)
description: GAP: only f64 softmax last-dim fast path was parallel; f32 softmax fast path, BOTH log_softmax fast paths (cross-entropy/NLLLoss hot path), and ALL FOUR general strided paths ran serial — torch parallelizes softmax over any dim. title: [perf] ft-api no-grad fast paths read inputs OWNED — the inference path copies the whole buffer (44 sites, 26 fns)
close_reason: Vein harvested and measured; remainder checked and documented as negative-value. LANDED, each A/B'd against the borrow itself with a same-run raw-kernel control: batch_norm1d_sum 9.643->0.993 ms (9.7x), avg_pool2d f64 forward 8.081->1.051 (7.7x), try_fused_batch_norm 17.324->8.643 (2.0x, shared by BN 1d/2d/3d), avg_pool2d f32 1.336->0.724 (1.84x), avg_pool2d_sum 1.942->1.539 (1.26x). Two mutation-verified tests guard the semantics against independent scalar references. THE SPREAD IS THE RESULT: 1.26x-9.7x for the same defect, because the copy's price depends on kernel cost and page state (cold first-touch ~2.4 GB/s vs warm memcpy) — a single figure for 'the no-grad borrow' is noise. REMAINDER NOT WORTH REOPENING, each checked not assumed: group_norm_sum/batch_norm2d_sum own only per-channel params; layer_norm/rms_norm/group_norm's reads are the else-branch of a contiguity check and MUST NOT be changed (a strided view cannot be a flat slice); embedding's read is the index tensor and is deliberate validation; cdist/pdist are O(p*r*m) compute over O((p+r)*m) reads so the copy cannot dominate; conv3d/conv_transpose2d are ~1 MiB against millisecond kernels; linalg is noise; checkpoint/clear_autograd_graph/requires_grad_copy/bernoulli/poisson are deliberate copies. Of 44 grep hits the worthwhile ones are fixed, several must NOT be touched, the rest are unmeasurable. METHOD NOTE kept for future sweeps: the grep misled three ways — over-counted parameter reads, under-counted activation reads, and flagged mandatory copies as defects; every candidate needed a human read. Reopen if a shape is found where a demoted site dominates; I could not construct one.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FOUND BY: RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08, while finishing frankentorch-k1h8g.

DEFECT. ft-api's no-grad "fast paths" read their inputs OWNED — `let pv = self.tensor_values(x)?` returns a `Vec<f64>` (or `tensor_values_f32` a `Vec<f32>`) — so the inference path copies the whole input buffer before calling the kernel. The GRAD path of the same op typically does NOT, because apply_function hands its closures BORROWED slices. The result is that the no-grad path, which exists to be the fast one, can be slower than the training path for the same kernel.

MEASURED PRECEDENT, both on avg_pool2d [8,64,64,64] k(2,2) s(2,2), with same-run raw-kernel controls that did not move:
  f64 (c791cf17):  no-grad forward 8.081 ms -> 1.051 ms  = 7.7x   (session wrapper 7.411 -> 0.282 ms)
  f32 (06edca18):  no-grad forward 1.336 ms -> 0.724 ms  = 1.84x  (wrapper 0.845 -> 0.174 ms; the
                   wrapper had been costing MORE than the 0.491 ms kernel it wrapped)
Fix in both cases: read via `values_borrowed` / `values_f32_borrowed`, scoped so the borrow ends
before the following `&mut self` call. Taking a `to_vec()` to dodge that borrow is what created the
copy.

INVENTORY — 44 sites across 26 functions, each an owned `tensor_values*` read within 8 lines of a
`requires_grad` / `in_grad` guard (grep + nearest-enclosing-fn attribution, so treat as a candidate
list to check individually, not a verified defect list):

  functional_conv3d                 30621, 30622, 30839, 30840
  functional_conv_transpose2d       31718, 31719, 31913, 31914
  tensor_cdist                      12413, 12414, 12467, 12468, 12727, 12728
  tensor_pdist                      12930, 12965, 13108
  functional_batch_norm1d_sum       38001, 38002, 38003
  functional_batch_norm2d_sum       38313
  tensor_batch_norm2d_sum           37369
  functional_group_norm_sum         36392, 36393
  functional_avg_pool2d_sum         33238
  functional_embedding              27410
  tensor_linalg_inv                 67448, 67519
  tensor_cholesky_solve             67100, 67101
  tensor_linalg_cholesky            66616
  tensor_linalg_eigh                69175
  tensor_linalg_eigvalsh            69430
  tensor_linalg_qr                  72147
  tensor_matrix_exp                 68987
  tensor_linalg_vector_norm         71695
  tensor_fft_norm                   79940
  tensor_rfft_norm                  80146
  supcon_loss                       57748
  bernoulli                         4657
  poisson                           4700
  checkpoint                        989
  clear_autograd_graph              651
  requires_grad_copy                88049

NOT A MECHANICAL SWEEP, and please do not treat it as one:
  - The win scales with BUFFER SIZE. conv3d, conv_transpose2d, cdist, pdist, batch_norm and
    group_norm carry large activations and are where the value is. The linalg entries operate on
    matrices that are usually small, where a clone is noise — measure before touching them.
  - Some sites may NEED the owned buffer: a kernel that takes it by value, mutates in place, or a
    later `&mut self` call that cannot be scoped around. Each site needs reading, not a regex.
  - `checkpoint`, `clear_autograd_graph` and `requires_grad_copy` are almost certainly legitimate
    owned reads (they are copying deliberately). They are listed only because the grep found them;
    expect them to be rejections.
  - AGENTS.md forbids script-driven code edits here anyway, which is the right call for exactly this
    reason.

HOW TO MEASURE ONE, cheaply: crates/ft-api/examples/avgpool2d_profile.rs is the template. It times
the raw kernel, the no-grad session path, and the grad session path separately, so
`no-grad path - raw kernel` isolates the wrapper. Include the raw-kernel control in the same run —
on the f32 case above, the first measurement WITHOUT a control was equally consistent with "no clone
at all", and scaling the f64 result by dtype width predicted ~3.7 ms where the truth was 0.845 ms.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY from k1h8g: that bead is one lane's vs-PyTorch standing. This is a
cross-cutting inference-path defect affecting ops that have nothing to do with pooling, and none of
it moves any vs-PyTorch lane ratio — the H2H harnesses run with requires_grad and take the GRAD
path. These are inference wins, internal FT-vs-FT, and must not be quoted as campaign numbers.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SITE RANKING — and conv3d, the site that LOOKS best, is near the bottom (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

I claimed this to fix the highest-value site and stopped at the arithmetic, because the obvious pick was wrong. Recording the criterion so the next person does not spend a session on the wrong four lines.

THE CRITERION is not "how many sites" — it is clone_bytes relative to the kernel's own cost. The copy is pure overhead; the kernel is the work it hides behind.

  avg_pool2d f64 (already fixed, c791cf17): input 2,097,152 elems = 16 MiB, raw kernel 0.65 ms.
    The clone was ~11x the cost of the kernel it preceded. Hence 8.081 -> 1.051 ms, 7.7x.
  conv3d (4 sites, looks like the biggest target): gauntlet shape [2,32,8,16,16] is 131,072 elems
    = 1 MiB, plus a [32,32,3,3,3] weight = 216 KiB. Against a conv3d forward measured in MILLISECONDS
    per call. The clone is single-digit percent of the op. Fixing it is correct but nearly
    unmeasurable, and an unmeasurable change is one nobody can defend later.

So the ranking is by op ARITHMETIC INTENSITY, inverted:

  HIGH VALUE — cheap kernel, large buffer. The clone can exceed the whole op:
    functional_group_norm_sum      36392, 36393
    functional_batch_norm1d_sum    38001, 38002, 38003
    functional_batch_norm2d_sum    38313
    tensor_batch_norm2d_sum        37369
    functional_avg_pool2d_sum      33238
    These are the *_sum shortcuts: a reduction over a full activation. Same shape as the pooling
    case that measured 7.7x, and for the same reason.

  MEDIUM — large buffers but real compute on top:
    tensor_cdist    12413, 12414, 12467, 12468, 12727, 12728
    tensor_pdist    12930, 12965, 13108
    functional_embedding  27410

  LOW — compute-heavy relative to input; correct to fix, not worth measuring first:
    functional_conv3d             30621, 30622, 30839, 30840
    functional_conv_transpose2d   31718, 31719, 31913, 31914

  LOWEST — small matrices, O(n^3) kernels. The clone is noise at any realistic size:
    tensor_linalg_inv / cholesky / cholesky_solve / eigh / eigvalsh / qr / matrix_exp /
    vector_norm, tensor_fft_norm, tensor_rfft_norm

  EXPECT TO REJECT — these copy on purpose:
    checkpoint 989, clear_autograd_graph 651, requires_grad_copy 88049, bernoulli 4657, poisson 4700

WHY I DID NOT JUST FIX conv3d ANYWAY. It is six lines and the pattern is proven. But this session's
one durable lesson is that an unmeasured change beside a measured one gets conflated in the next
summary — and I was nearly caught by exactly that on the f32 path, where scaling the f64 result by
dtype width predicted ~3.7 ms and the truth was 0.845 ms. A conv3d fix would land with "expected
small, unmeasured" attached, which is the shape of claim this campaign keeps having to walk back.
It is worth doing in a batch with a shape where it IS measurable, not alone.

NEXT CONCRETE STEP for whoever takes this: start with functional_group_norm_sum or
functional_batch_norm2d_sum. Use crates/ft-api/examples/avgpool2d_profile.rs as the template — it
already times raw kernel / no-grad session / grad session separately, and the raw-kernel control in
the SAME run is what makes the wrapper term attributable. Do not scale one dtype's result to predict
another's.

Leaving this open and unassigned rather than sitting on it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RANKING CORRECTED BY CHECKING IT, plus one measured fix (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: see the perf commit citing this bead.

MY HIGH TIER WAS WRONG ON 2 OF 5. I ranked the *_sum shortcuts highest assuming an owned tensor_values* read inside a no-grad guard meant an ACTIVATION-sized copy. Reading them:
  functional_group_norm_sum 36392/36393 — ALREADY borrows the input for contiguous layouts, with a comment saying so; only the per-channel weight/bias remain owned. NOT a defect.
  functional_batch_norm2d_sum 38313 — owns only the per-channel bias. NOT a defect.
  functional_batch_norm1d_sum 38001 — owns the full input. REAL.
  tensor_batch_norm2d_sum 37369 — owns the full input. REAL.
  functional_avg_pool2d_sum 33238 — owns the full padded activation. REAL, fixed now.
The grep cannot distinguish activation-sized from parameter-sized reads. That is the distinction to apply to every remaining site, and it is why this was filed as a candidate list.

MEASURED FIX (33238), before/after of that single edit — no raw-kernel control needed since the edit is the only variable:
  no-grad tensor_sum(avg_pool2d(x)) [8,64,64,64] f64:  min-of-12 1.942 -> 1.539 ms (-0.40 ms, 1.26x); median 2.350 -> 2.204 ms
  control in the same runs: no-grad plain forward 1.050 -> 1.130 ms, i.e. drifted the OTHER way, which is what makes the drop attributable rather than host noise.

MODEST AND NOISY, said plainly: far smaller than the 7.7x the plain forward gave, and the medians overlap more than the minima. The cause is allocator state, not a different defect — by that phase the process has already touched buffers of this size, so the removed copy is a WARM memcpy (~16 MiB ≈ 0.4 ms) rather than the cold-page first-touch that made the forward-path clone cost 6.8 ms. SAME COPY, an order of magnitude different price depending on page state. Whoever measures the rest should expect that spread and must not treat any single number as the vein's yield — including mine.

STILL UNFIXED and now correctly ranked: functional_batch_norm1d_sum 38001 and tensor_batch_norm2d_sum 37369 are the two confirmed activation-sized reads left in the top tier. cdist/pdist/embedding next. conv3d/conv_transpose2d are LOW (1 MiB input against a millisecond kernel — correct to fix, not measurable alone). Linalg is noise. checkpoint/clear_autograd_graph/requires_grad_copy/bernoulli/poisson are deliberate copies, expect to reject.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TOP RANKED TARGET DONE (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: see the perf commit citing this bead.

try_fused_batch_norm now reads its input BORROWED instead of cloning the whole [N,C,H,W] activation. Scoped per branch so each borrow ends before the &mut self call after it.

WIDER THAN THE INVENTORY SAID: try_fused_batch_norm is the fast path SHARED by BatchNorm 1d/2d/3d, so this single edit covers three ops, not just the 2-D site listed at 37369. Worth knowing when working the rest of the list — some entries are shared helpers and pay off wider than their line number suggests.

weight/bias left owned deliberately: per-channel, a few hundred floats. Activation-sized vs parameter-sized is the whole distinction in this vein.

TEST HAS TEETH, verified not assumed: fused_batch_norm2d_no_grad_matches_an_independent_scalar_reference covers BOTH branches — training (output + momentum-updated running mean/var incl. Bessel correction) and inference — against a scalar reference written from the definition of batch norm, NOT against another FrankenTorch path (which would pass if both read the same wrong tensor). Planting a wrong slice (&x[1..]) into the statistics call makes it FAIL; restored, it passes.

PERF NOT MEASURED FOR THIS SITE and I am not predicting a number. The removed copy is the same defect measured at 7.7x (avg_pool2d plain forward, cold pages) and 1.26x (avg_pool2d sum path, warm pages) — an order-of-magnitude spread driven entirely by page state. Quoting an expected figure here is precisely the conflation this bead's earlier notes warn about. The profile harness is avg_pool2d-shaped; BatchNorm wants its own phase.

REMAINING TOP TIER: functional_batch_norm1d_sum 38001 is the last confirmed activation-sized read in the HIGH tier (check whether it too routes through a shared helper before assuming it is one site). Then cdist/pdist/embedding.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BATCHNORM BORROW MEASURED: 2.0x, and the request's stated instrument does not exist (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

WHY NOT THE INTERLEAVED LANE + A/A VETO, as asked. That measurement is not available and would have misled:
  - the interleaved harness has NO BatchNorm lane (lanes are max_pool1d, avg_pool2d, max_pool3d, conv3d);
  - it builds leaves with requires_grad=true (gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.rs:150), so every lane takes the GRAD path.
A no-grad borrow cannot move a grad-path lane. Running it yields a null that says nothing about the change, and a null reads as 'the fix did not work'. So I measured the FT-vs-FT wrapper term, which is what the change actually moves, with the raw kernel as an in-run control.

MEASURED [8,64,64,64] f64 BatchNorm2d training, no-grad, A/B of the borrow itself:
                     with clone     with borrow
  bn nograd           17.324 ms      8.643 ms     = 2.0x faster
  BN wrapper          14.942 ms      6.443 ms     = -57%
  bn raw (control)     2.382 ms      2.200 ms     flat, as it must be

THE HONEST PART: 6.443 ms of wrapper on a 2.2 ms kernel REMAINS, and it is not the input copy. Something in this path still costs ~3x the kernel. Unmeasured candidates: the output tensor_variable materialising a fresh 16 MiB node — the same cold-page first-touch wall zoqws measures on the gradient side — and the per-call running-statistic tensors. I am naming it rather than letting the 2.0x headline imply the path is now fine. It is not.

This is inference-path, internal FT-vs-FT, and moves NO vs-PyTorch lane ratio.

NEXT RANKED TARGET: functional_batch_norm1d_sum 38001 — but check first whether it routes through try_fused_batch_norm, which the 2d fix already covers. If it does, the top tier is done and the next real target is cdist/pdist (6+3 sites, large buffers).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
INVENTORY CORRECTION #2 — it UNDER-counted as well as over-counted (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

Searching specifically for activation reads (`let x = self.tensor_values(input)?`) finds four remaining sites, and THREE OF THEM WERE MISSING from the original 26-function inventory — my first grep required the owned read to sit within 8 lines of a requires_grad/in_grad guard, and these have the guard further up:

  35675  functional_layer_norm
  36098  functional_rms_norm
  36877  functional_group_norm
  38016  functional_batch_norm1d_sum

But reading them flips three of the four the OTHER way. 35675, 36098 and 36877 are each the `else` branch of a contiguity check — the if-branch already borrows via contiguous_values, and the else is the NON-CONTIGUOUS fallback. A strided view cannot be handed to a kernel as a flat slice, so those copies are REQUIRED. They are correct code, not defects, and anyone sweeping this vein by grep would "fix" them into breakage.

So the running score on this inventory: it over-counted parameter-sized reads (group_norm_sum, batch_norm2d_sum — corrected earlier), under-counted activation reads (these three), and of the newly-found ones three are legitimate. That is three separate ways a grep-built list misleads, which is why it was filed as a candidate list and why every entry needs reading.

ONLY REAL TARGET LEFT IN THE TOP TIER: functional_batch_norm1d_sum 38016, inside a genuine `if !input_grad && !w_grad && !b_grad` guard, reading the full activation. It does NOT route through try_fused_batch_norm (the helper the 2d fix covered), so it is still open. Same fix shape: values_borrowed, scoped before the &mut self call; leave the per-channel weight/bias owned.

After that the ranking stands: cdist (6 sites) / pdist (3) / embedding, then conv3d and conv_transpose2d as LOW, then linalg as noise.

A CAVEAT FOR WHOEVER TAKES 38016: the BatchNorm2d measurement above showed the borrow is worth 2.0x on that path but leaves a 6.443 ms wrapper on a 2.2 ms kernel still unexplained. Expect the same residual here. The borrow is not the last word on these paths and should not be sold as one.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
HIGH TIER COMPLETE — batch_norm1d_sum 9.7x, the vein's largest win (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

MEASURED [8,64,4096] f64, A/B of the borrow, raw kernel as in-run control:
                        with clone     with borrow
  bn1sum nograd          9.643 ms       0.993 ms    = 9.7x
  wrapper                9.388 ms       0.701 ms    = -93%
  bn1sum raw (control)   0.255 ms       0.292 ms    flat

THE RANKING GOT THIS ONE RIGHT, worth recording since it has been wrong twice. batch_norm1d_sum is a REDUCTION (0.26 ms kernel) over a 16 MiB activation — precisely the 'cheap kernel, large buffer' profile flagged HIGH. The copy cost 36x the work it preceded.

The spread across this vein is now four measured points and it is wide: 9.7x (bn1d_sum, cheap reduction, cold pages), 7.7x (avg_pool2d plain forward), 2.0x (BatchNorm2d, large residual wrapper remains), 1.26x (avg_pool2d_sum, warm pages). Anyone quoting a single figure for 'the no-grad borrow' is quoting noise — the price of the copy depends on kernel cost AND page state.

TEST: fused_batch_norm1d_sum_no_grad_matches_an_independent_scalar_reference — per-channel mean/var over N*L, normalise/scale/shift/sum, written from the definition in the test, not compared against another FT path. Uses [N,C,L] so spatial > 1 and the strided per-channel indexing is exercised rather than the degenerate spatial==1 case. Mutation-verified: planting &x[1..] makes it FAIL.

HIGH TIER STATUS after this: functional_avg_pool2d_sum done; try_fused_batch_norm done (covers BN 1d/2d/3d); functional_batch_norm1d_sum done. group_norm_sum and batch_norm2d_sum were rejected earlier as parameter-only reads. So the HIGH tier as corrected is COMPLETE.

NEXT: MEDIUM tier — tensor_cdist (6 sites), tensor_pdist (3), functional_embedding. Expect smaller multiples than 9.7x: cdist/pdist do real O(n^2) work per element read, so the copy is a smaller fraction. Below that, conv3d/conv_transpose2d (LOW, ~1 MiB against millisecond kernels) and linalg (noise). And three sites that LOOK like defects — layer_norm 35675, rms_norm 36098, group_norm 36877 — are the else-branch of a contiguity check and MUST copy a strided view; do not 'fix' them.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEDIUM TIER REASSESSED — it is weaker than I ranked it; the vein is at diminishing returns (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

Read the MEDIUM entries before working them, and two of the three do not hold up:

  functional_embedding 27410 — REJECT. The owned read is `let indices = self.tensor_values(input)?`, and for embedding `input` is the INDEX tensor, not the weight table. It is small, and it is a deliberate VALIDATION read (the surrounding comment says it mirrors the validation tensor_index_select performs internally, to keep the prior error messages). Fixing it would trade a small copy for worse errors. I had ranked it MEDIUM on the assumption it copied the embedding table; it does not.

  tensor_cdist 12413/12414 (and the other 4 sites), tensor_pdist 12930/12965/13108 — borrowable but LOW YIELD BY CONSTRUCTION. The guard already requires both inputs contiguous, so values_borrowed is valid and the fix is mechanical. But cdist is O(p*r*m) compute over O((p+r)*m) bytes read: every element read participates in many operations, so the copy is a small fraction of the op at any shape where the op is worth timing. That is the same arithmetic-intensity argument that correctly demoted conv3d — and unlike the HIGH tier, where a 0.26 ms reduction sat behind a 16 MiB copy, there is no shape here that makes the copy dominant.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THIS BEAD. The HIGH tier is done and measured: bn1d_sum 9.7x, avg_pool2d forward 7.7x, BatchNorm2d 2.0x, avg_pool2d_sum 1.26x. Everything below it is either mechanical-but-unmeasurable (cdist/pdist/conv3d/conv_transpose2d), noise (linalg on small matrices), a mandatory copy (layer_norm/rms_norm/group_norm non-contiguous fallbacks), or a deliberate one (checkpoint, clear_autograd_graph, requires_grad_copy, bernoulli, poisson, and now embedding).

MY RECOMMENDATION: do not grind the remainder site-by-site. The correct-but-unmeasurable ones are still worth landing if someone is already editing those functions — the fix is three lines and cannot regress anything the tests do not already cover — but a dedicated pass over them would produce a long diff and no defensible numbers, which is the shape of work this campaign keeps having to walk back.

WHAT WOULD BE WORTH MORE than the remainder of this vein: the 6.443 ms residual wrapper on the BatchNorm2d no-grad path, measured earlier and still unexplained. It is larger than every remaining site in this inventory combined, it sits on a 2.2 ms kernel, and the leading candidate — a fresh 16 MiB output node paying cold-page first-touch — is the same wall frankentorch-zoqws measures on the gradient side. If that is the same defect, one fix covers both, and it is worth more than the tail of this list.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN PREVIOUS COMMENT — the 6.4 ms 'residual wrapper' was largely a measurement artifact (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 894d3295.

Last comment I called that residual unexplained and recommended it as worth more than the rest of this vein combined. Chasing it refuted my hypothesis and then corrected my method.

REFUTED — the output node is not the cost. tensor_variable on a freshly built 16 MiB Vec measures 0.000 ms. It MOVES the Vec into tape storage; it does not copy it. So 'a second 16 MiB write' was simply wrong.

CORRECTED — most of the wrapper is a cold-vs-warm ALLOCATION artifact between the two phases I was differencing. The raw control dropped its 16 MiB output each iteration, so the allocator returned the same block with pages already faulted in; the session path holds input and output live at once and cannot recycle. Adding a control that keeps every output alive — the session's real allocation pattern — closes most of the gap:
    bn raw (warm, drops output)    min 1.823 ms   median 2.982 ms
    bn raw (cold, keeps outputs)   min 1.811 ms   median 8.829 ms
    bn nograd (session)            min 9.048 ms   median 10.715 ms

THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT, which matters more than the BatchNorm number: MIN-OF-N IS THE WRONG STATISTIC when the arms differ in allocation behaviour. Those two controls are indistinguishable at the MINIMUM (1.823 vs 1.811) and differ 3x at the MEDIAN, because min systematically picks the iteration where the allocator recycled. I have quoted min-of-12 throughout this bead.

WHAT STANDS: every borrow A/B here — 9.7x bn1d_sum, 7.7x avg_pool2d forward, 2.0x BatchNorm2d, 1.26x avg_pool2d_sum. Those difference one phase against ITSELF with a single edit as the only variable, so both arms share an allocation pattern and the statistic choice does not bias them.

WHAT FALLS: the wrapper DECOMPOSITIONS (session minus raw kernel) reported for BatchNorm2d and avg_pool2d are inflated by this, and my recommendation to chase the BatchNorm residual as the next lever is withdrawn. To the extent it is real it is the cold-page first-touch wall frankentorch-zoqws already owns and already quantifies at 6.3 GB/s — not a separate ft-api defect.

NET EFFECT ON THIS BEAD: nothing landed needs reverting, and the HIGH tier results are unaffected. What changes is the guidance: there is no large unexplained ft-api overhead left on these paths. After the HIGH tier the vein is done, the remainder is correct-but-unmeasurable, and the real remaining wall on no-grad paths is zoqws's, not this bead's.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
HARNESS SELF-CONTRADICTION FIXED (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08). Code: 5c8753f4.

I documented last turn that MIN is the wrong statistic for a session-minus-kernel decomposition, and put that at length in the harness's module header. The code then computed every derived term from [0] — the min. A warning in a header that the output contradicts is worse than no warning: the next person reads the number, not the prose, and the prose gives false comfort that someone thought about it.

Every SUBTRACTION now uses the median (both *_wrapper lines, op work, raw kernels, total overhead, the three 'of which' terms, grad fetch), via a small med() helper so they read as medians at the call site. Per-phase rows unchanged, still printing both statistics — only the derived differences must avoid min.

MEASURED EFFECT, and the sign is what the correction predicts (min was hiding allocation cost in the control arm, so the decomposition gets BIGGER):
    op work                 3.661 ms (medians)
    raw kernels             1.232 ms  (34%)
    session+tape overhead   2.429 ms  (66%)
      session wrapper       0.209 ms
      graph, forward side   0.064 ms
      backward side         1.966 ms

The three sub-terms now RECONCILE against the total (0.209 + 0.064 + 1.966 = 2.239 vs 2.429, remainder = loss_sum + rounding). The min-based version could not do that at all — its terms were drawn from different iterations and had no reason to sum. That reconciliation is now a standing check on the harness itself: if those stop adding up, something is wrong with the phases, not just with the numbers.

CONCLUSIONS UNAFFECTED: the backward side still dominates and is still zoqws's wall; every borrow A/B in this vein differences one phase against itself with a single edit as the only variable, so none of them ever depended on this choice. This changes what the harness REPORTS, not what it established.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSING — the vein is harvested and the remainder is documented as negative-value (RainyReef/cc, 2026-08-08).

I filed this bead and I am closing it, so the bar should be higher than usual. The case is not "I ran out of ideas"; it is that the valuable part is done and measured, and the rest has been checked and found not worth doing. Leaving it open costs every agent a re-triage that ends in the same "do not pursue" conclusion — I have personally reached it three times.

WHAT LANDED, all measured with same-run controls and A/B'd against the borrow itself:
  batch_norm1d_sum          9.643 -> 0.993 ms   9.7x   (cheap reduction, 16 MiB activation)
  avg_pool2d fwd (f64)      8.081 -> 1.051 ms   7.7x
  try_fused_batch_norm      17.324 -> 8.643 ms  2.0x   (shared by BN 1d/2d/3d — one edit, three ops)
  avg_pool2d fwd (f32)      1.336 -> 0.724 ms   1.84x
  avg_pool2d_sum            1.942 -> 1.539 ms   1.26x  (warm pages)
Two mutation-verified tests guard the semantics (batch_norm 1d and 2d, each against an independent scalar reference written from the definition, not against another FrankenTorch path).

THE SPREAD IS THE RESULT, more than any single number: 1.26x to 9.7x for the SAME defect. The price of the copy depends on the kernel's cost and on page state — cold-page first-touch runs about 2.4 GB/s here, a warm memcpy an order of magnitude faster. Anyone quoting one figure for "the no-grad borrow" is quoting noise.

WHY THE REMAINDER IS NOT WORTH OPENING AGAIN, per tier, each checked rather than assumed:
  - group_norm_sum, batch_norm2d_sum: REJECTED. They own only per-channel weight/bias, a few
    hundred floats. group_norm_sum already borrows its input, with a comment saying so.
  - layer_norm 35675, rms_norm 36098, group_norm 36877: MUST NOT BE CHANGED. They are the
    else-branch of a contiguity check; a strided view cannot be handed to a kernel as a flat
    slice, so those copies are required. A grep-driven sweep would "fix" them into breakage.
  - embedding 27410: REJECTED. The owned read is the INDEX tensor, not the weight table, and it
    is a deliberate validation read that preserves error messages.
  - cdist (6), pdist (3): borrowable, contiguity already guarded, but O(p*r*m) compute over
    O((p+r)*m) reads — the copy cannot dominate at any shape worth timing.
  - conv3d (4), conv_transpose2d (4): correct to fix, but a 1 MiB input against a
    millisecond-scale kernel means single-digit percent and an unmeasurable change.
  - all linalg entries: small matrices, O(n^3) kernels, noise.
  - checkpoint, clear_autograd_graph, requires_grad_copy, bernoulli, poisson: deliberate copies.

So of 44 grep hits, the ones worth fixing are fixed, several must NOT be touched, and the rest cannot be measured. That is a harvested vein, not an abandoned one.

WHAT THE GREP TAUGHT, and the reason the inventory is worth keeping readable after close: it misled in THREE distinct ways — it over-counted (parameter-sized reads ranked as HIGH), under-counted (three activation-sized reads absent from the original list), and flagged mandatory copies as defects. Every conversion from candidate to defect needed a human reading the site. A future sweep built the same way should expect the same three failure modes.

IF SOMEONE WANTS THE REMAINDER ANYWAY: crates/ft-api/examples/avgpool2d_profile.rs is the template, it now reports median-based decompositions (min biases session-minus-kernel terms toward warm-allocator iterations), and the raw-kernel control must be in the SAME run. Do not scale one dtype's result to predict another's — doing that predicted 3.7 ms for the f32 case where the truth was 0.845 ms.

Reopen if a shape turns up where one of the demoted sites actually dominates. I could not construct one.

title: sign returns -1.0 for -0.0, diverges from torch.sign

title: tensor_cummax / tensor_cummin sever autograd; argmax-routing backward needed
description:
tensor_cummax (lib.rs:10992) and tensor_cummin (lib.rs:11020) compute cumulative max/min along the flattened tensor and rebuild requires_grad=false leaves. PyTorch's torch.cummax / torch.cummin are differentiable.

Gradient flows back via argmax-routing: cum_max[i] takes its value from x[argmax_{j <= i} x[j]] = cum_idx[i]. So backward:
   grad_input[k] = sum over i where cum_idx[i] == k of grad_output[i]

The cum_idx tensor is already computed in the forward; saving it for backward avoids any extra work. Wrap in tensor_apply_function with this analytical backward. Surfaced during /reality-check pass.
notes:
Fixed in this commit. Wrapped tensor_cummax and tensor_cummin's values branch in tensor_apply_function with argmax-routing backward: grad_input[k] = sum over i where cum_idx[i] == k of grad_output[i]. The cum_idx is computed in the forward (using a non-grad scan) and captured by the closure so the backward uses the same routing the forward used. The indices branch remains a non-grad leaf (correct — indices are integer-valued).

Added cummax_propagates_gradient_via_argmax_routing and cummin_propagates_gradient_via_argmin_routing regression tests asserting analytical gradients on representative input ([3,1,4,1,5] and [5,3,4,1,2]). ft-api lib tests: 1161.

Fixed to route through autograd-tracked tensor_gather (gather log_p at target, negate, reshape) while keeping reduction. Forward bit-identical; gradient now = softmax-onehot. Verified analytically. frankentorch-bug.

title: [test][tooling] proptest-regressions is gitignored as 'test detritus' — 11 saved counterexamples invisible to everyone
description:
.gitignore:62 ignores proptest-regressions/ under the heading 'Ephemeral files (agent-generated, build artifacts, test detritus)'. That classification is backwards. These files are the durable record of every counterexample proptest has ever found, and the file's own auto-generated header says so:

    # It is recommended to check this file in to source control so that
    # everyone who runs the test benefits from these saved cases.

CONCRETE COST, measured today: crates/ft-conformance/proptest-regressions/lib.txt exists locally and holds ELEVEN saved seeds, accumulated since at least 2026-04-30. None of them have ever been visible to another agent or to a fresh clone. proptest re-runs saved seeds BEFORE generating novel cases, so those eleven regression cases are being replayed for exactly one person and nobody else.

This is not hypothetical. While fixing frankentorch-jabbh I watched proptest save two fresh counterexamples (sum_permutation_invariant, index_add_sum_and_identity) into that file. Had I not fixed them in the same session, they would have been unreproducible for the next agent -- who would have seen an intermittently-green suite and no way to get the failing input back. I flagged that on jabbh as a discoverability problem; this is the root cause.

It compounds the finding on jabbh that this suite's greenness was partly luck of the seed. The mechanism proptest provides for converting a lucky-seed discovery into a permanent regression case is exactly the mechanism this repo throws away.

FIX: stop ignoring proptest-regressions/ and commit the existing corpus. The saved seeds all pass today (verified: 241/0 across four runs with the file present locally, so those eleven were already being replayed), so committing it changes no result -- it only makes the results reproducible for everyone else.

WORTH CHECKING while in there: whether any other genuinely-durable artifact is misfiled under that same 'ephemeral' heading.
close_reason: Fixed in e1211205: proptest-regressions/ un-ignored and the 11-seed corpus committed. Verified all seeds pass first (fuzz 461/0, --lib 203/0). Only the misfiled entry moved; genuinely ephemeral entries left alone.

title: [harness] record the PyTorch VERSION in provenance — same ELF reads 2.43x vs torch 2.12.1 and 1.29x vs 2.13.0
description:
FOUND BY: BeigeSummit during the REPS-16 re-bank (commits c839512f, e3bf75e2, artifact artifacts/perf/frankentorch-lane-sweep-reps16/).

DEFECT. Harness provenance records host, thread count, allocator, and executing-ELF SHA-256 — but NOT the incumbent's version. The incumbent's version is part of the arm, and on this suite it is not a small part.

MEASURED, one unchanged ELF (7286dcfc85bc6c77caff8b434be4429f05a4261e75fd011f1b0dc70d54fb982c), 18 runs per oracle:
  max_pool1d: 2.43x vs torch 2.12.1  ->  1.29x vs torch 2.13.0   (PT 6.976 -> 13.502 ms)
  avg_pool2d: 6.87x vs torch 2.12.1  ->  4.21x vs torch 2.13.0   (PT 1.149 ->  2.089 ms)
  max_pool3d: 7.45x -> 7.78x  (robust, 1.04x)
  conv3d:     3.77x -> 3.89x  (robust, 1.03x)

FrankenTorch's own arm moved <3% across the two oracles on all four lanes (FT medians 17.413/17.129, 8.011/7.780, 5.309/5.145, 21.049/20.756). THE ENTIRE EFFECT IS IN THE INCUMBENT: PyTorch 2.13.0 is 1.93x and 1.82x SLOWER than 2.12.1 on max_pool1d and avg_pool2d on this host.

WHY THIS IS A REWARD-HACKING SURFACE, NOT JUST A HYGIENE GAP. Upgrading the oracle venv would have 'improved' max_pool1d from 2.43x to 1.29x and avg_pool2d from 6.87x to 4.21x with ZERO FrankenTorch change — a 1.9x free 'win' on two lanes, available to anyone who re-runs after a torch upgrade and quotes the delta. This is proof-class inflation waiting to happen, and nothing in the current provenance would catch it.

LEVER. Print the torch version (and ideally its build/ISA config) from inside the PyTorch arm, alongside executing_elf_sha256, in every h2h harness. Treat a version change like an ELF change: it invalidates cross-run comparison.

PROBE THAT MUST PASS TO CLOSE: a harness run whose output carries the torch version self-reported by the Python child in the same invocation, plus a check that quoting a ratio without it is impossible from the printed row alone (i.e. the version appears on the same provenance block a quoter would copy). Apply across the h2h example family, not just gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h.

Offered to CyanAnchor (owner of 87sz8) first and left unclaimed.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. The three live-torch provenance-emitting harnesses (gauntlet_lane_sweep_h2h, avgpool1d_h2h, groupnorm_h2h) now carry the incumbent's version, self-reported by the Python child in the same invocation, on the same provenance block a quoter copies.

NAMED PROBE PASSED, on the shipped ELF 934f2538e733cda6cda6493115fc13ce3bf6d0411502c4be5d7fa08e0ea81a3f:
  executing_elf_sha256=934f2538e733cda6cda6493115fc13ce3bf6d0411502c4be5d7fa08e0ea81a3f
  incumbent=PyTorch 2.12.1+cpu (self-reported by the arm, same invocation), threads=8
  incumbent_rule=a delta whose incumbent arm moved (version, build, or measured time) is NOT a win
Re-run against the other interpreter reports 2.13.0+cpu, so the line tracks the actual arm rather than a constant.

A harness that loses its probe cannot print ratios at all — it exits with the error naming the marker, the rule, and the fix. That is what makes the version unskippable rather than advisory.
